title: docs(process): the camcraft-mcp skill's tool signatures match the server, with a drift test
body:
**Fixes #724.** The `camcraft-mcp` skill told agents argument names the server refuses, for 8 tools. This corrects them, brings the gap list current, and adds a test so the skill can't drift from `tools/list` silently again.

**Process change:** `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 4 -> 5. A suggested #681 line for the merging session:

> **PROCESS_VERSION 5** · PR #(this) · the `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool signatures now match the server (`post` takes `output`, `add_operation` takes `source`, `set_stock` takes `box {dx, dy, dz}` / `cylinder` / `from_model`, `set_operation_area` / `set_operation_geometry` take `operation`, `set_work_offset` takes `word`, `load_machine` takes `builtin` / `path` / `clear`, `add_tool` takes `catalog`), and its gap list is current. **Fork action:** pull the process files; an agent that learned the old names should use the new ones.

### What changed

- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the tool reference:** the 8 drifted entries now use the names the server publishes. The list is in #724.
- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, "Known Remaining Gaps":**
  - Moved to "shipped": pocket recognition (#35, `detect_pockets`), in-plane part axes (#557, `set_part_axes`), and the live GUI session (#183, #567, `--mcp-port` / `mcp --connect`). Also three-point alignment (#555, `lay_part_on_points`) and the fixture locate (#561, `locate_part`), which merged while this PR was open (3961e031).
  - `MoveModel` and `RepairModel` now point to their open PRs, #719 and #721.
  - Face-to-plane alignment (#330) is noted as GUI-only.
- **`crates/app/tests/mcp_skill_signatures.rs` (new), the drift alarm:** for every `` - `name { … }` `` signature in the skill, the tool must exist, each top-level documented key must be an `inputSchema` property, and each required argument must be documented.
  - A floor on how many signatures it finds (30; the skill has 34) keeps a format change from making it pass on nothing.
  - `the_key_reader_takes_top_level_keys_only` pins the small parser itself: quoted values and nested object fields aren't arguments.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`:** 4 -> 5.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/724-mcp-skill-signatures.md`.

No product code changes.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 47a7d0e7.

- **Quick gate plan:** `mcp_skill_signatures`, 2 passed.
- **The same test on `main`'s skill** (the file put back for the run): it fails with 13 named lines across 6 tools. For example: `line 106: post has no argument "path" (it takes {"output", "post"})`, `line 93: add_operation has no argument "model"`, `line 99: set_operation_area requires "area", which the skill leaves out`. The other 2 of the 8 (`set_stock`, `add_tool`) were wrong in their prose, which the test doesn't read.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, other suites (no product code changed).

Changelog: none

Fixes #724

title: fix(app): verify's ok is false while an op's own warnings hold the post
body:
**Fixes #722.** `verify` said `"ok": true` for a program whose post was then refused by the ops' own warnings. So `camcraft-cli process <project>` (no `-o`) exited 0, "clean", for a job it couldn't post.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/script/api.rs`, `v_verify`:** behind `cam.verify`, `cam.check` and the MCP `verify` tool, and through them the CLI's exit code.
  - `ok` now also requires that no op in scope holds the post with its own cached warnings.
  - The rule is the post's own, in the new `holds_post`: a suppressed op is not in the program, and a warning counts exactly when `Warning::blocks_post()` is true. That is when `posting::stream_records` writes it as a `WARN` record, and any `WARN` record refuses the post. A Scallop or ProbeSearch note still doesn't count.
  - The report gains `held_by`: the labels of the ops in scope holding the post, empty when none.
- **`assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` and its template in `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`:** `VerifyReport` documents `ok` and the new `held_by` (the bindings drift test keeps the two equal).
- **`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`:** the `verify` tool's description says what `ok` and `held_by` mean.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/722-verify-ok-warnings.md`.

What stays the same: the program gate (`posting::verification_report`), the post's refusal text, and the findings list. Only the summary now agrees with them.

**Behaviour change, intended:** `camcraft-cli process <project>` without `-o` now exits 1 ("the job is not clean") for a job whose ops' warnings would refuse the post. Before, it exited 0.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_verify.rs`, new)

The fixture is a real collision. `EM-0400-2FL` is a Ø4 cutter with 12 mm of flute on a Ø6 shank, so contouring a 30 mm wall rubs the shank on the part below the flutes (84 `shank_hit` findings). A 10 mm wall stays inside the flutes and is clean.

- `verify_is_not_ok_while_an_ops_own_warnings_hold_the_post`: the 30 mm job has a fresh op and a passing gate, and every finding blocks the post. `ok` is `false`, `held_by` is `["C1"]` (the same answer for `verify {name: "C1"}`), and the post is still refused with "warning(s)".
- `a_contour_inside_the_flutes_still_verifies_ok_and_posts`: the 10 mm neighbour has no findings, `ok: true`, `held_by: []`, and the post writes.
- `the_cli_process_lane_exits_one_for_a_job_its_warnings_hold`: both jobs saved as projects and run through the real `camcraft-cli process`. The 30 mm job exits 1 with "not clean", the 10 mm job exits 0.

With `api.rs` put back to `main`, all three fail. The first fails at `a program the post refuses is not ok`, and the CLI test because the held job exits 0. The neighbour fails too, but only because `held_by` is a new key.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 43943371.

- **Quick gate plan** (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`), plus the other suites that read verify's `ok` (`mcp_setup`, `mcp_live`, `mcp_render`, `contour_arc_sim`, `wall_column_gouge`, `program_entry`), run by hand at `-j 4`. No failures, nothing ignored.
  - App lib: 103 passed.
  - Suites: `cli` 7, `contour_arc_sim` 1, `mcp` 13, `mcp_live` 10, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp_pockets` 3, `mcp_render` 5, `mcp_setup` 4, `mcp_verify` 3, `post_not_judged` 4, `program_entry` 9, `scripting` 18 (including the bindings drift test), `setup_mounts_post` 6, `wall_column_gouge` 3.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **The original report**, reproduced by hand on `main` f42d3788 with `camcraft-cli mcp` and `camcraft-cli process` (see #722).
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, the batch tier. The GUI is untouched: its status line reads `verification_report`, which this PR doesn't change.

Changelog: `verify` (and `camcraft-cli process` without `-o`) no longer reports a job as clean when an operation's own warnings would refuse the post; the report names those operations under `held_by` (#722)

Fixes #722

title: feat(app): an MCP repair_model tool welds and closes an imported mesh
body:
**Fixes #717.** Adds an MCP `repair_model` tool, so a headless session can close an imported mesh's open edges. Until now, only the Model page's Repair button could do that.

**Stacked on #719** (#716, `move_model`): both add to the new `crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs` and `crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`. This PR's own change is the last commit, b595b24e. Please merge #719 first; this PR will then merge `main` and show only its own diff.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs`:** the `repair_model { name, weld_tol?, max_hole_edges? }` tool.
  - It builds the GUI's own `RepairModel` and runs it through the document History: one undo step that restores the exact previous facets.
  - The defaults are the Model page's, 0.001 mm and 256 edges (`RepairUi::default`), kept as named constants.
  - The reply carries every `RepairReport` count (vertices and triangles before and after, `welded`, `dropped`, `holes_filled`, `triangles_added`) and the command's one-line `summary`.
  - The repair runs at construction, so a refused repair never reaches the history. Every refusal is the command's own text: an unknown name, setup furniture, a negative tolerance, a budget under 3 edges, a repair refusal, and "nothing to repair". The tool itself only refuses a value of the wrong JSON type, by name.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/717-mcp-repair-model.md`.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`)

- `repair_model_fills_an_open_boxs_missing_face_in_one_undo_step`: an STL box with its top face left out has 10 facets. The repair reports 1 hole filled with 2 triangles (10 to 12), the defaults 0.001 and 256, and "filled 1 hole". Undo brings back the 10 facets and redo the 12. A second repair is refused with "nothing to repair".
- `repair_model_refuses_by_name_and_a_refusal_enters_no_history`: each case is refused by name: a closed box ("nothing to repair"), an unknown name, `weld_tol: -0.1`, `max_hole_edges: 2`, `max_hole_edges: 2.5`, a string tolerance, a missing name. Nothing changes, and the next `undo` still undoes the last import.

On `main` both fail at their first `repair_model` call, because the tool doesn't exist there.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on b595b24e.

- **Quick gate plan** (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 6`): no failures, nothing ignored.
  - App lib: 103 passed.
  - App suites: `contour_arc_sim` 1, `mcp` 13, `mcp_live` 10, `mcp_model` 5, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp_pockets` 3, `mcp_render` 5, `mcp_setup` 4, `wall_column_gouge` 3.
  - UI `models`: 4 passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, the batch tier. The existing command-level suite `repair_model` isn't in the plan either, because `RepairModel` is unchanged. `camcraft-cli mcp` over stdio wasn't tried; the tests drive the same `Server::handle` in-process.

With this PR, the `camcraft-mcp` skill's gap 3 (`RepairModel`) is done too. The skill is left alone for the same reason given in #719: editing it is a process change, with a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump.

Changelog: The MCP server can repair an imported model's mesh (`repair_model`): weld, drop degenerate triangles and fill open loops, with the counts reported back (#717)

Fixes #717

title: fix(app): pocket recognition refuses an inside-out or open mesh by name
body:
## What changed

The blocker from the maintainer's review of #512 reached main when #512 merged at 7e39726.

`recognize::pockets_of` read "up" and "leans into" straight off the facet winding. So an inside-out 10 mm cube came back as `Pocket { kind: Closed, floor_z: 0, depth: 10, boundary: the part's outline }`, and `detect_pockets create` would cut the whole footprint to the base.

`pockets_of` now runs #387's body-winding verdict (`pick::winding::winding_of` / `verdict_for`) over the whole model first. Any body whose outside can't be trusted is refused by name, in recognition's own words: inside-out, open (torn), non-manifold, mixed winding, flat, or no readable facet.

`docs/decisions/718-pocket-winding.md` records the choices: why whole-model and not per-pocket, and why the refusal has its own wording instead of `refusal()`'s "before aligning to it".

## Pinned by

- `pocket_recognition::an_inside_out_mesh_is_refused_never_read_as_a_pocket`. A reversed cube and a reversed pocket block are refused with "inside-out", and the same block wound outward still reads its one pocket. **It fails without the fix:** the reversed cube reads as a 10 mm closed pocket.
- `pocket_recognition::degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly`: the torn half-pocket now expects the "open body" refusal. Before, it only checked for no panic.

## How tested

On upstream main plus this commit:
- `pocket_recognition` 11/11, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13 and `pick` 9/9 pass;
- the ui lib pocket tests pass;
- clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the app lib and `pocket_recognition`.

## Not exercised

No GUI run. Recognition has no UI entry point yet (#511).

The fork is synced at v0.16.0; the branch is cut from upstream/main.

Changelog: Pocket recognition refuses an inside-out or open mesh by name instead of reading its outline as a pocket (#718)

Fixes #718

title: feat(app): an MCP move_model tool places and turns an imported part
body:
**Fixes #716.** Adds an MCP `move_model` tool, so a headless session can place and turn an imported part. Until now, only the GUI's model move could do that.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs` (new):** the `move_model { name, position: [x, y, z], rotation?: [x, y, z, w] }` tool.
  - It builds the GUI's own `MoveModel` command and runs it through the document History, so the move is one undo step.
  - An omitted rotation keeps the part's current one, so lifting a part doesn't untwist it. A non-unit quaternion is normalized by the command, as for fixtures.
  - The reply holds the part's new placement and a `stock` list: each stock that moved with the part (stock made from it, or a one-part document's stock), with its new placement.
  - Every refusal is `MoveModel`'s own text, returned as a tool error: a fixture, a work offset, the machine table, an unknown name, a rotation that isn't a quaternion. A short or missing `position` is named too.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs`:** a new read-only accessor, `MoveModel::following_stock()`. It names the stock the move carries, so the tool can report it.
- **`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `mod.rs`:** the new module's rows are registered after the align tools.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/716-mcp-move-model.md`.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_model.rs`, new)

- `a_moved_part_carries_a_one_part_documents_stock_and_one_undo_puts_both_back`: `tools/list` shows the tool with `name` and `position` required. Dropping a 20 x 10 x 4 box 4 mm moves its bounds to z -4..0. The box stock's bounds move by the same 4 mm and the reply lists that stock. Undo and redo restore and replay both bounds exactly.
- `a_quarter_turn_swaps_x_and_y_and_a_later_move_without_rotation_keeps_it`: `rotation: [0, 0, 2, 2]` comes back as `[0, 0, 0.7071…, 0.7071…]`, and the part's X and Y extents swap. A later move with no rotation keeps the turn.
- `move_model_refuses_by_name_and_a_refusal_enters_no_history`: each case is refused by name: a fixture, the work offset, an unknown name, a zero quaternion, a missing position, a 2-number position. None of them moves anything, and the next `undo` still undoes `add_fixture`.

On `main` all three fail at their first `move_model` call, because the tool doesn't exist there.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 6cec6cca. The only later commit, 964e9d4a, adds a line to the decision file.

- **Quick gate plan** (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 6`): no failures, nothing ignored.
  - App lib: 103 passed.
  - App suites: `contour_arc_sim` 1, `mcp` 13, `mcp_live` 10, `mcp_model` 3, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp_pockets` 3, `mcp_render` 5, `mcp_setup` 4, `wall_column_gouge` 3.
  - UI `models`: 4 passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.
- **Not run:** Linux, macOS, the batch tier. `camcraft-cli mcp` over stdio wasn't tried either; the tests drive the same `Server::handle` in-process.

### Note for the process files (not changed here)

The `camcraft-mcp` skill's "Known Remaining Gaps" list still has items 2 (setup alignment, now `set_part_axes`) and 6 (pocket recognition, now `detect_pockets`), which have shipped. With this PR, item 1 (`MoveModel`) is done too. I left the skill alone because editing it is a process change: it needs a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump and an announcement on #681.

Changelog: The MCP server can move and rotate an imported part (`move_model`), with the stock that follows it reported back (#716)

Fixes #716

title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

Changelog: grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic grblHAL 3-axis machine; G41/G42, G84, probing and go-home are refused by name

Fixes #710

title: fix(app): the program sim sweeps a tap at its thread's minor diameter
body:
**Replaces #271**, which closed itself on 2026-11-10 when its branch was pushed: the old fork `austin62jake/Camcraft` had left this repo's fork network, so GitHub could no longer follow its head. Same commits, now from the new fork `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, with `main` f42d3788 merged in (no conflicts). The review history and mkinney's conflict notes are on #271.

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, created 2026-11-10 from upstream `main` f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4).

**Partial fix for #266.** This removes one of the two checks that refuse a tap on a normally modelled hole. The other one still blocks the post; see "What is left" below.

### What changed

- The program sim (the stock-sim clause of the post gate) swept a Tap-kind tool at its full major diameter. CAD models a tapped hole at the thread's minor (tap-drill) size, and a tap only cuts the thread band outside that wall. So the sim read the band as a gouge down the whole hole wall and refused the post.
- A Tap-kind tool now sweeps its thread's core: `diameter / 2 - 0.5413 x pitch`. That is the ISO 724 radial thread depth, the same constant the thread-mill generator already uses (`machining2d::THREAD_DEPTH_PER_PITCH`). For M6 x 1 the core is Ø4.917.
- The rule lives in one place, `operation::tool_law::cutting_radius`, so a later fix to the generator's verify can read the same number. Every other tool still sweeps half its diameter. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name.
- A tap over a hole smaller than its core, or over solid metal, is still a gouge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-minor-sweep.md`.

### Readings

| Case (M6 x 1 tap, plate with a blind hole) | Program sim before | Program sim after |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | gouge, worst 12.000 mm on the hole wall | clean, 0 gouge cells |
| Ø3 hole (too small) | gouge | gouge (still refused) |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`: fails on `main` (`worst 12.000 mm at (-0.31, -2.94, z 8.0)`), passes with the fix.
- `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge`: guards the other side; passes before and after.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

**On this head (9410e5ba, `main` f42d3788 merged), Windows 10:**

- The quick gate's plan (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 4`): app lib 103 passed, plus 24 suites, 130 passed: `carried_fixtures_cache` 6, `carried_verify` 8, `contour_arc_sim` 1, `edge_break_bound` 3, `edge_break_gate` 5, `lathe_field_sim` 6, `lathe_field_tools` 2, `post_not_judged` 4, `posting` 17, `probe_only_sim` 2, `real_tip_contour` 4, `rotary_field_parity` 3, `setup_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `stock_engine_agreement` 0, `stock_export` 2, `stock_field_cost` 0, `stock_sim_document` 9, `stock_view` 4, `tap_sim` 2, `tool_law` 4, `verify` 21, `wall_column_gouge` 3. 7 are `#[ignore]`d in the source (`rotary_field_parity` 1, `stock_engine_agreement` 3, `stock_field_cost` 1, `verify` 2). No failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**On the earlier heads (#271):**


- Both pinning tests alone, with the fix, and with `stock_sim.rs` put back to `main` (the first one fails there as above).
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: app lib plus 13 suites (the gate map's `stock_sim` and `tool_law` suites plus `tap_sim`), 155 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The app, through `camcraft-cli mcp`, built from this branch (upstream `main` 897a820 plus this commit): imported a plate STL with a round Ø5 blind hole, added `TAP-M6` and a Drill/Tap op, generated, verified. The program gate now reports `ok` with no problems. With a Ø3 hole it still reports `gouge: program cuts below the model in 127 cell(s), worst 6.00 mm`.
- Baseline batch tier on clean `main` 897a820 on this machine: all suites pass except three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which also fail without this change. Not run on Linux or macOS.

### What is left (why this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`)

With this fix the Ø5 tap job still does not post. The op's own verify flags `move 1 cuts past the finish surface` and `move 2 cuts past the finish surface` (the tap feeding in and out). That verify hands one tool radius (`tool.geom()`) to every law, including the rapids laws, where a tap's full diameter is the right envelope: a tap must never rapid into the thread band. I tried shrinking only the containment solid law's cutter; the tangency law still flags the same two moves, so I dropped that. Fixing it means splitting the cutting radius from the rapid envelope in the verifier's inputs, and it meets the convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs` that a tapped hole is modelled at the tap's major diameter. I left that for you to decide on the issue.

title: feat(ui,app): every picker resolves through the one pick rule (#692 step 2)
body:
**Stacked on #705** (#692 step 1). It includes #705's commit until that merges; its own commit is the last one.

## What changed (step 2 of #692)
Every viewport picker and the MCP pick tools now resolve through #705's one pick rule. No page carries its own pick logic.

### The UI router: `crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs` (new)
- It builds the `PickRay` from the camera, in perspective or ortho.
- It converts the pixel radius to mm by depth.
- It says which kinds the armed tool accepts:

| Tool | Accepts |
|---|---|
| Plane row | faces only (#554) |
| Axis by edge | edges |
| Axis by two points | points |
| Operation geometry | Face, Edge (with the face between edges) or Vertex mode |
| Boundary | faces or edges |

- **Hover** uses exactly the rule its click would.
- **Origin/WCS chips** read the operation picks, so they get the same rule.

### Removed from the UI
- **`interact.rs`:** `pick_face`, `pick_edge`, `hover_feature_at`, `edge_nearest`, `point_seg_dist_px` and `feature_of_facet`. The old edge pick was screen-space, with no depth test, and offered facet seams. The file drops from 1779 to 1542 lines.
- **`vertex_pick.rs`:** its local nearest/sight logic. It drops from 271 to 122 lines.

### App side
- **`pick/feature_sel.rs` (new):** maps a pick to the `FeatureSel` the pages store (`Chain`, run or `Segment`). `check_pickable` refuses a pick by id that a click could never make.
- **MCP `list_features`:** now lists only feature-edge chains and feature points.
- **Graph cache:** cached per facet allocation, so hover never re-hashes a mesh.
- **Occlusion:** capped at 32 sight rays per candidate tier, a choice measured on `sample_ap214`.

### Intended behaviour changes (#692's rule)
- Rim vertices of round holes and bosses are no longer pickable points.
- Facet seams of smooth walls are no longer edges.
- Hidden edges are no longer pickable.
- In the feature modes, the stock-mesh hover triangle gives way to the feature highlight.

Thresholds and trade-offs are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-wire.md`.

## Tested
**New UI tests** (`egui_app::tests::one_pick_rule`, real egui_kittest clicks):
- `a_click_on_a_flat_faces_diagonal_picks_the_face_never_an_edge`
- `a_click_over_a_hidden_edge_takes_the_near_face_or_nothing_never_the_edge`
- `a_box_corner_picks_as_a_point_where_points_are_taken`
- `a_smooth_walls_facet_seam_is_no_edge`

**New app tests** (`feature_pick_wire`, 4, plus an ignored timing lane):
- `a_pick_resolves_to_the_selection_its_page_stores`
- `the_per_depth_radius_holds_at_a_miss`
- `the_shared_graph_cache_answers_the_same_allocation_without_rebuilding`
- `a_pick_by_id_must_be_one_a_click_could_make`

**New MCP test:** `mcp_pick::listed_chains_and_vertices_follow_the_one_pick_rule`.

**Existing tests rewritten to the new rule:** `vertex_pick_tests` (3, same claims through the real State), `law_tests::feature_pick_tests`, and one `plane_face_pick` assertion.

**Gate:**
- ui: all binaries green (lib 427).
- app: lib 103, `feature_pick` 7, `feature_pick_wire` 4, `pick` 9, `mcp_pick` 3, `mcp` 13, `vertex_pick` 4, `plane_align` 8, `plane_align_edges` 5, `axis_align` 10, `wcs_align` 5, `face_origin` 3, `feature` 18, `fixture_ux` 9, `probe_pick` 9, `mcp_setup` 4.
- clippy `-D warnings`: ui lib+tests and the app lib are clean.

**Timing** (release, 400 hover picks, 12 px radius):

| Model | All kinds, mean | Edges+faces, mean |
|---|---|---|
| sample_ap214 (1.5k facets) | 32 µs | |
| Synthetic 100k-facet cylinder | 2.8 ms | 2.8 ms |

## Not exercised / not done
- **Fixture locate (#566):** not on this base. It wires to `feature_click::feature_at` / `pick::pick_selection` when #566 merges, which is why this says Refs, not Fixes.
- **Pick-through toggle:** not added. `through: false` is set everywhere, and the API keeps the field.
- **Others still owed:**
  - round-edge centres have no `FeatureSel` variant yet;
  - the WCS anchor markers are still overlay picks;
  - the user-docs note for #688 isn't written.
- **Hand check:** no hand GUI check yet. **This stays a draft until the user tries a fresh build.** Clicking is the whole change.

title: feat(machines): Makera Carvera and Carvera Air, with a Carvera post
body:
## What changed

**Machines.** `assets/machines/makera-carvera.mch` and `makera-carvera-air.mch` are new, registered in `posting::MACHINES`. The figures come from the "Specs" tables on Makera's own product pages (read 2026-11-10):

| | Carvera (C1) | Carvera Air |
|---|---|---|
| Work area (mm), as ±stroke | 360 × 240 × 140 | 300 × 200 × 130 |
| Spindle | 200 W, to 15000 rpm | 200 W, to 13000 rpm |
| Axis feed and rapid | 6000 mm/min | 4000 mm/min |
| Tool changer | 6 | none stated (quick changer) |
| Coolant | Air (M7) | Air (M7) |

No `min_speed` is stated, because Makera publishes "0 – 15000 rpm" and the validator refuses 0. The optional 4th-axis module is left out; it's a later step.

**Post.** `assets/posts/carvera.cps` is registered as "Makera Carvera". It writes only words from the firmware's supported-codes tables (Smoothieware-based).

| Area | What it writes |
|---|---|
| Header | `G21 G17 G90 G94`. An inch machine is refused by name, because G20 halts the firmware. |
| Tool change | `M6 Tn`. There's no G43, because the firmware measures tool length itself. Tool 0 (the wireless probe) is refused as a cutter. |
| Spindle and air | `M3 S…`, then the machine's M7 air, off with M9. |
| Arcs | `G2`/`G3` with relative I/J/K, in G17, G18 or G19. |
| Drilling | No canned cycles in the firmware, so drilling posts as its expanded chain, with `G4 P<s>` dwells at the hole bottom. |
| Program end | `M2`, because M30 does nothing on a Carvera. |
| Refused by name | tapping, control cutter compensation, tilted moves and probe operations. |

`docs/decisions/707-carvera.md` records every choice and its source.

## Pinned by

- **`carvera_machines`:** `every_carvera_states_makeras_figures`.
- **`carvera_post`:**
  - `a_two_tool_pocket_posts_in_the_carveras_own_words` locks the golden `golden/nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc` on the shipped C1 file and asserts no G43 / G49 / G40 / G80 / G91.1 / G20 / M8 / M30 / G53;
  - `an_inch_machine_is_refused_by_name`;
  - `tool_zero_is_the_probe_and_refused_as_a_cutter`;
  - `control_cutter_compensation_is_refused_by_name`.
- **`conformance`:** the Carvera on every mill golden (`golden/nc/carvera/`), with `tap_plate` refused by name; the synth stream (`synth_carvera.nc`); and the extension pin.
- **`machine`:** the shipped-machine list.

## How tested

On upstream main plus this branch:
- every `camcraft-app` test suite and `--lib` pass. `lathe_thread_travel` was left out because it doesn't build on main (#686). The `probe_dialects` fix (#700) has already merged.
- clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the app lib and the touched tests.

## Not exercised

There has been no run on a real Carvera or in Carvera Controller. I'm asking a contributor with the machine to run `two_tool_pocket.nc` before the post is trusted on a machine. The fork is synced at v0.16.0; the branch is cut from upstream/main for the current machine registry.

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one the origin stays the model's own. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - four kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

- The pin commit alone is red: at `35f399d1` the `wcs_roles` binary does not compile (no `pick::Role`/`align_roles` on main) and the ui lib does not compile (no `crate::wcs_pick`, row unwired) - the API and surface the pins demand did not exist.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` - 6 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` - 103 passed. Full `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (state.rs and interact.rs touched) - 430 passed, 5 ignored. Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` (`4827fde6`) and re-run green.
- Pre-existing on `origin/main`, untouched here: `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` does not compile - its `OpParams::Threading` initializer was never given #629's `hand` field (verified broken at both `dfb5e6a8` and `4827fde6`). It is the only build failure under `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run`; fixing it belongs in its own PR.

Changelog: the Setups page can set the WCS from feature picks - click faces, edges, corners and walls in the viewport, say what each one sets, and Apply places the work zero on the fitted frame, undo and redo included (#701)

Fixes #701

title: feat(app): one feature graph and pick API - welded faces, feature edges and points, visible-first (#692 step 1)
body:
## What changed (step 1 of #692)
This adds one app-layer picking service. Step 2 (a separate PR) moves every UI picker and the MCP pick tools onto it. No picker uses it yet, so app behaviour is unchanged.

### New modules
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_graph.rs` (330):** the feature graph of a mesh.
  - Welded faces are the existing `geometry::feature` patches, reused through `model::features_of_local`. `list_features` is unchanged.
  - Feature edges are creases between welded faces, plus open boundary edges. Seams between the strips of a tessellated wall are filtered out.
  - Feature points are corners (3 or more edges meet), turns over 30° and chain ends.
  - The graph has a cap-8 cache keyed by the facets' digest.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_arc.rs` (90):** circle and arc centres of round feature-edge runs.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_pick.rs` (314):** the one pick API, `pick_feature(world, &PickQuery { ray, radius, kinds, through }, skip)`, with `pick_bodies` for world-free callers.
  - It finds the front-most surface, then snaps point → centre → edge → face, only among the accepted kinds.
  - Edges and points must be visible from the eye: a perspective view checks the sight line, an ortho view the parallel view line. `through = true` turns the occlusion check off.
- **`pick.rs`:** registers the new modules; `ray_triangle` becomes `pub(crate)` so the new code shares it.

The thresholds and the alternatives dropped are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-graph.md`.

## Tested
**Pinned by `crates/app/tests/feature_pick.rs` (7/7):**
- `flat_face_triangulation_edges_are_not_pickable`
- `cylinder_facet_edges_are_not_pickable_but_its_rim_is`

- app lib 103, `pick` 9, `mcp_pick` 2, `mcp` 13, `face_origin` 3, `vertex_pick` 4, `plane_align` 8, `plane_align_edges` 5, `axis_align` 10, `wcs_align` 5, `feature` 18.

title: fix(cl): clearance-seeded mill paths always open with an approach rapid
body:
## What changed

Follow-up to #690 / #694. Mill generators seed their `PathBuilder` at (0, 0, clearance) and rapid to their start. When the start is exactly X0 Y0, that rapid has zero length and the builder drops it, so the first posted motion was a feed from the tool-change position (#690's bug through another door).

- **`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`:** a new `PathBuilder::approached(seed)`. If a path's first move would not be a rapid, the builder states a zero-length rapid at the seed first.
  - It happens before any move is recorded, so cycle and comp-span indices never shift.
  - It's opt-in: `new()` is unchanged, so drilling, ladders and the lathe keep their openings byte for byte.
- **The 19 motion files** that seeded `PathBuilder::new(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, p.clearance_z))` now use `approached`. Face's #694-only insert is removed in favour of the shared rule.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/697-approached-builder.md`.

## Pinned by

`crates/motion/tests/origin_approach.rs` (new, 5 tests):
- `a_start_at_the_seed_still_opens_with_a_rapid`
- `an_arc_first_move_is_approached_too`
- `a_path_that_opens_with_its_own_rapid_is_unchanged`
- `a_plain_builder_keeps_its_old_behaviour`
- `no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law` (a source scan, so a new generator can't reintroduce it)

`machining2d::a_face_entering_at_the_origin_still_opens_with_its_approach` from #694 still passes through the shared rule.

## How tested

On upstream main 4aec95a9 plus this commit:
- **cl and motion:** every `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-motion` suite passes, and clippy on both with `--tests` is clean.
- **app:** every `camcraft-app` suite and `--lib` pass, apart from two known breaks on main:
  - `lathe_thread_travel` doesn't build (#686).
  - `probe_dialects` fails 3/13 on main; #700 fixes it.
- **Goldens:** no app golden changed, so no existing fixture starts exactly at X0 Y0. Every existing program is byte-identical.

## Not exercised

The lathe generators (blade, parting, contour door and rides) seed at a clearance radius and station and have their own approach rules, so they're out of scope; noted on the issue. No machine run. The fork is synced at v0.16.0.

title: fix(motion): Face opens with an approach rapid on the clearance plane
body:
## What changed

Face's posted program had no approach rapid. The facer started its path *at* its entry point in the air, so its first move was the plunge. Posts write only a move's end point, so the first posted motion after the tool call was a **3-axis feed from wherever the tool change left the spindle, straight to cutting depth** (`G01 X-5 Y5 Z-2 F100` in the old Fanuc golden).

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs`: Face starts its cursor where the other mill generators do, at (0, 0, clearance), and its first move is a rapid on the clearance plane to the entry. The plunge follows. An entry at exactly X0 Y0 (where the builder would drop a zero-length move) states the approach outright as a zero-length rapid.
- Every dialect now posts `G00 X<entry> Y<entry> Z<clearance>` before the plunge feed.
- The Tormach golden's old `G0 X0 Y0 / G0 Z0` opening (the #131 workaround in the script, which had no start point to use) now goes to the real entry.

The decision record is in `docs/decisions/690-face-approach.md`. A generic post-layer approach rule was considered and dropped as wider than this bug.

## Goldens and tests updated

- **Goldens:** the `face_square_40x40{,_blended,_stepped}.cl` goldens and all their `.nc` goldens (Fanuc, Haas, Tormach, Mazak, Sinumerik, Heidenhain) gain the approach. So do `program_entry/{fanuc,haas}_pause_home.nc`.
- **`regression_models`:** path moves +1, posted lines +1, minutes plus the approach rapid's time.
- **`fixture_law_gaps`:** with a clamp arm over the plunge, the gate now names the approach (move 0) as well as the plunge (move 1).
- **`tormach_post`:** the line before the first feed is still a rapid to clearance. It now restates X Y.
- **`machining2d`:** `rapids_only_appear_at_the_ends` and `face_steps_down_through_levels` count the approach.

## Pinned by

- `machining2d::rapids_only_appear_at_the_ends` (the first move is a rapid at clearance, then the plunge)
- `machining2d::a_face_entering_at_the_origin_still_opens_with_its_approach` (new; the X0 Y0 edge)
- the regenerated face `.cl` and `.nc` goldens (`golden_cl`, `conformance`, `fanuc_post`, `heidenhain_block_form`, `program_entry`)

## How tested

On the fork base (v0.16.0):
- all `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion` debug suites pass;
- clippy on `camcraft-motion --tests` is clean.

After merging upstream/main into the branch (an import-line conflict in `face.rs`, resolved):
- all `camcraft-motion` suites pass;
- every `camcraft-app` suite that uses Face passes;
- clippy is clean.

## Not exercised

Two failures come from upstream main and are not caused by this branch:
- **`lathe_thread_travel` doesn't build.** This is #686.
- **`probe_tormach` fails 6/7.** Its Tormach probe goldens from #583 are stale against #579's (#570) probe cycle. I'm filing this separately.

The other generators that start their cursor at (0, 0, clearance) may share the X0 Y0 edge. They weren't checked here; a note goes on the issue.

No machine run. The fork is synced at v0.16.0.

Changelog: Face programs open with a rapid to the start point on the clearance plane instead of a feed from the tool-change position to cutting depth (#690)

Fixes #690

title: fix(motion): a step too small to ladder is refused by name, never allocated
body:
## What changed
A stepover or stepdown that's too small to ladder is now refused by name at generate. It no longer allocates until the process aborts (#691).

- **The ladders:** `motion::machining2d::band` (Face, zigzag pocket and slot rows) and `cut_levels` (every depth-stepping 2D op and the 3D entry ladders) now return `Result`.
- **The check:** before allocating, `pass_budget` refuses a step that needs more than `MAX_PASSES` (100 000) passes, or one too small to advance the coordinate (`span + step == span`). The message names the parameter: `stepover 1e-9 mm over 4.000 mm needs more than 100000 passes - raise the stepover`.
- **Callers:** face, bore, circular, contour/chain, pocket, troch/HSM pocket, slots and 3D entry propagate the refusal with `?`.
- **Normal steps** produce byte-identical output.

The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/691-tiny-step.md`.

## Tested
**Pinned by:** `crates/motion/tests/tiny_step.rs`
- `a_face_stepover_too_small_to_ladder_is_refused_by_name`: 1e-9, and 1e-300 (below float resolution).
- `a_stepdown_too_small_to_ladder_is_refused_by_name_on_face_and_contour`: staged Face and 2D Contour at 1e-9.
- `a_small_but_real_step_still_generates`: 0.05 mm still runs.

**Gate (`scripts/gate.sh quick`), on upstream main b57f8d52+:**
- geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion (incl. `tiny_step`) and ui suites are green.
- The app suites and the full clippy failed to compile only on `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` (missing `hand`). That break is already on main and is tracked as #686, not this PR.
- So I ran these instead:
  - app lib;
  - app `face_holes`, `face_blend`, `mill2d_b`, `mill2d_c`, `golden_cl`, `roughing2d`, `operations`, `mcp`, `corner_blend`, `control_comp`, `level_links`, `slot_caps`, `whole_model_pocket`: all green;
  - clippy `-D warnings` on motion (all targets) and the app lib: clean.

## Not exercised
- **Offset-ring pockets and 3D stepovers:** these generators have their own loops and don't go through `band`/`cut_levels`. They're not reported crashing, and this PR leaves them alone.
- **Live repro:** I didn't run the MCP repro in the GUI or the CLI live. The refusal reaches it as a normal `GenError` at generate.

Changelog: A stepover or stepdown too small to ladder (over 100 000 passes) is refused by name at generate instead of aborting on a huge allocation (#691)

Fixes #691

title: docs(process): /resolve-conflicts skill and the conflict rule in the automation law (PROCESS_VERSION 3)
body:
Adds the **`/resolve-conflicts`** project skill and a rule for it in AGENTS.md's Autonomous Work Law.

- **Contributor mode** (`/resolve-conflicts [login]`): for the author's conflicting PRs it merges main (no rebase, no force), keeps both sides of additive conflicts, takes main's snapshot PNGs and changelog files, runs the targeted gate, pushes, and comments "ready for a re-check". When both sides changed the same logic, or a safety rule could be dropped, it stops and reports the hunk.
- **Maintainer mode** (`/resolve-conflicts check`): re-reads every `conflicts` PR. If it still conflicts, the author is asked once. If it's clean again, the label is dropped and it's sent to the review it needs: `merge-ready` restored, a delta review, or a full review.
- **AGENTS.md:** the new rule, including that fork agents run contributor mode each session.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`:** 2 to 3 (to be announced on #681).

Docs and process only.

title: feat(app,motion): drilling refusals mark the hole they are about
body:
#677, the follow-up to #261 part 2: the drilling refusals that quote a hole now name it, so the viewport marks the hole and the op page's refusal line jumps to it.

**Stacked on #678.** This branch is built on `vilts:issue/261-refused-location`. Because that branch lives in a fork, this PR can't target it, so it targets `main`, and until #678 merges its diff also shows #678's commit (82428410). **Review only the last commit (016d417d).** Once #678 merges, this PR shrinks to that commit. #678 is a `feat` that merges at the cut, so this one merges at the same cut, after it.

Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

- **Axial drill (app):** the flute-reach, holder and shank-fit refusals (`drill_reach`) and the R-plane refusal (`drill_top`) mark the hole at the material top their law measured from. When that top is unknown, they use the entry Z.
- **Cross drill:**
  - The flute-reach refusal (`cross_reach`, already in world) and the finished-part refusal (`cross_part`) mark the modelled mouth.
  - The kernel's plunge-axis and bottom-above-entry refusals (`drilling/cross.rs`), and the raw stock's plunge-direction refusal (`cross_stock`), mark the local mouth, which `in_world` carries to world.
  - `to_raw_mouths` was the one spindle-frame refusal that didn't pass through `in_world`; now it does. Its sentence for an off-origin work offset now quotes the world mouth, like every other cross-hole refusal. Nothing changes on origin.
- **Lathe axial drill (`drilling/axial.rs`):** the off-axis and wider-than-bore refusals mark the mouth. The past-the-bar-end refusal marks the floor.
- **Listed sites that name no spot** get a one-line comment saying why:
  - The stitch fork runs at collect time, in the tilted walk frame, before `run_job` maps frames.
  - The turning chamfer/taper doors name meridian stations, and there is no meridian-to-world map yet.
  - The deburr, rotary-height, bore-bar and thread-axis refusals are about a size or an angle, not a place.
- `drilling/cross.rs` is at 401 lines, from 400. A local closure keeps the change to one line.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/677-refusal-spots.md`.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests (existing refusal tests that now also assert the spot):
- `camcraft-motion` lib:
  - `drilling::tests_cross::cross_drill_refuses_nonsense_by_name` (a Z plunge marks its mouth)
  - `drilling::tests_cross::cross_drill_refuses_a_bottom_above_the_mouth`
- `camcraft-app`:
  - `drill_rplane::an_r_plane_below_the_unfaced_stock_top_is_refused_by_name`: spot (0, 0, 25), the stock top.
  - `drill_reach_fit::a_bore_bar_whose_shank_is_wider_than_the_hole_is_refused_by_name`
  - `drill_reach::a_short_flute_cross_drill_on_raw_stock_wider_than_the_part_is_refused_by_name`: world mouth (10, 0, 0), on lathe and mill-turn.
  - `drilling_axial::an_off_axis_hole_refuses_by_name`
  - `drilling_axial::a_hole_past_the_bar_end_refuses_by_name`: the floor.

Quick gate (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -Base 82428410` on the last commit, by a separate gate-runner agent): green.
- motion: lib plus 10 mapped test binaries, 0 failed.
- app: lib plus 12 mapped binaries (drill_*, drilling_cross_*, stitch_cross, deburr_links, edge_break_gate), plus drilling_axial, lathe_post_refusals, operations and refusal_location; 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden changed.

## Not exercised

- An off-origin cross drill hitting the raw-stock plunge-direction refusal. The shift is `in_world`'s, which its own unit test (from #678) covers.
- Located refusals under a 3+2 tilt, same as #678.
- Nothing in the UI changed; #678 covers the mark and the link.

Changelog: Drilling refusals (flute reach, holder, shank fit, R plane, cross-hole and lathe axial doors) now mark the hole they name in the viewport (#677)

Fixes #677

title: docs(process): review-prs posts an estimated token cost when a PR turns merge-ready
body:
Adds **step 2c** to the `review-prs` skill. When a review ends `merge-ready`, the dispatcher posts one comment with the estimated agent token cost of getting that PR there.

- **Marker:** `<!-- review-cost: <head sha> -->`, so the comment is never posted twice for the same head.
- **What's counted:** every dispatched run on the PR: reviews, re-reviews, conflict and replacement agents, and the fix agent for our own PRs. Each run's tokens come from its completion notification.
- **Pricing:** a blended upper estimate, 90 % input / 10 % output at list price. Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M. Cache reads make the real cost lower.
- **Not counted:** main-session coordination isn't attributable per PR, and the comment says so.
- **Other verdicts:** no cost comment for red, orange or yellow. The next merge-ready review sums every run so far.

Docs and process only. Merged directly on the maintainer's instruction.

title: feat(post): a PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL
body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/671-plasma-post.md` (the sources and ten choices). CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md are updated.

## Golden (`tormach-plasma/plasma_plate_with_holes.nc`, inch; excerpt)
```
G20
G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80
G64 P0.005 Q0.005
(T1 PLASMA TORCH - KERF 0.0591)
G54
G43 H1
G30
(C0 INNER IN C4 - SMALL HOLE 65% FEED)
G0 X3.3465 Y0.7874
M200
M207 P0.1496
M209 P0.5
G15
G16
G1 X3.3465 Y0.9547 F63.98
...
M205
G30
```
Siblings: `_mm.nc` and `_control.nc` (`G41.1 D0.0591` … `G40`). The CLI post is byte-identical to the inch golden.

## How tested
- **`plasma_post` (5):**
  - the inch and mm goldens, with structural checks: no Z/S/T/M3-M9/M6, per-contour order, G30 after every M205, ending `G30 M30`;
  - the in-app dump equals the `.cl` golden;
  - the control-comp golden;
  - a stream round-trip, plus malformed-record refusals;
  - an in-app 1300PL document posts through the gate.
- **`plasma_post_refusals` (5):** every refusal, the engine torch law, every milling builtin declining the stream, and the registry.
- **Pins updated:** plasma_machine, machine_library, plasma_profile, golden_cl and conformance.
- **Gate:**
  - those suites plus posting, camcraft-post and camcraft-cl;
  - also tormach_post, control_comp, coolant, after_op, program_comments, fanuc_post, lathe_post, per_op_files and probe_guard;
  - clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (why this is a draft): a PathPilot Hub 1300PL simulator run
It should check:
1. G20 and G21 both load and run, and `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` reads as inches under G21.

title: feat(app,ui): a refused generation marks the spot it names
body:
#261 part 2 (show where a refused generation was refused), by the triage's middle ground: a refused generation does not draw a partial path; it **marks the spot its refusal names** and lets the user jump there. Nothing is generated or cached, so nothing refused can post.

Fork synced at v0.16.0 (branch made from `vilts/Camcraft` main at 66791aa6, which contains the v0.16.0 tag).

## What changed

- **motion**: `GenError` gains `At { msg, at }` (built with `GenError::invalid_at`), plus `location()` / `map_location()`. It displays exactly like `Invalid`, so no refusal sentence, log line or golden changes. A non-finite spot is dropped, never stored. The enum moved to `machining2d/gen_error.rs`; `face.rs` re-exports it, so every `super::face::GenError` path is untouched.
- **First adopters** (the refusals that already quoted a coordinate):
  - Face: the narrow strip between two holes (the #260 shape). The spot is the strip's midpoint on the quoted row, at the cut height; `face_holes::narrow_gap` now also returns that midpoint.
  - Drill cycle: the R-plane, counterbore, bore-fit and centre-cutting doors (the hole's mouth).
  - Bore and Thread: the counterbore and fit doors (the hole's mouth).
  - Plunge law: "would plunge axially into solid" (the plunge's bottom).
- **app**:
  - `run_job` carries the spot from the generator's frame to world through the op's `TiltedFrame`.
  - The generate command turns it into `CommandError::MachiningAt { msg, at }`, which reads like `Machining`; `CommandError::location()` returns the spot.
  - The cross-hole spindle frame (`cross_spindle::in_world`) moves the spot by the same world/local shift it already applies to the sentence.
  - `plunge_solid`'s reason-appending arm keeps the spot.
- **ui**:
  - `State::feedback_at` sits beside the refusal sentence and is read only through `State::refusal_focus()`. That returns `None` as soon as the refusal no longer describes the page: the next command, undo/redo, another op on the page, or a draft edit.
  - The viewport draws a 3-axis cross at the spot in the colour-vision palette's gouge colour (`path_lines::refusal_mark`). It is twice the size of a warned move's cross, so the two never read alike.
  - The op page's refusal line becomes a link: the hover says so, and a click centres the camera on the spot (part 1's `frame_at`; view state, no command).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/261-refused-location.md`.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-motion` lib `machining2d::gen_error::tests::{a_located_refusal_reads_exactly_like_an_invalid_one, a_non_finite_spot_is_dropped_never_shown, the_spot_rides_the_frame_map_and_unlocated_refusals_pass}`
- `camcraft-motion` `face_holes::the_narrow_strip_refusal_points_at_the_strip`
- `camcraft-motion` lib `drilling::tests::depth_override_applies_to_every_hole` (now also pins the mouth)
- `camcraft-app` `refusal_location::{a_refused_hole_names_its_mouth_in_world, the_spot_is_the_hole_the_refusal_is_about, a_refusal_about_no_spot_names_none}`
- `camcraft-app` lib `operation::cross_spindle::tests::a_located_kernel_refusal_lands_on_the_world_mouth`
- `camcraft-ui` lib `refusal_focus_tests::{a_refused_generation_marks_its_spot_and_caches_nothing, the_mark_retires_with_the_refusal}`
- `camcraft-ui` lib `path_lines::tests::a_refused_spot_draws_one_wide_gouge_cross_and_nothing_when_non_finite`

Quick gate (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick` on 82428410, by a separate gate-runner agent): green.
- motion: lib plus 36 test binaries, 500 passed, 0 failed.
- app: lib plus 114 test binaries (`center_cut_multiaxis` included), 1091 passed, 0 failed.
- ui: lib plus 11 test binaries, 488 passed, 0 failed (pixel snapshots ignored, as in quick).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden changed.

## Not exercised

- The op-page link click in a live window. The link is a plain clickable `egui::Label` with a hover hint (`REFUSAL_LINK_HINT`) that calls the same `frame_at` part 1's warning links use. `refusal_focus` and the overlay are pinned at state level; there is no kittest click test.
- A located refusal under a real 3+2 tilt: the frame map is `TiltedFrame::to_world`, already covered by its own tests, and the call site is one line in `run_job`.
- No pixel snapshot changes (snapshots are release-lane).

## Left open

- The other ~620 refusal sites that name no spot yet. They adopt one by one (swap `GenError::Invalid(format!(..))` for `GenError::invalid_at(format!(..), spot)`); follow-up issue #677.
- Drawing the partial path a generator built before it refused stays out of scope (the triage's "large, and a design call"). That's why this PR says `Refs`: the maintainer decides whether #261 closes with this or stays open for that.

Changelog: A refused toolpath generation now marks the spot it names in the viewport, and its message on the operation page jumps there (#261 part 2)

Refs #261

title: feat(sim): plasma through-cut laws - cut order, kerf crossing, tip-up
body:
## What changed

**#672 step 1** (part of #621's plasma research): `sim::verify::plasma`, the laws that replace the gouge and collision checks for a 2D plasma through-cut. Based on main, with no dependency on #674 or #670.

**What it judges:** a neutral `PlasmaProgram`:
- the kerf;
- the cuts in cut order, each the torch-on polyline with its contour id, inner/outer and parent outer;
- the rapid into each cut.

So it reads the CL's torch records (#670's `TorchOn { contour, inner, parent }` / `TorchOff`) and nothing of the operation's internals.

| Law | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Cut order:** an inner contour cut after the outer that frees its part | **refusal** | plain plasma practice; the part drops before its holes |
| **Kerf crossing:** a cut within one kerf of an earlier cut's centre line | warning | LinuxCNC Plasma Primer §12 (THC dive into an open kerf) |
| **Tip-up:** a rapid across a part already cut free | warning | Tormach 1300PL manual UM10720 §1.4.2, §4.12.8 |
| **Malformed:** a non-positive or non-finite kerf, a NaN point, a cut with no path | **refusal** | Prime Directive |

**Not yet wired.** Step 2 builds the `PlasmaProgram` from the plasma op's CL torch records once #670 lands, blocks the post on a refusal, and updates the machine check's `notes` (#674) to say these laws judge plasma ops.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs`, 5/5.** Each law is tripped by one fixture and passed by another:
  - a plate with a hole, hole-first (clean) versus outline-first (refused);
  - two outlines 1 mm apart at a 1.5 mm kerf (warned) versus 5 mm apart (clear);
  - a rapid over a freed part (warned) versus around it (clear);
  - the malformed kerf, point and path cases.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass.
- **Clippy** on sim with `-D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The CL reader and verdict wiring (step 2, after #670). The 2D gouge (the kerf band against the part's section) needs the part's 2D section from the op, also step 2.

Changelog: none (internal: plasma laws, not yet wired)

Refs #672

title: feat(machines): a plasma machine kind and the Tormach 1300PL
body:
First slice of the plasma work (#621 research → #669-#672): a **`plasma` machine kind** and the **Tormach 1300PL**.

## What changed
- **`Kind::Plasma`** (`kind: plasma`, "plasma cutting"), declared only and never inferred from the axes. `Kind` moves to `crates/post/src/machine/kind.rs` and is re-exported.
- **File rules,** in one place: `machine/plasma.rs::plasma_refusals`. These are refused by name:
  - any `spindle.*` key, each one separately;
  - `live_tool`;
  - coolant (station or tooling root);
  - any rotary axis.
  - The Machines-pane validator also requires X, Y and Z (Z is the torch lifter).
  - The rules are held at every door: `parse_mch`, the validator, and `Machine::is_sane` for project files and `SetSetupMachine`.
- **Machine check** (`crates/app/src/machine/plasma.rs`):
  - **Judged:** X/Y travel (arc quarter points included), the X/Y share of each feed, and the tool count.
  - **Refused by name:** a non-plasma op ("a Face operation is milling work - a plasma table cuts only plasma operations"), a tool with rpm, and a tilted move.
  - **Skipped:** Z depth and travel, and rpm and spindle power. They are **named, not failed**: a new non-blocking `MachineCheck.notes`, which the status line prints as "not judged: …".
  - The per-move helpers move to `machine/judge.rs`, so `mod.rs` drops from 427 to 370 lines.
- **Command door:** `family_gate` refuses milling and turning ops on a plasma setup, and the ribbon shows no section. **No op can be posted on a plasma table until #670.**
- **Posts:** a new `posting::PLASMA_POSTS`, empty until #671. Every cutting post declines a plasma table, and `post_offer` never offers a post that wouldn't serve the mounted machine.
- **`assets/machines/tormach-1300pl.mch`** (UM10720 v1223A §2.2.1 and the 03/24 spec sheet):
  - inch; X ±48.5, Y ±50, Z ±3.9. The smaller of the two documents' figures (the manual says X 50 / Y 51.5); both are recorded;
  - 1000 IPM on X/Y and 120 IPM on Z; rapid unstated;
  - a torch head with no spindle; `number_of_tools: 1`; no `safe_retract` (the plasma post retracts with G30).
- **UI:** the machine editor's kind combo and the Machines pane's New blank list offer plasma.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/669-plasma-kind.md`.
  - Kerf lives on the torch tool, as its diameter, so the existing offset code works unchanged.
  - Coolant is refused.
  - A second tool, such as a scribe, stays allowed.

**Seams left for the sibling issues:**
- **#670:** add a `Family` arm in the exhaustive `cuts_plasma`, plus a torch tool kind (relax `Tool::is_sane`'s rpm > 0 for torches only).
- **#671:** add a BUILTINS entry and its name to `PLASMA_POSTS`.
- **#672:** owns what the check skips.

## How tested
- **New `plasma_machine` (6):**
  - spindle, coolant and rotary keys and a missing Z are refused by name;
  - an unknown kind is still refused, and undeclared XYZ reads as a mill;
  - the 1300PL spec pin;
  - the check skips depth and rpm with a note and judges XY (a mill-kind copy does report Z);
  - a mill op is refused at the command door and at the verification gate;
  - a 1300PL setup round-trips byte-identical, and a hand-edited rpm refuses to load.
- **Updated:** the machine, machine_library, machine_edit and tormach_safe_retract expectations.
- **Gate:**
  - machine, machine_edit, machine_library, tormach_machines, tormach_safe_retract, sinumerik_safe_retract, axis_direction, posting, conformance, project_roundtrip, ribbon, lathe_post, setup_mounts_post, tormach_post, vmc_stroke and lathe_stroke pass;
  - camcraft-post passes, and the ui machine and ribbon lib tests pass;
  - clippy is clean on post, app and ui.

**MACHINES list:** this PR appends to `posting::MACHINES`, as do #624, #627, #634 and #654. Whichever merges later takes a trivial list merge.

Changelog: A plasma machine kind (`kind: plasma` - X/Y cut, Z torch lifter, no spindle; spindle, coolant and rotary keys refused by name; machine check judges X/Y travel and feed, skips Z depth and rpm with a named note) and the Tormach 1300PL machine (UM10720 / spec sheet 03/24); no op or post serves it yet (#670, #671) (#669)

Fixes #669

title: fix(ui): the setup-pick sweep runs every frame, whatever the dock shows
body:
**Stacked on #666** (#664, setup picks disarm on page change). Review only this PR's own commit, `75c8b710`.

**P2 (#667, found in M5's review of #666):** #666's disarm sweep ran inside `pages::properties`, so only while the Properties tab was drawn. With the tab closed or hidden behind another tab, an armed Setups pick stayed armed and viewport clicks fed the hidden draft.

## What changed
- **`shell_layout`** wraps the dock with the sweep, once per frame.
  - **Before the dock:** if `layout::is_shown(dock, Properties)` is false, `axis_pick::disarm_all` runs. `is_shown` is new: the tab is in the dock, active in its leaf, and the leaf isn't collapsed.
  - **After the dock:** `axis_pick::disarm_hidden` runs.
- **Ordering:** viewport clicks are routed inside the dock, and egui_dock draws leaves by node index, so the viewport can draw before Properties.
  - The before-dock check closes the one-frame gap: a pane hidden by a click in frame N-1 is disarmed before frame N's viewport runs.
  - It also stops a stale `axis_rows_shown` from letting `hint_stray` swallow clicks while the pane is closed.
  - This is documented at the call site and in `docs/decisions/667-sweep-every-frame.md`.
- **`pages::properties`** loses #666's wrapper and is back to a single function. The rows still mark themselves.

## How tested
- **`setup_picks_disarm`, now 5 tests (headless, real clicks through the View door):**
  - `an_axis_pick_disarms_when_the_properties_tab_is_closed`: arm +Y by Edge and pick, close Properties, click the part, and the draft is unchanged. Reopening shows "Pick +Y edge" with the edge kept.
  - `a_plane_pick_disarms_when_another_tab_hides_the_properties_pane`: opening Machines in front of Properties disarms the face pick. Closing Machines shows "Pick a face" with the face kept.
  - Both fail without the fix. #666's three tests still pass.
- **Gate:**
  - ui lib 391 pass. The 1 failure is the known no-GPU `headless_run_succeeds` in the agent sandbox;
  - boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick and operations pass;
  - clippy is clean. No snapshot PNGs changed.

Changelog: A Setups page pick (axis by Edge or Two points, or lay-on-a-plane) now disarms when the Properties tab is closed or hidden behind another tab, so viewport clicks no longer feed the hidden setup draft (#667)

Fixes #667

title: fix(ui): setup picks disarm when their page is left
body:
**Stacked on #573** (#557, part axes by edge or two points). Review only this PR's own commit, `04d8f749`.

**P2 (#664, found in M5's review of #573):** an armed Setups-page pick stayed armed after leaving the page. Edge, vertex and face clicks on an operation page then fed the hidden setup draft instead of the operation's geometry.

## What changed (ephemeral view state, no command)
- **One sweep.** `pages::properties` clears the "rows drawn" markers (`axis_rows_shown`, the new `State::setup_pick_rows`) and draws the page. It then calls `axis_pick::disarm_hidden`, which stops every armed axis or plane pick whose setup rows weren't drawn this frame.
  - That covers a page or tab change, opening an operation, closing the section, and another setup's page.
  - The axis and plane rows record their setup each frame they are drawn.
- **The plane draft is paused, not dropped.** `PlanePick` gains `picking`, `pause()` and `collecting()`.
  - Re-arming resumes it with the face kept, and on return the row shows the picked face and Apply while disarmed.
  - The row's own "Stop picking" still drops the draft.
- **Click routing:** `interact.rs`, `vertex_pick.rs` and `hint_stray` ask `plane_pick::collecting`. The plane outlines draw only while collecting, the same as the axis draft.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/664-disarm-setup-picks.md` (one sweep rather than per-navigation resets; pause rather than drop).

## How tested
- **New `tests/setup_picks_disarm.rs` (headless, real clicks).** Each test arms the pick from its row and picks once, then switches to the Contour1 operation page and clicks the same pixel: Contour1 gets the pick and the setup draft is unchanged. Back on the setup page, the pick is disarmed and kept.
  - `an_axis_edge_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left`
  - `an_axis_two_points_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left`
  - `a_plane_face_pick_disarms_when_its_page_is_left` (re-arming resumes with the face)
  - With the sweep commented out, all three fail.
- **Updated:** `plane_face_pick`'s existing test armed the plane pick while the operation page was showing, which was the bug. It now opens the setup page first.

title: feat(post): Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor (#614)
body:
(fork synced at v0.16.0)

Implements a dedicated post-processor dialect for Doosan DNM vertical machining centers with Fanuc 0i / 31i-M controls (#614).

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`**:
  - Clean-room implementation specced from published Fanuc 0i/31i operator manuals and Doosan Infracore / DN Solutions DNM series programming guides (behavior only, clean-room protocol).
  - **Through-Spindle Coolant (TSC):** Supports `PARAM Coolant through-tool`. Emits Doosan high-pressure TSC M-code `M88` (with `M89`/`M09` on shut-off). Supports `useM8ForTSC` option for machines where TSC is triggered via `M08`.
  - **Rotary Table Brake (4th-axis A):** On index positioning (`G00 A...`), unclamps the pneumatic brake (`M11`) before rotating, and clamps the brake (`M10`) after positioning before cutting moves.
  - **High-Speed Smoothing / AICC (`G05.1 Q1` / `G05.1 Q0`):** Modal Fanuc AI Contour Control lookahead smoothing. Automatically deactivated (`G05.1 Q0`) prior to canned drilling cycles (`G73`, `G81-G89`), probing (`G31`), tool change, and program close, and reactivated on subsequent cutting moves.
  - **Chip Conveyor:** Commands `M31` (start) and `M33` (stop) when chip conveyor option is enabled.
  - **Probing:** Supports standard Fanuc `G31` macro-B skip moves and Renishaw Inspection Plus macro format (`G65 P9810`/`G65 P9811`) when `probingStyle: "inspection-plus"` is requested.
- **`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`**:
  - Doosan DNM 5700 machine definition (X: 1020 mm, Y: 570 mm, Z: 510 mm, 12,000 RPM, rapid 36/36/30 m/min, coolants Flood M8, Mist M7, Through-tool M88).
- **Registry & Conformance**:
  - Registered in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
  - Registered in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` (`POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS`), with all 13 golden `.nc` outputs locked under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/doosan-dnm/`.
- **Decision Record**:
  - Recorded in `docs/decisions/614-doosan-dnm-post.md`.

## How tested

- **`crates/app/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `doosan_dnm_posts_basic_milling_clean`: basic program structure, preamble, tool change, work offset, retracts, safe end.
  - `doosan_dnm_through_spindle_coolant_modes`: verifies M88/M89 default TSC and M8 option.
  - `doosan_dnm_rotary_brake_clamp_unclamp`: verifies M11 unclamp precedes A-axis indexing and M10 clamp precedes cutting.
  - `doosan_dnm_high_speed_smoothing_aicc`: verifies G05.1 Q1 engagement and G05.1 Q0 deactivation before canned drilling cycles.
  - `doosan_dnm_chip_conveyor`: verifies M31 start and M33 stop.
  - `doosan_dnm_probing_modes`: verifies standard G31 skip and Inspection Plus G65 macro formats.
- **`crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` across all 13 goldens.
  - `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`, `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`, `the_dialects_actually_differ`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- Physical cutting on a physical machine tool (the issue author `@spikeypineapple` offered to test on their DNM).

Changelog: Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor with through-spindle coolant, 4th-axis rotary brake clamp/unclamp, G05.1 AICC smoothing, chip conveyor, and probing (#614)

title: feat(post): probing on an inverted X/Y axis for the Haas post
body:
**Stacked on #522** (the Haas, Mazak and Siemens probing hooks). Review only this PR's own commit, `8f0a6d1b`.

The Haas part of #392. #465 made the Fanuc post probe on an inverted X/Y behind the manifest flag `probeAxisInversion`, and left Haas until its probing hooks landed.

## What changed
- **`haas.cps` declares `probeAxisInversion = true`.** #522's Haas hooks write the same controller words as Fanuc:
  - G31, the trip read from `#5061-#5063`, and a `#3000=2` no-contact alarm;
  - a `G91 G1` back-off and the deviation into `#190..`;
  - `G10 L2 P.. X[#5221+#190]`.
  - Each reads in the controller's own frame, so #465's mirrored stream gives the **physical** correction with no Haas-specific code. A comment in the probing section says why.
  - The `onProbeGuard` positioning moves mirror correctly too.
- **`invert.rs`:** the refusal text now names "Fanuc and Haas". `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is updated to match.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/392-haas-probe-inverted.md`. It records the reasoning, what was dropped (a separate Haas macro reader; relying on G101 or the control's axis-direction setting) and the sources.

## How tested
- **`inverted_probe` (9) now runs every case for both posts:**
  - the cases: face −Z / −X, edge −Y, corners +X+Y / −X−Y, bore and boss;
  - each on standard, inverted X, inverted Y and inverted XY machines;
  - G55 lands on the physical datum, and a part where the model says leaves the datum unchanged;
  - no contact alarms `#3000=2`, and out of tolerance alarms `#3000=1`;
  - the converse also holds: the untranslated program misses, and undoing any one translated word breaks it.
- **New tests:**
  - `an_uninverted_program_is_unchanged_by_the_flag`: both posts give byte-identical standard-machine output, and #173's Haas golden is unchanged;
