title: feat(setups): part alignment turns about the WCS origin and lays the picked face down
body:
**Stacked on #603** (#330, the face-lay rows, which also carries #593 and #573). Review only this PR's own commit, `e14ee4a2`.

#606 left three items to decide. Each is recorded in `docs/decisions/606-align-pivot.md`, with what was considered and dropped.

## 1. The typed-angle Apply turns about the WCS origin, with a choice
- **Default pivot: the setup's WCS origin.** That is the WCS entity's position, or zero if none is placed, read the same way as `posting::wcs_context`. The part point on the origin stays on it, which answers the maintainer's report that alignment "shifts the model relative to the origin".
- **Angles stay absolute from "as modelled".** Re-applying the same angles is refused ("already holds the part that way") rather than drifting. All-zero means "as modelled".
- **The choice:** an `about [WCS origin | part centre]` combo sits beside Apply, and the tooltip names the pivot. "Part centre" is the old behaviour.
- **Presets (Flip over X, Turn Z 90, …) still turn about the part centre,** and their tooltip says so. About the origin, a flip would put a part sitting on Z 0 under the table.
- **Code:** new `crates/app/src/setup_turn.rs` and `AlignPartToSetup::turn(…, pivot)`. `CommandKind::AlignPart` gains `pivot`. It is still **one undoable command**.

## 2. Lay on a plane defaults to face down (maintainer's call: recommended option taken)
- The face row's "Flip" becomes **"Face down"**, on for a new pick: the picked face sits on the plane with the part on top. The points row's "Flip points" becomes **"Points down"**, also on by default.
- **Only the UI draft default changed.** `PlaneLay::flip` keeps its meaning for the app, MCP and scripts.
- **Saved setups store the resulting transform, so old projects load and post identically.**

## 3. The structural test checks the pane, not the window
- `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` now asserts every alignment control, including the new combo and Apply, lies inside the **properties pane's tab rect**.
- Putting the face row back on one line (the #330 regression) **fails** the test: `"Face down" … [[1349.8 344] - [1429.4 362]]` against the pane's right edge at x 1264.

## How tested
- **New app suite `turn_pivot` (5):**

- **New UI tests (headless, real clicks):**

title: refactor(sim): a carried field reads back as the column body, the same on both engines
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #651** (#637 step C), which is stacked on #649 and #646. Merge them in order #646, #649, #651, then this. This is **#637 step D**.

**New `CarriedField::column_body(lattice, judged_before) -> Body`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_body.rs`) reads the carried, clipped field onto the next setup's lattice (`Lattice { x0, y0, cell, nx, ny }`, new frame).
- **Per column:**
  - the **top** is one down-march (`march`);
  - the **floor** is step B's exact shell floor (`floor_at`);
  - a **flip** swaps them, since the new top is the old floor;
  - the **clip** trims the column, and `Clip::Empty` leaves every column empty;
  - a floor a cut reached, or a column the field cannot read, is **refused by name**.
- **The result** is the same `carry::Body` the column engine makes (new `Body::from_parts`), so `deviate` (the two-sided verdict), `display`, `volume` and `bounds` run **unchanged** on either engine.
- **Plumbing:** `march::world` is now `pub(crate)`.

**A decision, recorded in `docs/decisions/637-carried-field-read-back.md`:** this replaces the planned `Body = Column | Field` enum. The enum needed a second, field-native implementation of every `Body` method, each new verdict code to prove. The read-back reuses the one verdict the column carry already proves, and tops and floors still come from the field, never interpolated.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/carry_engine_agreement.rs`, 2/2, about 3 s in debug.** The same 20×12 block, cut by the same slot (shallow at z 3, deep at z 1), is carried through **all 8 lattice turns** (quarter turns and flips) on **both** engines.
  - Per column, `empty_at` matches and the top and floor agree to **1e-6**.
  - The volumes agree to 1e-6, and `floor_judged` matches.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: field_carry 8, field_floor 3, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3, and app setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, rest_across_setups 7.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

- **Step E:** the app holders (#586) taking a field carry. Nothing in the app calls `column_body` yet.
- **A field-native verdict finer than the lattice:** possible later behind the same `Body` API.
- **The two #651 nits** (a `Display` for `ClipRefusal`, and the mod sort order) are left for step E, which touches the same file.

title: fix(app): the lathe stroke check judges the posted radius, not world X
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting and the built-in Lathe's X floor of -2.5). Review only this PR's own commit, `dd45a6c4`.

**P1 (#647):** the machine travel check compared each move's **world X** with a lathe's X band. Turning kernels carry their radius on the **Y meridian**, so a lathe radial over-travel was never judged. It also judged the nose-centre cache, not the control point the post writes.

## What changed
- **New `crates/app/src/machine/lathe_stroke.rs`.** On lathe-kind machines only, each op is judged on **`posting::nose::posted_path`**, the exact stream the post gets: the control point for the nose-centre turning ops, and the cache for the others.
  - **X** is the signed offset from the axis on the path's meridian, read as `fanuc-lathe.cps` `radiusOf` reads it, with the same 0.0005 tolerance. Past centre is negative and meets the floor.
  - **Z** is relative to the origin.
  - **Arcs** about the spindle axis are judged on their radius, with arc quarter points included.
  - **Any point off every meridian** is judged three ways: on signed world X, on its radius, and on Y against any Y band. No single reading can clear it.
  - **Refusal wording** is unchanged: "<op>: move i reaches v in X, the stroke is lo..hi".
  - **When the post refuses the orientation**, the check falls back to the nose-centre cache, so the op is still judged.
- **`machine/mod.rs` (+9 lines):** calls the lathe judge first and skips the world-X block for lathe machines. Mill and mill-turn checks are unchanged.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/647-lathe-stroke-radius.md`.

## How tested (`lathe_stroke`, now 10 tests)
- **New:**
  - `a_facing_control_point_below_the_x_floor_is_refused_by_name`: with the floor at -0.5, Face1 on the Y meridian is refused with "reaches -0.800 in X". It fails without the fix.
  - `a_turning_pass_beyond_the_x_ceiling_is_refused_by_name`: X max 9 on an r10 bar refuses Rough1. It fails without the fix.
  - `a_facing_control_point_on_the_x_floor_passes`: a guard at the band edge.
  - Unit test: `machine::lathe_stroke::tests::the_meridian_radius_is_read_signed`.
- **Updated:** `a_clearance_past_the_lathe_carriage_still_refuses_by_name` now expects Rough1 at Z 634.200, the control point (r 0.8 below the nose centre), not 635.000. Mill-turn still expects 635.000.
- **Gate:** conformance, golden_cl, every lathe_* and turning_* suite (including thread), machine, machine_edit, machine_library, posting and tormach_machines pass. Clippy is clean.

## Interactions
- **#643 (#631):** `mod.rs` merges cleanly. After both merge, lathe machines are judged here first, so #643's `spindle_arc` branch goes unused on lathes; a follow-up can remove it.
- **#643 vs #640:** separately from this PR, #643's `lathe_thread_travel` fixture states `"min": 0.0`, and #640 moves the built-in floor to -2.5. Whichever merges second updates that string.
- **#644:** its converted groove and part paths are judged automatically, through the same `posted_path`.

Changelog: On a lathe, the machine travel check now judges the posted radius — the control point, on the path's own meridian, signed past centre — so a turning or facing over-travel in X is refused by name instead of passing unseen (#647)

Fixes #647

title: refactor(sim): a carried field clips to the next setup's block by intersection
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #649** (#637 step B), which is stacked on #646 (step A). Merge them in that order. This is **#637 step C**, the clip from the design comment on #637.

`CarriedField` gains an optional **clip block** in the new frame.
- **The law:** the carried solid is **intersected** with the later setup's own stock block, `distance = max(d_body, d_block)`, and membership is body **and** block. That's the field's form of the column body's `lower()` clip in `stock_sim_carry`.
- **A second clip** narrows the block; it never widens it.
- **Carrying again** (`then`) carries the clip through the same turn.
- **New `box_signed(lo, hi, p)`:** the exact signed distance to an axis-aligned box (negative inside), re-exported from `stock_sim`.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing uses it yet. That's step D, the `Body` enum and its agreement lane.

It merges step B's review fix: the 3×3×3 near-tool floor refusal.

title: refactor(sim): a field column's floor reads exactly from the shell, or is refused
body:
## What changed

**Stacked on #646** (#637 step A). Merge #646 first. This is **#637 step B**, option 2 from the design comment on #637.

**New `SdfField::floor_at(x, y) -> FloorRead`** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_floor.rs`) reads the **lowest face of the stock under a column**.
- **How:** straight from the shell's own lowest crossing on that column. That's a mesh plane, so it's **exact**.
- **Why:** it's the column body's commonest re-clamp, a part flipped onto a face an earlier setup left uncut.
- **What it refuses:** a column whose floor a cut actually removed (a claim > 0 at or next to the floor cell) gets **`FloorRead::CutFromBelow`**, by name. The down-march's exactness rests on `cut_ups`, and no upward companion exists yet, so no bracketed guess is given. A `cut_downs` companion (option 1) can lift this later.
- **Other results:** `NoMaterial` for a column beside the stock, `Unreadable` for an `Open` parity column.
- **Not yet wired:** nothing uses it yet. It's for steps C–D.

**Also folded in, from the review of #646:** the `unapply` doc now says the round trip is exact **to rounding** (exactly for integer shifts, within an ulp of a fractional one), not "bit for bit".

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_floor.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `an_uncut_floor_reads_the_shell_exactly`: a plate's floor is −6.0 exactly. A shallow top slot leaves it −6.0, since a band reaching down isn't a cut floor. Beside the stock reads `NoMaterial`.
  - `a_floor_a_cut_reached_is_refused_by_name`: a slot cut through the plate gives `CutFromBelow` over the slot, and the floor beside it is still exactly −6.0.

title: fix(turning): facing approaches at rapid and lifts off the face before retracting
body:
**Stacked on #640** (#630, control-point posting, which changes the facing output). Review only this PR's own commit, `39ceb9c2`. The merge `c18542f9` brings in #640's latest tip.

**P2 (#632):** lathe facing had two problems.
1. Its first move after the tool call was a **feed** from wherever the turret was parked.
2. Every pass rapided straight out in X at the Z just cut, **dragging the nose across the fresh face**.

## What changed (`crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs`)
- **Approach:** the path starts on the axis at the clearance plane, the mill kernels' convention. Its first move is a **rapid to the clearance point (rho_clear, clearance)**, then the existing plunge feed.
  - Posted, the first motion after the tool call is `G00 X13 Z25`.
  - The meridian rapid law (#103) judges this rapid. rho_clear sits outside the stock radius, and a clearance plane inside the bar is refused (`RapidInStock`) and not posted.
- **Retract:** every pass lifts **`LIFT` = 0.2 mm (capped at half the stepdown)** up the axis, then rapids out in X at the lifted Z.
  - The cap keeps the lift inside air the pass above already cleared.
- **Profile Rough:** checked and unchanged. It already starts with a G0, and each rung exits radially outward at the top of its window, away from the finished diameter. This is recorded in the decision file.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/632-facing-approach.md`.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/facing.nc`)
- `G00 X13 Z25` is added before the first plunge.
- Each retract `G00 X13 Z<s>` becomes `G00 X-1.6 Z<s+0.2>` then `G00 X13 Z<s+0.2>`.
- The header's existing envelope-warning move index shifts by one. That fixture faces the part's own end by design, the same as on main.

## How tested
- **motion `turning_face`:**
  - `the_first_move_is_a_rapid_to_the_clearance_point`;
  - `every_pass_lifts_off_its_face_before_it_rapids_out` (3 stepdown/nose combinations, and no rapid slides along a cut face);

  - `a_clearance_plane_inside_the_bar_is_convicted_not_posted`.

title: refactor(sim): a field carried between setups is the same field seen through the turn
body:
## What changed

**#637 step A** (M7.3, the carried stock on the field engine). The design is in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637 (research comment).

- **Not yet wired:** nothing in `carry::Body` or the app uses it. That's steps B–D (B's design finding is posted on #637). So this PR is behaviour-neutral, new API plus tests.

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_carry.rs`, 3/3:**

- **Blades reuse #630's `orientation`,** read on the LinuxCNC chart. There is no new field or file key, and the same editor row and undoable `ChangeTool` apply.
  - **1**: the right corner (+Z).
  - **2**: the left corner (−Z). This is the **default**, from LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §4.2's parting example, a blade touched off on its left side.
  - **6**: the width centre, the old behaviour. **9** is read as 6.
- **Conversion:** `posting_nose.rs` shifts GrooveRough, GrooveFinish and Part paths by (0, ±w/2) through #640's rigid `control_point_path`.
  - X does not move: the CL radius is already the tip line.
  - There is no corner-radius term: a rounded corner's imaginary tip is the sharp corner.
- **Refused by name:** codes 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 (ID or face), and a blade with no usable width.
- **Unchanged:** the cache, verifier, stock sim and gouge laws keep the true blade. The parting plane still means the kerf centre.
- **Editor:** a Groove tool's row reads "Touched-off corner" and offers only 1, 2 and 6. The tool note prints `ORIENTATION q`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/641-blade-corner.md`.

**Behaviour change for existing programs:** the left-corner default moves every grooving and parting program by −w/2 in Z. A shop that touched off on the width centre sets its blades to 6.

## Golden diff (`fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`)
- **2 mm groove:** Z-5.8/-4.6 → **Z-6.8/-5.6**, the left corners at the walls.
- **3 mm part-off:** Z-10 → **Z-11.5**.
- Clearances move by the same amount; X is unchanged.

## How tested
- **New `lathe_blade_corner` (4 tests, each fails before the fix):**
  - a 3 mm groove at Z-10 posts Z-11.5, Z-8.5 or Z-10 for orientation 2, 1 or 6, and the cache stays at Z-10;
  - a part-off at Z-20 leaves the part's back face at Z-18.5 for every setting (before the fix, a left-corner blade left 17 mm);
  - ID and face codes are refused by name;
  - undo and redo.
- **Units and round-trip:** a tools unit for the blade chart, and `project_roundtrip::a_blade_corner_round_trips_and_old_blades_take_the_left_corner`.
- **Regressions, all green:** lathe_nose_tip, lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, turning, turning_blade, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, the tool suites, tools lib, and the ui orientation row. Clippy is clean.

**Not exercised:** a Hub run, which comes with the lathe kit after #626.

title: fix(app): a lathe thread's spindle arcs are judged by radius in the travel check
body:
## What changed

#631: the built-in Lathe (`lathe.mch`, X 0..320) refused **every thread**, with "move 2 reaches -5.600 in X, the stroke is 0.000..320.000".

**Cause:** a thread pass is a chain of arcs **about the spindle axis**. Their far side, and the travel check's added quarter points, read negative X. That's the CL's antipode: the spindle turning the work, never a slide position. The machine check judged that raw signed X.

**Fix** (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`, the travel law in `check_ops`): on a machine of kind lathe, an XY arc **centred on the spindle axis** is judged in X by its **radius** at each extreme. Every other move keeps its signed X, so a real past-centre move is still judged against the band.

**Not changed:** the band itself. `lathe_stroke::lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band` records that a lathe's X is a one-sided centreline band. Whether a nose-radius face to centre (#630 / PR #640, which ends at X -r) should widen it is #640's call, not this PR's.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/631-lathe-spindle-arc-travel.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/lathe_thread_travel.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `a_thread_passes_the_built_in_lathe`: **fails without the fix**, with the issue's exact message ("move 2 reaches -5.600 in X…").
  - `a_real_over_travel_on_a_lathe_is_still_refused`: the same thread against an X stroke of 0..2 mm is refused "… in X".
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the app suites pass.
- **Named:**

  |---|---|
  | machine | 32 |
  | machine_library | 11 |
  | turning_thread | 8 |

A Hub run on a lathe. The PathPilot lathe post is #626.

**Stacked on #595** (issue #585, the `Columns` seam). Merge #595 first. This is M7.3 step 3/6 (#26), **in part**.

title: fix(turning): lathe posts write the tool's control point for its orientation, not the nose centre
body:
**P0 (#630):** lathe posts wrote the insert's **nose-centre** path under G40. With normal touch-off, the controlled point is the imaginary tip (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information §7.1), so turned diameters came out **2r oversize** and faces **r long**. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot's conversational posts the orientation's control point with G40, and refuses a tool whose orientation can't make the cut. That sample is used as behaviour reference only.

## What changed
- **Tool orientation** (LinuxCNC 1-9 chart: Lathe User Information §3 figure, §7.1, §4.1):
  - `Tool.orientation: Option<u8>`. Turning inserts default to **2** (OD, cutting toward the chuck), boring bars to **3**.
  - Editable in the tool editor, which shows the default, through the undoable `ChangeTool`.
  - The project key is written only when set, so old files load with the default. 1-9 is enforced at command creation and at file read.
  - Fanuc's tip chart is different, and no post writes either number, so only the LinuxCNC chart is modelled.
- **One shared conversion,** `crates/post/src/post/nose_tip.rs::control_point_path`, called once from `posting::op_streams` (`posting_nose.rs`), not per .cps:
  - Every move, rapids and arc centres included, shifts by r·(ox, oz) for the orientation.
  - This is exact on diameters, faces, tapers and arcs: the cutting path is already the profile offset by r, and the insert is rigid.
  - Refused by name: a path on two meridians or off every meridian, a C angle, an off-plane arc, and paths carrying cycle, thread, compensation or probe records.
  - Converted ops: facing, profile rough/finish, chamfer, taper, multi-pass, boring. Grooving, parting, threading, form and drilling post as before.
- **The cache stays the nose centre.** The verifier, stock sim, gouge laws and CL goldens are unchanged. Orientation is not part of the op stamp, so editing it never stales an op.
- **Orientation fit, refused by name at post:** a corner tip reaches within 45° of its direction, an axis tip within 90°, and 9 fits anything.
  - Facing needs −Z and −X (2, 6, 7 fit), OD turning −X, boring +X.
  - A cut needing −X and +Z gives exactly [1, 5, 6], matching PathPilot's own refusal.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:** the header states the control-point rule (G40). The tool note adds `ORIENTATION q` from a new commentary parameter `PARAM ToolOrientation`, documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/630-nose-tip.md`.

## Golden diffs (Fanuc Lathe; r = 0.8, orientation 2)
- **`facing.nc`:** every changed line shifts X −1.6 (diameter) and Z −0.8. The last pass now posts the facing plane (Z14, was Z14.8).
  - Passes end at **X-1.6**: the nose centre still reaches the axis, so the control point stands r past centre. This is a normal facing overtravel, but a machine with a 0 X limit would need #631.
- **`profile_rough_finish.nc`:** shifts by X −1.6 / Z −0.8. The Ø12 flange posts **X12** (was X13.6), the shoulder Z2 (was Z2.8), and the Ø7 neck X7 (was X8.6). Three points differ by 0.001 from a pure shift because of 1 µm grid rounding.
- **Unchanged:** groove/part, axial drill, thread G76 and C-axis goldens. In `lathe_post.rs`, the facing assertion now expects `X-1.6 Z14` and `ORIENTATION 2`.

## How tested
- **`nose_tip` units (7):**
  - the OD finish posts the finished diameter, and a face posts Z0;
  - every orientation's offset;
  - a 30° taper is exact;
  - arcs keep their radius and move their centre;
  - the X-meridian case;
  - refusals;
  - orientation 9 is identity.
- **`orientation` units (3),** including PathPilot's [1, 5, 6].
- **App `lathe_nose_tip` (6):**
  - a Ø19.05 neck posts X19.05 and the shoulder Z0, while the cache stays nose-centre;
  - facing reaches the axis;
  - every fitting orientation equals cache + r·offset, and editing never stales the op;
  - mismatched orientations are refused;
  - ChangeTool undo/redo, and code 10 is refused;
  - a boring bar defaults to 3.
- **Round-trip and UI:** `project_roundtrip::a_lathe_orientation_round_trips_and_old_tools_take_the_default`, and the UI orientation row.
- **Gate:**
  - the non-thread turning and lathe suites, `lathe_post_g76`, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip and commands_undo;
  - the tool suites, c_axis_live, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, inverted_post and coolant_followups;
  - camcraft-post and camcraft-tools.
  - Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups
- **Grooving and parting blades:** they post the centre of the blade's width, but a blade is touched off on a corner (LinuxCNC §4.2), so a width/2 Z offset is likely owed. Filed separately.
- **Refusal rule:** checking the leading direction would need insert lead angles, which the tool library doesn't model.
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** consumes the converted stream once merged; its goldens need regenerating.
- **#639 (#629):** may hit small conflicts in test `Tool` literals.

Changelog: Lathe posts write the turning tool's control point for its orientation (LinuxCNC 1-9, editable per tool; default 2 for turning inserts, 3 for boring bars) instead of the nose-centre path: a Ø19.05 finish now posts X19.05 and a face at Z0 posts Z0; an orientation that cannot cut the operation is refused by name (#630)

Fixes #630

title: fix(turning): threads cut right-hand toward the chuck by default; the hand is stated, never dropped
body:
**P0 (#629):** every lathe thread was cut **left-hand**. The engine ran every pass toward +Z (away from the chuck), and the Fanuc Lathe post wrote `M03` and dropped the CL's arc sense. Confirmed against the control vendor's own behaviour: PathPilot Hub 8L conversational right-hand OD G76 runs toward −Z under M3. That sample is cited as behaviour confirmation only.

## What changed
- **Hand rule:** `cl::ThreadHand` (Right by default, or Left). A helix is RH if it turns ccw (seen from +Z) while rising, or cw while falling. With the free end at +Z, M03 means the tool goes cw around the part, so a cw half-turn needs M03 and a ccw one M04.
- **Engine (`turning/thread.rs`):** every pass starts at the top and **descends toward the chuck**. Arc sense = `hand.ccw_for(true)`, and the infeed schedule is unchanged.
- **Record and stream:**
  - `ThreadCycle.hand`; `is_sane` requires every half-turn to wind that hand.
  - The `THREAD … HAND right|left` word is required.
  - `PARAM SpindleDirection "reverse"` is emitted when M04 is needed.
  - New manifest flag `threadHands`: a script without it is refused a reverse section by name. Documented in CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps:**
  - writes M03, or M04 (with an operator note) when the stream asks for reverse;
  - checks **every G32 half-turn** against the spindle it wrote and refuses a mismatch ("would cut the other hand");
  - G76 refuses a record with no hand, or one whose hand and Z direction need the other spindle.
- **Verdict:** `thread_hand_warnings` raises a Gouge at the first wrong-hand half-turn, so the gate blocks.
- **App:**
  - `OpParams::Threading { hand }` (Right).
  - The project file always writes `hand`; an old file loads as Right.
  - The cache stamp includes the hand, so every old threading cache goes Stale once and regenerates toward the chuck.
  - MCP picks it up through the params DTO.
  - UI: a "Hand" row on the Passes tab, undoable.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/629-thread-hand.md` (no project version bump: reasoning inside; the feed-away-from-chuck option is left for a follow-up).

**Golden diff** (`fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`): `G00 X12.1 Z8` → `Z14`, and `G76 X9.6 Z14 …` → `Z8 …`. The cycle now starts at the top and feeds toward the chuck under M03.

## How tested
- **New tests (each fails on the old code):**
  - motion: `every_pass_runs_toward_the_chuck_and_the_helix_winds_the_asked_hand` and `the_hand_of_a_turn_is_the_screw_law`;
  - app `lathe_post_g76`: `a_right_hand_thread_posts_toward_the_chuck_under_m03` (18 G32 blocks descending, G76 Z14→Z8), `a_left_hand_thread_posts_toward_the_chuck_under_m04` and `the_hand_is_never_dropped`;
  - `lathe_post_refusals`: ccw falling under M03 is refused;
  - `turning_thread`: hand edit undo/redo;
  - `project_roundtrip`: an old file loads as Right, Left survives, and an invalid word is refused;
  - ui: the hand row.
- **Gate:** motion, post, cl and the app lathe, turning, inverted, conformance, golden_cl, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo and mcp suites pass. Clippy is clean on 5 crates.

## Follow-ups and merge notes
- **#626 (PathPilot lathe post):** must declare `threadHands`, read `PARAM SpindleDirection`, check half-turn sense, and take the G76 direction from Z→EndZ.
- **Threading stack (#516-#518, #468):** must carry `hand` and keep the descending passes and arc sense.

Changelog: Lathe threads cut right-hand toward the chuck under M03 by default; Threading gains a Hand (Right/Left, LH posts M04), the thread record and stream state the hand, and the Fanuc Lathe post refuses any pass or G76 whose hand disagrees with its spindle (#629)

Fixes #629

title: fix(#622): view-cube pole clicks keep the roll, snapped to the nearest quarter turn
body:
Clicking TOP/BOT on the view cube threw the roll away. A face click commands `Camera::toward(face normal)`; at a Z pole the normalized direction is exactly `[0, 0, +-1]`, so `toward` read `yaw = atan2(0, 0) = 0` and `basis_right`'s zero-guard returned literal world `+X` whatever the yaw - every pole click landed on one canonical orientation and the model spun up to 180 degrees on screen (#622 repro: orbit near-overhead at yaw ~90 deg, click TOP, the part rotates half a turn).

## The change

`Camera::toward` (`viewport.rs`) grows one clause: when the normalized direction is exactly a Z pole (`n[2].abs() == 1.0`), the yaw is the *pre-click* camera's yaw snapped to the nearest quarter turn, `(yaw / FRAC_PI_2).round() * FRAC_PI_2`, instead of the vanishing atan2. `basis_right`'s pole guard evaluates that yaw - `(-yaw.sin(), yaw.cos(), 0.0)` - which is the same expression the guard already produces for every non-pole view, extended to the one point where `cross(forward, +Z)` underflows `normalize`'s EPSILON floor (`cos(pi/2)^2 ~ 3.7e-33`).

Result: a near-pole click turns the screen frame at most 45 degrees from the up it had (the snap's own bound); screen up/right still ride world axes at the pole (the surviving half of the old law); views sharing a quarter turn roll alike; and a second click at the same pole is exact idempotence - the reported double-click twitch cannot happen. Non-pole directions (edges, corners, `oriented`, orbit) are untouched. Rationale in `docs/decisions/622-viewcube-roll-snap.md`.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::pole_views_hold_a_stable_roll` - re-pinned from "screen right is +X at both poles for arbitrary yaws" to the quarter-turn law: right `(-sin y_s, cos y_s, 0)`, up `(-cos y_s, -sin y_s, 0)` at TOP / `(cos y_s, sin y_s, 0)` at BOT.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::toward_turns_the_eye_without_moving_it` - new cases: start yaw 2.0 -> TOP lands `pi/2`; start yaw -2.3 -> BOT lands `-pi/2`.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::a_pole_click_keeps_the_roll_the_view_had` - near-pole view (yaw 1.0, pitch 1.5), TOP click lands the on-screen up within 45 degrees of the pre-click up. On main the swing is ~147 degrees.
- `law_tests::view_cube_tests::a_second_pole_click_lands_the_same_view` - the reported double-click: the second `toward([0,0,1])` changes nothing (passes before and after; it pins the property the issue asked for).

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib view_cube_tests` runs 3 failed / 4 passed, exactly the predicted law breaks - `a pole click keeps the pre-click yaw's quarter turn: 0` (`[-0.5389488413540798, -0.8393630887186533, 0.07073720166770292] -> [-0.0, 1.0, 0.0]`), and `screen right at the [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] pole: [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib view_cube_tests` - 7 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 379 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). One earlier run failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness.
- The `egui_app` view-cube gesture tests (face click orients, arms nothing) pass untouched.
- Not exercised: the full app suite beyond the two crates, and the on-screen cube itself - the law is pinned instead.

Changelog: view-cube TOP/BOT clicks now land the pole view at the nearest quarter-turn roll instead of spinning the model to canonical +X (#622)

Fixes #622

title: perf(sim): a field block stock builds in closed form, not by band fill
body:
## What changed

#633: the field stock engine was about 300× slower than the column engine on a large box (found in PR #625's review). This blocked #589, the column engine's retirement.

**Profile** (release, `drill_plate.cl` on a 120 mm box at the CLI's 0.375 mm auto cell, 320 × 320):

| Phase | Column | Field, before | **Field, after** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build the block | 27 µs | **58 s** | **42 µs** |
| Cut (9 moves) | 23 µs | 3.4 ms | 2.6 ms |
| Read every column | 0.2 ms | 66 ms | 53 ms |
| Cut cells | 399 | 399 | **399** |

- **Cause:** it was not the cutting (the M7.3 per-brick law, #584, holds). `block_field` meshes the floorless block **ten spans deep**, and `SdfField::from_mesh`'s BFS band-filled every cell along those 1.2 m walls.
- **Fix:** a new `field_box::AnalyticBox`, the closed-form signed distance of an axis-aligned box.
  - `SdfField::from_box` builds the block's shell, which is a handful of facets and still answers parity and bounds, and **stores no bricks**.
  - `mag_at`, the single reader of the mesh layer, answers unstored cells from the box, clamped to `cap` by the existing band law.
  - The cut layers and every other reader are unchanged. Cylinder and model stocks still band-fill, bounded by their real size.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/633-field-block-closed-form.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/sim/tests/field_block_cost.rs`, 3/3:**
  - `a_block_stores_no_band_at_build`: the 58 s case stores 0 bricks.
  - `the_closed_form_reads_the_stock_the_band_fill_read`: across a lattice around a block, same sign everywhere and agreement within 2 cells with the band-filled field.
  - `a_large_field_block_runs_a_drill_program_quickly`: heavy lane, release, a 120 mm block plus 4 plunges under 2 s.
- **Heavy release lanes**, run to confirm verdicts are unchanged:
  - `stock_engine_agreement`: 3/3, **0 findings**, every `max |delta|` 0.
  - `stock_backend_parity`: 13/13.
  - `stock_field_cost`: total **7.6 s (was 83.9 s)**. Build is 0.00 s on every golden program, at 0.19-10.9 ms/move.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** the sim suites pass. Named: stock_columns 3, stock_preview 10, stock_bull_nose 7, wall_slack 5, headless_bin 3, and app stock_sim_document 9, stock_view 4, stock_play 7, setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8.
- **Clippy** on sim and app with `-D warnings`: clean. No golden changed.

## Not exercised

Cylinder and model-stock build cost. Those still band-fill; a closed-form cylinder can follow if profiling shows a need.

Changelog: The field stock engine builds a block stock in microseconds instead of up to a minute (closed-form box distance) (#633)

Fixes #633

title: feat(post): per-operation smoothing, opt-in, in every mill dialect
body:
## What changed

Requested by @spikeypineapple on #616. Smoothing differs per control, and the "auto" behaviour is maximum accuracy on finishing, with roughing aggressiveness following the stock left. The design was posted on the issue before code.

- **The option:** **"Smoothing per operation"**, a new document post option (`PostOptions.smoothing`), **off by default**.
  - **Off:** no smoothing PARAM is in the stream, so every program, and the `postOptions` object, is **byte-identical**.
  - **Saving:** the additive `smoothing` project key, absent when off. Undoable through `SetPostOptions`, and offered as a checkbox under the post picker for every mill post.
- **On, each operation states its ask** (`app::smoothing::of`) as `PARAM Smoothing <mm>` + `PARAM SmoothingMode finish|rough`:
  - **finish:** an op with a contour tolerance and no stock left asks **half** its tolerance (the control's deviation stacks on the verified path);
  - **rough:** an op leaving stock asks **stock × 0.2, capped at 0.25 mm, never more than that fifth** (no floor);
  - **nothing:** drilling, tapping, probing, threading, facing and the lathe kinds ask nothing.
- **Each mill post writes its control's words** after the section preamble and **undoes them at the section end**, so no tolerance leaks:

  | Post | On | Off |
  |---|---|---|
  | Tormach / LinuxCNC | `G64 P<tol>` | the header's `G64 P0.001` / `P0.025` |
  | Fanuc | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - G5.1 STATES NO TOLERANCE" (G5.1 has no tolerance word; review of #635) | none |
  | Haas | `G187 P3\|P1 E<tol>` | `G187` |
  | Siemens 840D | `CYCLE832(<tol>,_FINISH\|_ROUGH,1)` | `CYCLE832()` |
  | Heidenhain (ISO) | `G62 T<tol>` | `G62` |
  | Mazak | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - NO MAZAK FORM STATED" (no guessed word) | none |

- **Fanuc writes nothing yet:** `G5.1 Q1` states no tolerance, so it can't be held to the op's ask. A bounded form can follow with #614's Doosan sample. Decision record: `docs/decisions/616-smoothing.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/smoothing.rs`, 4/4:**
  - `off_is_byte_identical_and_writes_no_smoothing_word`: every mill post.
  - `each_dialect_writes_its_words_and_undoes_them_at_the_section_end`: finish and rough per dialect; the words are stated before the first cut and reset after.
  - `mazak_names_the_ask_once_and_writes_no_guessed_word`
  - `finish_ops_ask_their_tolerance_and_rough_ops_ask_from_their_stock`: including the clamp ends and drill → none.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** post and app suites pass after the follow-up commit. The first run caught `lathe_post_g76` pinning the whole `postOptions` object; the key is now omitted when off. The only ui reds are the 3 known GPU-adapter tests (#615 / #623).
- **Named, all with the option off:**

  | Suite | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | conformance | 6 |
  | golden_cl | 23 |
  | posting | 17 |
  | tormach_post | 10 |
  | fanuc_post | 11 |
  | heidenhain_block_form | 4 |
  | sinumerik_safe_retract | 3 |
  | coolant | 7 |
  | after_op | 10 |
  | project_roundtrip | 69 |
  | per_op_files | 9 |
  | lathe_post_g76 | 5 |
  | ui structural / post_options / after_op | 5 |

- **Clippy** on post, app and ui with `-D warnings`: clean. **No golden or snapshot changed.**

## Not exercised

A run on a real control or simulator with smoothing on. PathPilot Hub can check the Tormach `G64 P` per section. The Haas `G187`, Siemens `CYCLE832` and Heidenhain `G62` words come from public documentation and haven't been run on a control. That's why the option is opt-in.

Changelog: An opt-in "Smoothing per operation" post option writes each control's smoothing mode per operation (finish tolerance or a roughing deviation from the stock left): G64 P, G5.1, G187, CYCLE832, G62 (#616)

Fixes #616

title: feat(machines): Tormach 24R and xsTECH Pro router machine files
body:
Machine files for Tormach's three routers (#620): the **24R**, the **xsTECH Pro** and the plain **xsTECH**.

## Sources (cited in `docs/decisions/620-tormach-routers.md`)
- **24R:** Tormach UM10564 0826A §2.2, Machine Specifications.
- **xsTECH Pro:** the xsTECH Pro spec sheet (2026) and UM10859 (xsTECH Pro CE manual) §2.

## What changed
- **`assets/machines/tormach-24r.mch`:**
  - X 24.75 / Y 55.75 / Z 6.7 in;
  - 1.5 kW electrospindle, **10000-24000 rpm**;
  - 200 IPM on every axis;
  - ATC left unstated (optional, no station count given).
- **`assets/machines/tormach-xstech-pro.mch`:**
  - X 10.2 (with the standard tool changer);
  - **Y 7.9** (the CE manual) over the US sheet's 9.3, and Z 6.3 over the CE manual's 6.5. Where the documents disagree, the smaller travel is used, since it can only refuse a move, never let a bad one through;
  - 0.35 kW, max 20000 rpm with no minimum stated;
  - a 4-station ATC (T5 and up is refused);
  - **no feed ceiling stated**, because none is documented.
- **Both machines:**
  - rigid tapping false (not documented), so a tapping cycle is refused by name;
  - no coolant (none documented), so a Flood op is refused by name;
  - safe retract Z0, the Tormach convention.
- **Registration:** added to `MACHINES`. Both get the Tormach PathPilot mill post, as the Tormach mills do.

## How tested
- **New `tormach_routers` (4):**
  - the documents' figures;
  - the xsTECH Pro states no feed ceiling;
  - both post through PathPilot (S18000, G20, no warnings);
  - a **5000 rpm job is refused on the 24R** ("below the machine's 10000"), and the same job at 18000 posts.
- **Gate:** machine 32, machine_library, tormach_machines, tormach_safe_retract, tormach_post, posting and conformance pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised
A PathPilot Hub run of a profile on a router.

## The plain xsTECH Router (commit e1ff076d)
Tormach told the contributor that no separate manual was made for it (its documentation lives in the knowledge base). Its figures therefore come from Tormach's published spec sheet, product pages and knowledge base, each cited with its URL and retrieval date in the decision file.
- **Travel:** X 8.6 / Y 6.3 / Z 2.4 in. All sources agree.
- **Spindle:** 5000-15000 rpm, 0.08 kW, direct drive. The sources disagree (80-125 W, 3000/5000 to 15000/20000 rpm), so the narrowest window and the smallest motor are used: a refusal limit that is too narrow can only refuse a job, never pass a bad one. A 15-20k rpm job on a newer unit is refused by name, and the decision file says how to widen it.
- **Feed:** 120 IPM on every axis, as both feed and rapid. **Tool change:** manual ER11 collet, no ATC.
- **Rigid tapping and coolant:** not documented, so both are refused by name.
- **Left unstated:** a separate rapid rate, tool length and diameter limits, and 4th-axis figures.

**Tests:** `tormach_routers` 5 pass. The xsTECH spec row is new. The PathPilot posting test now covers all three routers (12000 rpm). `the_xstech_spindle_window_is_the_narrowest_stated` checks that 18000 and 4000 rpm are refused and 12000 passes. tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, conformance, tormach_safe_retract and tormach_post pass, and clippy is clean.

**Not exercised:** a Hub run of a router profile.

Changelog: Tormach 24R, xsTECH Pro and xsTECH router machine files (PathPilot post; spindle windows, travels and tool changers from Tormach's published figures, undocumented capabilities refused by name) (#620)

Fixes #620

title: fix(ui): GPU tests fall back to the hardware adapter and say when they skip
body:
## What changed
Every GPU test, and the real `--headless` run, requested `force_fallback_adapter: true`, a software adapter. Metal has none. So on every Mac:
- `gpu_render`, `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` silently skipped and reported **pass**;
- `headless_run_succeeds` and the two headless CLI tests **failed** with "No suitable graphics adapter found".

New `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`:
- **`device()`:** tries the software adapter first (deterministic CI on Linux/Windows), then the default hardware adapter. It returns the device, queue, which kind it got and the adapter's name and backend. If both fail, the error names both reasons.
- **`device_for_test(suite)`:** prints the adapter it renders on. With no adapter it prints a loud `*** <suite>: SKIPPED (no adapter) - NOT a pass ***`, and `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns that into a failure.
- **Headless app path:** `headless::run` (shell.rs) now uses the helper, so the CLI tests are fixed through the app path itself.
- **Not an `#[ignore]` lane:** that would drop these ~1 s suites from quick and batch everywhere. Reasoning in `docs/decisions/615-gpu-adapter.md`.

## How tested (on a real Apple M3 Max, Metal)
| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| gpu_render (9) | 9 silent skips | 9 rendered, pass |
| trace_composite (4) | 4 silent skips | 4 rendered, pass |
| trace_parity (5) | 5 silent skips | 5 rendered, pass |
| `headless_run_succeeds` | FAIL | pass (Metal) |
| the two headless CLI tests | FAIL | pass |

- **Totals:** 0 of 21 before, 21 of 21 after.
- **Stability:** three parallel runs in a row pass, and so does `trace_parity` with `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`.
- **No tolerance changes:** every coverage, parity and depth assertion holds on hardware. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- **Clippy:** clean.
- **Not exercised:** the skip path itself, because this Mac always finds an adapter, and Linux/Windows runs.

Changelog: On macOS the GPU tests and the headless run fall back to the hardware (Metal) adapter, and a GPU test with no adapter prints a loud SKIP (CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1 turns it into a failure) (#615)

Fixes #615

title: fix(ui): orthographic view casts parallel rays for the traced stock and vertex-pick visibility
body:
Two Orthographic-view follow-ups found while fixing #600 (that depth fix is carried by #604). This branch is off main and doesn't depend on #604; its tests check the ray and camera math on the CPU.

## #609: the traced stock casts parallel rays in ortho (`7b9800d1`)
- **`PreviewCamera`** (sim `stock_sim/preview.rs`):
  - a new `ortho_half_height: Option<f64>`;
  - `orthographic(h)`, which refuses a non-finite or non-positive half height by name;
  - `ray(px, py, w, h) -> (origin, dir)`. In ortho, each pixel's ray starts on the eye plane and runs along the view direction, matching `Camera::mvp` and `ray_through`. Perspective is unchanged.
- **Who uses the same rule:** the CPU march, the GPU march (`trace.wgsl`, via the unused `world_lo.w`) and the compositor (`composite.wgsl`, via `frame.z`).
- **Viewport wiring:** `eye_geom::preview_camera` takes the half height from the viewport camera, and the cache key includes it, so switching modes re-traces.

## #610: vertex-pick visibility in ortho (`4d9922b1`)
- `vertex_pick::sight_origin`: perspective starts at the eye as before. Ortho starts at the corner's own point on the eye plane, so the test runs back along the view direction, as `ray_through` does.
- A corner at or behind the eye plane is not offered.

## How tested
- **sim `stock_preview::an_orthographic_eye_casts_parallel_rays_from_its_view_plane`:** parallel rays from the eye plane, the box top at one depth, misses off the footprint, perspective unchanged, and a bad half height refused.
- **ui `trace::eye_geom::tests::the_traced_stock_lands_on_the_mesh_pixel_in_both_projections`:** all 8 corners of a stock box, projected through `Camera::mvp`, lie on their pixel's traced ray in both projections. With the fix reverted, a corner misses by 2.81 against a pixel width of 0.80.
- **ui `vertex_pick_tests::orthographic_visibility_runs_along_the_view_direction_not_to_the_eye`:** an occluder on the parallel ray hides a corner, and an occluder only on the line to the eye doesn't. The old test got both backwards.
- **Gate:** ui lib 378, stock_preview 11, gpu_render, trace_composite and trace_parity pass. Clippy is clean (ui, sim, app).
- **Shaders:** both pass naga 30.0.1's parser and validator. **This machine has no wgpu adapter, so the GPU and compositor paths weren't exercised; a review on a machine with an adapter should run gpu_render, trace_composite and trace_parity.**

Changelog: Orthographic view: the traced stock sim view now casts parallel rays, so it lines up with the ortho-drawn part, meshes and toolpaths (#609)
Changelog: Orthographic view: vertex picking tests visibility along the parallel view direction, so a hidden corner is no longer offered and a visible one is no longer refused (#610)

Fixes #609

title: test(ui): structural tests no longer race on the live theme table
body:
## What changed
`structural::shell_structure_light` and `shell_structure_dark` failed intermittently in parallel ui runs (#605).
- **Cause:** the live theme table `theme::LIVE` (read through `theme::current()`) is one per process. The structural and snapshot tests already serialise on `snapshot_guard()`, but `tests/theme_door.rs::the_theme_door_switches_the_theme_and_undo_restores_it` drives the real light → undo → redo → undo frame-edge sync without that lock, so it flips the shared table in the middle of a structural test.
  - A flip to dark breaks `shell_structure_light` ("frame-edge sync rode the world's reference").
  - A flip to light breaks `_dark`.
- **Fix (tests only):** the theme-door switch test takes `snapshot_guard()`, and the `SNAPSHOT_LOCK` doc says any test whose frames move the world's theme must take it too.
- **Why not per-harness:** the table is process-wide by design, read at ~44 sites with no `State` to hand. Making it per-harness would be a large production change for a race that exists only in tests.

## How tested
- **Before:** 30 parallel runs of `egui_app::tests::` gave 5/30 failures, all `shell_structure_light`. With the theme-door test skipped, 0/30, which confirmed the cause.
- **After:** 0/30 on those runs, and 20 full parallel `camcraft-ui --lib` runs gave 0 structural or other failures. The headless-GPU test fails only on this machine.
- Clippy is clean.

Changelog: none (test-only)

Fixes #605

title: fix(ui): orthographic depth maps into WebGPU's clip volume, not OpenGL's
body:
The ortho branch of `Camera::mvp` mapped depth the way OpenGL's `glOrtho` does - NDC z over [-1, +1]. WebGPU's clip volume wants `0 <= z <= w`, and the ortho matrix holds `clip.w == 1` (the #434 law tests pin that), so every point nearer than `(near + far) / 2` was clipped away before rasterization. With `far = 40 * dist`, that cut plane sits twenty times the orbit distance out: everything in view, so clicking **Orthographic** blanked the viewport.

Perspective carries the same OpenGL-style z row but `clip.w` is the eye distance there, which keeps clip z positive beyond ~0.2 mm - far closer than the camera can orbit - so perspective was unaffected.

## The change

The ortho z row (`viewport.rs`, the `[col][row]` proj literal) becomes

```rust
[0.0, 0.0, 1.0 / (near - far), 0.0],
[0.0, 0.0, near / (near - far), 1.0],
```

near maps to 0.0, far to 1.0, and ortho depth is now linear. The depth attachment already clears to 1.0 under `CompareFunction::Less`, so no pipeline or shader change is needed. The x/y rows already speak WebGPU and are untouched, as is the perspective branch (its z quirk costs depth precision, not geometry - out of scope here).

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `law_tests::projection_tests::the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` - depth at the near plane, the far plane, and strictly between with monotonic climb. On main: "the near plane sits at -1".
- `gpu_render::orthographic_paints_the_band_perspective_does` - the stock box from `box_stock_paints_steel_over_background` under `test_cam()`, painted in both modes, with the same band bounds and a comparability check (each within 1.5x of the other). On main: 0/65536 pixels.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` builds clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 378 passed, 5 ignored.

title: fix(ui): the setup page's lay-on-plane controls stay on screen, so a picked face is turned flat
body:
**Stacked on #593** (#555), which is on #573 (#557 + #554). It includes their commits until they merge.

## Root cause of the reopened #330
The turn itself was never broken. `pick::lay_on_plane` / `AlignPartToSetup` turn a picked tilted face onto G17/G18/G19 on main, and a new app test pins that. What was broken is what a user could reach on the Setups page. Reproduced through the real shell (1280×720, the block turned 30° about X, real viewport clicks):
1. **Edge snapping (main):** the plane row armed Edge mode (`plane_pick.rs:31`), so a click on the tilted face took an edge, `check_lay` refused it, and Apply stayed grey. **Already fixed by #573** (7d641c8b, #554: the plane row picks faces only).
2. **Controls off screen (main and the stack):** the face row was one long line. In the ~285 px properties pane, **Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply fell past the right edge**, so clicks on them did nothing. The only Apply in reach was the Part alignment row's angle Apply, which turns about the bounds centre. That matches the report's "it only moves the model". Without a reachable Flip, the default also lays the face's outside up, with the part below the plane.

## What changed
- **Face row:** split into short lines: label + "Pick a face"; plane + Flip; "Face to plane level"; the picked face; then **Apply face** on its own line.
- **Other rows:** the three-points row (#555) and the "Axes in the plane" rows (#557) overflowed the same way and got the same treatment.
- **Not used:** `horizontal_wrapped`, which didn't work because other rows widen the pane's content.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/330-face-lay-rotate.md`.
- **Maintainer's call:** the default Flip is unchanged: unflipped means the face's outside points along +axis, so a face picked on G17 lays "outside up". Many users will expect the picked face to become the bottom, so flipping the default may be worth it.
- **Not addressed:** the Part alignment row's angle Apply turning about the bounds centre (the "shifts relative to the origin" part of the report). Follow-up or maintainer's call.

## How tested
- **New UI real-click test:** `plane_face_lay::a_clicked_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_g17_not_only_moved`.
  - It clicks Pick a face → the tilted face in the viewport, asserts Flip, "Face to plane level" and Apply face are on screen, then clicks Flip → Apply face.
  - Result: face normal −Z, face at Z 0, part above. Ctrl+Z restores.
  - It fails on main (an edge is taken) and on the stack without the layout fix (the Apply click misses).
- **Structural:** `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` asserts every option of the face, points and axes rows is inside the window.
- **App:** `plane_align::a_tilted_face_is_turned_flat_onto_each_plane_with_the_part_above_it` covers G17/G18/G19 with undo. It passes on main too, which pins that the command was right.
- **Gate:** plane_align, plane_align_edges, points_align, axis_align, setup_align, winding_align, commands_undo and ui lib 385 pass. The headless-GPU test fails only on this machine. Clippy is clean.

Changelog: Setups page "Lay on a plane": Flip, "Face to plane level" and the row's own "Apply face" stay on screen in the properties pane (they ran off its edge), so a picked tilted face can be laid flat on G17/G18/G19; the three-points and axes rows get the same fix (#330)

Fixes #330

body:
Second slice of #370 (and part of #361): auto-aligning a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems.

## What changed
- `ToolCsysReport::align_tool_body()` extracts the tool axis (from CIP, or CSIF if CIP is absent) and calculates the tip offset (`-dot(origin, axis)`) so that the cutting reference point sits at Z = 0 in the tool frame, pointing up into the spindle along +Z.

- `tool_body_view::load_aligned(&path)` returns `LoadedBody` carrying the auto-alignment result or fallback reason, preserving `load` backwards compatibility.
- In the tool editor (`ToolBodyUi`), importing a STEP file with ISO 13399 coordinate systems automatically sets the axis and tip offset with the note "aligned by ISO 13399 coordinate systems"; importing a file without them or with degenerate/ambiguous coordinate systems falls back to default numeric placement ([0, 0, 1] axis, 0 offset) with a note naming why.

title: feat(post): optionally end a Tormach program in the operator's units
body:
## What changed
After the contributor's mm probe run on a 770MX (#521 / #583), PathPilot stayed in G21. LinuxCNC's `M2`/`M30` reset MDI mode, G54, G17, G90, G94, M48, G40, M5, G1 and M9, but **not the length unit** (LinuxCNC G-code reference, M-codes, "M2, M30 Program End").

A new Tormach post option, **End in**, takes one of three values:
- **Program's unit** (the default, byte-identical output);
- **Inch (G20)**;
- **mm (G21)**.

When the choice differs from the program's unit, `G20`/`G21` is written on its own line after the final `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30` and right before `M30`, so no move is read in the new unit.
- **Setting:** `PostOptions.end_units` (`EndUnits` in schema.rs), set through the existing undoable `SetPostOptions`.
- **Project file:** an optional `post_options.end_units` key; a missing key means the default, so there is no version step. An unknown word refuses the file by name.
- **Post page:** an "End in" row, shown only while Tormach PathPilot is the post.
- **Other posts:** ignore it.
- **Dropped, with reasons in `docs/decisions/596-end-native-units.md`:**
  - a machine-file `native_unit` key, which would need a guess written into every stock file;
  - a closing comment only;
  - an on/off switch.

## How tested
- **New `tormach_end_units` (7):**
  - the default writes no key, and the output is byte-identical;
  - a mm program for an inch control ends `G53 G0 Z0 / G30 / G20 / M30`, and the G20 line is the only difference;
  - an inch program for a mm control ends with G21;
  - matching units add nothing;
  - undo and redo;
  - round-trip, including the unknown-word refusal.
  - The two G20/G21 tests fail with the old .cps.
- **UI:** `after_op_tests::end_units_choice_commits_and_undoes`.
- **Gate:** tormach_post, tormach_machines, conformance (goldens unchanged), posting, program_entry, project_roundtrip, after_op, lathe_post_g76, per_op_files and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy (post/app/ui) is clean.

## Not exercised
A PathPilot Hub run with the option set.

Changelog: Tormach post: new "End in" post option (default off) writes G20/G21 before M30, so a program can leave PathPilot in the operator's units (LinuxCNC's M30 does not reset G20/G21) (#596)

Fixes #596

title: fix(app): a probe-only program's stock sim judges the uncut stock
body:
## What changed

A probe-only program posted with "stock sim did not judge this program: invalid stock simulation setup: stock box and cell must be finite, box non-empty, cell positive". That names the wrong cause; the stock was fine.

**Cause:**
- A touch probe stays out of the program sim's plan, because it removes nothing (#108). In a probe-only program the plan is therefore empty.
- The stock lattice is sized by `min(radius)` over the planned tools, which is +inf over an empty plan.
- The infinite cell was then refused as an invalid setup.

**Fix (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`, `stock_grid`):** when no tool radius is finite, the lattice is sized by the stock's span alone (`auto_cell(0, span)`, the grid ceiling's floor).
- **What the sim does now:** it judges the uncut stock against the part. That reads clean when they agree and rest where they differ, and it cannot report a gouge it never cut.
- **Unchanged:** a missing or invalid stock still refuses by its own name, and `auto_cell` in the sim crate is untouched.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/592-probe-only-sim.md`. It records why I judged the uncut stock rather than skipping the sim with a note.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/probe_only_sim.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `a_probe_only_program_is_judged_not_refused_as_an_invalid_setup`: a 3 × 2 × 1 in part with stock equal to it, and one top-face probe. `verification_report` has no problems and **no not-judged note**. It **fails without the fix**, with the old note present.
  - `a_probe_only_program_without_a_stock_still_says_why`: no stock gives no "invalid setup" text, and any refusal names "no stock".
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`** ran the app suites: 1504 passed, 0 failed.
- **Named:** post_not_judged 4, stock_sim_document 9, setup_carry 9, carried_verify 8, posting 17, probe_op 11.
- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`:** clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## Not exercised

A GUI post of a probe-only job. The note is a post-report string, and the test reads the same `verification_report` the GUI shows.

Changelog: A probe-only program no longer posts with a misleading "stock sim did not judge: invalid stock simulation setup" note; the uncut stock is judged (#592)

Fixes #592

title: fix(post): comment text is escaped per dialect
body:
## What changed
Operation, setup and tool names were already cleaned by each post's `clean()` (#257), but the **machine name in the program header was written raw**. Five shipped machine files have parentheses in their names (`Tormach 770MX (ML)`, `Tormach PCNC 1100 (Series I/II/3)`, `Tormach PCNC 770 (Series 3)`), so their headers posted a nested comment such as `(Tormach 770MX (ML))`, which LinuxCNC/PathPilot refuses. Hand-edited machine names (#478's editor) could break any dialect the same way.
- **The six affected posts:** the header name now goes through the post's own `clean()`, with a fallback of `CAMCRAFT` if nothing is left.
- **Tormach:** `note()` also guards against LinuxCNC active comments. A text starting with `MSG`, `DEBUG`, `PRINT`, `LOG*`, `PROBEOPEN`/`PROBECLOSE`, `ABORT`, `AXIS` or `PY*` (any case, whole word) is prefixed with `- `, so a user's name never becomes an operator message or a log command.
- **Engine default:** `writeComment()` (js.rs) turns `(`, `)` and control characters into spaces.
- **Rules:**
  - `( )` dialects (Fanuc, Fanuc lathe, Haas, Mazak, Tormach; RS-274 / ISO 6983): `( ) % ;` become spaces, non-printable or non-ASCII characters become `?`, runs of spaces collapse, 40-character cap.
  - Sinumerik: `;` comments get the same `clean()`.
  - Heidenhain: already safe; it is now tested.
- **Not done:** no uppercasing, so existing goldens stay byte-identical. Parentheses become spaces rather than `[ ]`, because brackets are expression syntax on macro B and LinuxCNC.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/594-comment-escape.md`.

## How tested
- **New `comment_escape`:**
  - `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_in_every_mill_dialect`: machine `MSG, Mill (A); B*`, op `Op (1); debug*`, tool `EM(6);*`. Every line holds at most one balanced comment closed at the end of the line, with no `;` and ASCII only. Tormach writes no active comment, and the Sinumerik and Heidenhain block rules hold.
  - `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_on_the_lathe`.
  - `every_bundled_machine_name_posts_a_single_header_comment`: every shipped Tormach .mch.
  - All three failed before the change.
- **Gate:** the 25 post-related app suites (conformance, golden_cl, posting, and every post, lathe, inverted, coolant and comment suite) and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean. **No golden changed.**

Changelog: Posts clean the machine name in the program header like every other comment (no nested "(...)" from names such as "Tormach 770MX (ML)"), and the Tormach post never writes a user name as a LinuxCNC active comment (MSG/DEBUG/PRINT/LOG...) (#594)

Fixes #594

title: feat(app): moving a part warns when it or its stock would sink into a fixture
body:
**Stacked on #576** (#571), which is on #566 (#561). It includes their commits until they merge.

## What changed
Locate (#561) already warns when the part or its stock would sink into a fixture. A plain Model-page move or turn didn't check at all (#582).
- **Shared check:** locate's sampled test and its by-name part and stock messages moved into a new `fixture_clash.rs`. `fixture_locate` calls it, and its wording is unchanged.
- **`MoveModel::new` now carries a `warning()`:**
  - the moved part is checked against every fixture in every setup, read through each setup's alignment;
  - a stock that follows the move is checked only in the setup that owns it;
  - setups with no fixtures are skipped without reading any geometry.
- **No double check in locate:** `MoveModel::locating` and the new `MoveFixture::locating` skip it, because locate runs its own check.
- **Fixture moves warn too:** `MoveFixture::new` checks the moved fixture against the setup's parts and stock.
- **Where it shows:** the status line reads `moved X - warning: …` (a shared `with_warning`), and MCP `move_fixture` gains a `"warning"` field.
- **A warning, not a refusal.** It warns on the result, so a part already inside a closed vise warns on every nudge.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/582-move-interpenetration.md`.

## How tested
- **New `move_interpenetration` (7):**
  - sinking into the floor warns by name;
  - a turn swinging into the jaw warns;
  - a stock-only sink warns for the stock alone;
  - a clear move warns nothing;
  - no fixtures means no check;
  - undo and redo of a warned move;
  - moving the fixture into the part warns.
- **UI:** `a_model_page_move_into_the_fixture_warns_on_the_status_line`.
- **Gate:** move_model_stock, commands_undo, fixture_locate(_stock), fixtures, fixture_ux, setup_align, project_roundtrip, mcp_setup and the ui fixture_ux/locate tests pass. Clippy is clean.

title: refactor(sim): law (d)'s prior readers read the stock through Columns
body:
## What changed

M7.3 step 2/6 (#26 umbrella, split in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/26#issuecomment-6754685656).

Law (d)'s prior-stock readers, `verify::prior_surface` and `verify::acquit_by_prior`, took `&Dexel`, which names the column engine directly. They now take `&Columns<'_>`, the M7.3 column seam that a column or field `Stock` already answers through.

- **`Columns` gains `Columns::of_grid(&Dexel)`:** a borrowed bare rest grid, read through the same seam. The reader's source becomes an internal `Source::{Grid, Field}`, so a reader no longer needs a whole `Stock`.
- **`Columns` gains `cell()`, `center(ix, iy)` and `origin()`.**
- **The operation layer** (`drill_prior::PriorRead::surface`, `generate.rs`'s acquittal) still holds the program-ahead grid as a `Dexel`, so it wraps it with `of_grid`. #586 moves that holder onto `Stock`, and the call then becomes `stock.columns()?`.
- **Scope corrected from the research:** `solid_rest` names no `Dexel`. `carry::Body` uses `Dexel` as storage, not as a reader, so that move goes with #586/#589. It's recorded on #585 and in `docs/decisions/585-prior-readers-on-columns.md`.

The change is behaviour-neutral: `Columns` maps a point to its column by the column engine's own formula, so a grid read through it answers identically.

## How tested

- **The existing `verify::prior` unit tests pass unchanged, 4/4**, wrapped in `Columns::of_grid`.
- **New `crates/sim/tests/prior_columns.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `the_prior_surface_reads_alike_through_a_grid_and_a_field`: inside the hole, across its rim and on the raw top, the column and field stocks agree within 1e-6. It reads the hole floor at 15 and the raw top at 25.
  - `a_dive_is_acquitted_alike_on_either_engine_and_through_a_bare_grid`: a column stock, a field stock and a bare grid acquit the same dive and keep the same conviction.

title: fix(units): status lines, refusals and the gate's gouge clause speak the document's units
body:
## What changed

Tier 1 of the #578 split (tiers and drops kept in `docs/decisions/578-units-in-errors.md`): transient strings - the ones that quote the numbers the user is already reading on screen - format at print time through `app::units::of(world)` and the pure `geometry::units` formatters. Millimeter strings stay byte-identical (the `len`/`feed`/`area` law: inches ride the mm precision plus extra decimals); only inch documents hear anything new.

- `geometry::units`: new `vol` formatter (inches get `mm_prec + 3`, mirroring `area`) and `Unit::vol_suffix`'s superscript spellings "mm³"/"in³" (matching `area_suffix`; a plain "mm3" would have changed the mm strings). Re-exported by `app::units`.
- The posting gate's gouge clause (`posting_sim::sim_clause`): worst depth and its location lens - `worst 0.1969 in at (-0.0246, -0.0738, z 0.1969)`.
- `commands/set_stock` refusal: `stock dimensions exceed 1000000 mm` - the shape changes from the old `{:e}`'s "1e6 mm" (see the correction comment on #578; the issue body's "2000 mm" misquoted it).
- `commands/cutting_data` "already runs the suggestion": spindle and feed through `feed`/`feed_suffix`.
- UI status strings: the applied-suggestion note, the tool-body tip offset, the feeds page's fz note, and the setup stock page's box range and volume (the only volume sentence in the UI).
- `ui::actions::deviate_readout` takes a `Unit` parameter, mirroring its sibling `sim_readout(&sc, t, Unit)`; both callers pass the world lens.

Held back, with reasons in the decision file: persisted notes (they freeze the unit into the `.camproj`; they want `Warning`-shaped structured notes - its own issue), machine-limit strings (those speak the machine's numbers; the inch-`.mch` unit-never-converted bug is noted on the issue, not fixed here), and the generator/pure-crate refusals (no world or unit in scope below the app).

## Pinning tests

- `blind_floor::the_gouge_clause_speaks_the_document_s_units` - the same gouging world told in inches ("... in at (...)", no "mm" anywhere); flip the lens back to mm and the sentence is unchanged.
- `egui_app::tests::deviate_readout_rides_the_units_lens` - REST and GOUGE sentences pinned in inches; the mm pins next to them untouched.

## Quick gate, green at 7775c1ff

`cargo test -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` clean, zero warnings. Then: `geometry --lib` 39, `app --lib` 101, `ui --lib` 378 (5 ignored), and the touched integration binaries `blind_floor` 7, `post_not_judged` 6, `cutting_data` 5, `edge_break_gate` 4, `commands_undo` 32, `dirty_flag` 2, `project_roundtrip` 69 - all pass.

Not exercised: the full suite (the pre-existing wgpu race upstream), and the on-screen widgets themselves - their formatting functions are pinned instead.

Changelog: errors, warnings and status notes ride the document's units - an inch document hears inches (saved notes and machine-limit messages stay mm, each its own issue).

body:
**Stacked on #521** (#362, Tormach PathPilot probing), which adds Tormach's probe result block. It includes #521's commits until that PR merges. #521 itself is unchanged.

## What changed
A probe program reported nothing about what it measured: on success it silently wrote `G10 L20`, and the offset table was the only trace. This came up in #521's run on a real 770MX.
- **Tormach PathPilot / LinuxCNC** (`tormach.cps` `onProbeResult`): writes `(DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n)` once per probed axis.
  - It sits after that axis's tolerance check, so the value shown has passed it, and before the `G10 L20`.
  - In a measure-only op it comes before its `(MSG, …)` / `M0`.
  - DEBUG shows in the status display without stopping and replaces `#n` with its value (LinuxCNC G-code reference, Messages/Comments, cited in the .cps).
- **Fanuc / Haas / Mazak:** no report. Custom macro B has only `#3000` (alarm) and `#3006` (stop with message), and DPRNT/POPEN go to an external device. A provenance comment next to `onProbeResult` says so, and output is unchanged.
- **Sinumerik and Heidenhain:** these posts have no probe hooks yet. The decision file records the future choice: Sinumerik `MSG("PROBE X ERROR "<<R190)` then `MSG()`; Heidenhain none until FN16 to `SCREEN:` is confirmed not to stop.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/575-probe-report.md`.

**Golden diffs:** only the Tormach probe goldens changed. Each gains one `(DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n)` line after its `o90n endif`: `probe_face`, `probe_edge`, `probe_corner`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm` and `probe_boss_centre`. Fanuc probe goldens and all cutting goldens are byte-identical.

## How tested
- **New `probe_report` (4):**
  - `tormach_face_reports_z_after_its_tolerance_test_and_before_g10`
  - `tormach_corner_reports_each_axis_before_g10`
  - `tormach_measure_only_reports_before_its_stop`
  - `fanuc_has_no_non_stopping_message_so_writes_no_report`
  - The three Tormach tests failed before the change.
- **Gate:** probe_tormach 7, probe_op 12, conformance, posting, tormach_post, fanuc_post, probe_reach, heidenhain_block_form, inverted_post and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
Seeing the DEBUG line on the real control. That can ride with #521's remaining mm run.

Changelog: Probe programs report each probed axis's measured deviation before writing the work offset: Tormach/PathPilot shows (DEBUG, PROBE <axis> ERROR #19n) without stopping; Fanuc-family controls have no non-stopping message and write none (#575)

Fixes #575

title: fix(post): an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change in every post
body:
**Stacked on #579** (#570, probe search limit and feed-only approach). It includes #579's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
Every mill post now writes an explicit spindle stop between a probe's tool change and length offset and its first move. Today the probe is safe on a Tormach only because PathPilot's `M6` stops the spindle, which is a property of the control, not something the program says.
- **Rule:** in `startPreamble`, `probeStop = spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`. Only a probe states 0 rpm, because tools refuse 0. After the spindle block and before coolant, the post writes the stop.
- **Per post:**
  - Fanuc, Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain: `M5`.
  - Mazak: `MOTOFF`, its own stop word.
  - Fanuc Lathe: untouched (no probing).
- **Unchanged:** cutting sections and older streams post byte-identical output.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/574-probe-m5.md`.

**Stack merge (`fd1076af`):** #579 branched from a main older than #174's protected probe moves, so merging it hit conflicts in three Fanuc goldens and broke `probe_guard`. The merge commit resolves both.
- #579's new feed from the safe plane down to the approach plane now posts as a protected move: `G31` plus the `#5063` alarm on Fanuc, `G38.3` plus the `#5070` check on Tormach.
- `probe_guard` expects one more protected move per mode.
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc` and `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc` are regenerated to match.

#579 will need the same resolution when it takes main.

**Golden diffs from #574 itself:** each file gains one `M5` line right after the `G43` line:
- `fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner_negative.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_edge_negative_x.nc`
- `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`

Until #526 merges, some posts still write a probe's spindle start (`S0 M3`) before the new stop. The flag is computed separately, so it works in either merge order; Heidenhain will have a small hand-merge next to #526's lines.

## How tested
- **New `probe_spindle_stop`, all six mill posts:**
  - `a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`: the stop comes after the tool change and offset, before the first move, and nothing restarts the spindle. It failed before the change.
  - `a_cutting_section_states_no_spindle_stop_before_its_first_move`: the control case.
- **Also passing:** probe_op, probe_guard, inverted_probe, conformance, posting, tormach_post, fanuc_post, heidenhain_block_form, sinumerik_safe_retract, plus #579's probe_search, probe_pick and probe_reach, and all camcraft-post tests. Clippy (post and app) is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
A Hub or machine run of a probe program with the new `M5`. It is a defensive stop on an already-stopped spindle.

Changelog: Every mill post writes an explicit spindle stop (M5; MOTOFF on Mazak) after a probe's tool change and length offset, before its first move (#574)

Fixes #574

title: fix(app): a probe searches a short way past the face and feeds below the safe plane
body:
## What changed

Found on the contributor's real Tormach 770MX during #521's hands-on probe test. Two things alarmed the operator: a new Probe op searched **5 mm** past the expected face (`G38.2 Z-0.1969`), and its approach was a **rapid straight down** to 0.197 in over the part.

- **Shorter default search:** a new Probe op's probe distance is `default_overtravel(tolerance) = max(2 × tolerance, 1 mm)`, which is 1 mm for the seeded 0.5 mm tolerance. Existing documents keep their stated value.
- **Named, non-blocking advisory:** a new `Warning::ProbeSearch` flags any probe distance past `SEARCH_LIMIT_MM` (2 mm). Like `Scallop`, it never holds the post, so old 5 mm documents still post. It is wired into the UI warning list, MCP `job` and `warned_moves`.
- **Protected approach:** `probing::probe_cycle` now opens with a positioning rapid that ends at the **safe plane** over the first start, then **feeds** at the seek feed down to the approach point. No probe rapid runs below the safe plane. The positioning rapid is zero-length in the path's frame, because the path cannot know the tool-change position, and every post writes it as its positioning block. That keeps the Fanuc post from feeding diagonally from the tool change.
- **Probe page hint:** it now says the distance is a search **limit**, not a destination, and that over 2 mm is flagged.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/570-probe-search-and-approach.md`.

## Readings

- **Before**, Fanuc golden: `G00 X-22 Y5 Z25` (a rapid to the approach point).
- **After**, the same golden:
  ```
  G00 X-22 Y5 Z50
  G01 X-22 Y5 Z25 F300
  ```
- The 770MX run with a hand-edited approach-as-feed and a Z-0.05 search touched at Z≈0. G54 Z moved from -8.3252 to -8.3259, a 0.0007 in correction, in line with a manual 0.0009 check.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/probe_search.rs`, 3/3:**
  - `a_new_probe_op_searches_a_short_way_past_the_face`: the seed follows its tolerance and draws no advisory.
  - `a_deep_search_is_named_and_never_holds_the_post`
  - `below_the_safe_plane_a_probe_only_feeds`: Face, Edge, Corner, Bore and Boss. It **fails on the old cycle** with "positioning ends at the safe plane, not 15".
- **Fixtures:** `probe_pick` and `probe_reach` move to the new 1 mm default, since they stand for new ops. `probe_op` and `fanuc_post` keep 5 mm, standing for old documents.
- **Goldens:** the 3 Fanuc probe goldens are regenerated, with one line added each. No snapshot changed.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** sim, motion and app suites ran 2307 passed, 0 failed. The ui suites are green except the 3 known headless-GPU tests on this host ("No suitable graphics adapter found"), which are environmental.
- **Named:** probe_search 3, probe_op 11, probe_reach 5, probe_pick 9, fanuc_post 11, posting 17, conformance 6.
- **Clippy** on app, ui, motion and sim with `-D warnings`: clean.
- Fork synced at v0.15.0.

## Not exercised

The post straight from this build on the real 770MX. The hand-edited equivalent ran clean, but PathPilot flagged "Axis XY not specified" on the hand edit, which this post's `startXY` G0 X Y avoids.

**Stacked after this, by the M3:** #574 (an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change), then #575 (report the deviation).

Changelog: A new probe op searches only 1 mm past the expected face (was 5 mm), a probe distance over 2 mm is flagged, and a probe never rapids below the safe plane - it feeds down to its approach point (#570)

Fixes #570

title: fix(app): turning a part keeps a square stock square
body:
**Stacked on #566** (#561, locate the part in a fixture). It includes #566's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
Turning a part on the Model page rotated its stock rigidly with it (`move_model.rs`), so a square blank came out tilted. #566 fixed this for locate only. Now every `MoveModel` that **turns** the part uses the same square-stock rule (`stock_follow::keep_square`):
- **Square stocks:** a box or cylinder whose axes lie along the setup's axes (any quarter turn) keeps its orientation. It is refitted around the part's new place, keeping each side's allowance, measured in the stock's own frame before the move.
- **Quarter turns refit too; the block doesn't rotate with the part.** One rule for one gesture, so 89.99° and 90° give the same kind of blank. Top stays top, so a "+top for facing" allowance never moves onto a side. A yaw quarter turn refits to the same size anyway.
- **Unchanged cases:**
  - Translation-only moves keep the old rigid carry, with no refit and no mesh rebuild.
  - A copied-from-model stock, or one already off the axes, still turns rigidly with the part.
- **Locate:** `MoveModel::locating` now just calls `MoveModel::new`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/571-movemodel-square-stock.md`.

## How tested
- **Updated pin:** `commands_undo::moving_one_part_carries_existing_stock_and_undo_restores_both` keeps its intent (the stock follows, undo restores both). After a 90° yaw plus a move, the stock stays square and wraps the part.
- **New `move_model_stock`:**
  - a 30° turn keeps a box stock square with each allowance, and undo/redo are exact;
  - a 30° turn keeps a cylinder upright;
  - translation-only moves carry the stock rigidly as before;
  - a turned or copied stock still turns rigidly.
  - The pin and both 30° tests failed before the change.
- **Gate:** app lib (105), commands_undo, fixture_locate(_stock), setup_align, plane_align(_edges), top_stock, setup_stock_source, stock_stamp, project_roundtrip, wcs_align, pick_doors, stock_view, stock_play, the ui models tests and the ui locate tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised
A hands-on GUI turn on the Model page.

Changelog: Turning a part on the Model page keeps a square box or cylinder stock square to the machine, refitted around the part with its per-side allowances; moves that only slide the part carry the stock as before (#571)

Fixes #571
