title: feat(machine): per-axis direction in the machine file; inverted axes refuse posting until #374
body:
## What changed

Part of #372 (decision: the machine's axis really moves the other way; the CAM side stays right-handed per ISO 841).

- **Machine file:** a linear part of a file-form `.mch` takes `"direction": 1 | -1`. Absent or null means `1`. Anything else (`0`, `2`, `0.5`, `"-1"`, a vector, a bool) refuses at load and names the axis: `machine file: axis X direction must be +1 or -1, not 2`. A numeric `-1` on a rotary part refuses too (a reversed rotary is not supported).
- **Model:** `AxisLimits::direction: machine::AxisDirection { Standard, Inverted }` (new `crates/post/src/machine/direction.rs`), plus `Machine::inverted_axes()`, `Machine::inverted_post_refusal()` and `AxisLimits::program_travel()`, ready for #374 to read. The project file stores it as `1`/`-1`; a bad value refuses the load. A standard axis writes no key, so every shipped machine, every saved project and the post mirror are byte-identical.
- **Travel check:** a stated stroke is the machine's own, in the coordinates its controller reads. An inverted axis is judged as `-v` against `[lo, hi]`, and the breach line says `(inverted axis)`. The derived table box maps the stroke to `[-hi, -lo]` in the program frame.
- **Posting is refused until #374:** the verification gate adds `machine <model> has an inverted X axis; posting for inverted axes is not supported yet (#374)`. That one gate blocks the single post, per-op posts and the script API's gate. The CLI `post --machine` refuses the same way, and now also refuses a file that `parse_mch` refuses. Standard-sign code is never posted for an inverted machine.
- **Machine page:** the machine editor gets a per-axis choice: "X+ moves: right / left", Y "away / toward you", Z "up / down", other letters "standard / reversed". An inverted axis shows a note that posting is refused until #374. The editor edits a draft that is applied through the existing undoable `EditMachineApply` -> `LoadMachine` command, so no new command was needed.
- Docs: grammar row in `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`; decisions in `docs/decisions/373-axis-direction.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/axis_direction.rs` (11 tests):
  - `direction_reads_plus_one_minus_one_and_absent`, `any_other_direction_refuses_by_name`, `a_reversed_rotary_refuses_and_other_rotary_shapes_are_not_read`
  - `every_shipped_machine_stays_standard` (every `posting::MACHINES` entry: no inverted axis, no serialized key, mirror unchanged)
  - `direction_round_trips_through_serde_and_refuses_garbage`, `an_inverted_machine_survives_a_project_save_and_load`, `loading_an_inverted_machine_undoes`
  - `travel_is_judged_in_the_machines_own_coordinates`, `the_table_box_maps_an_inverted_stroke`
  - `an_inverted_machine_refuses_posting_by_name`, `the_refusal_names_every_inverted_axis`
- `crates/post/tests/axis_direction_cli.rs`: `the_cli_refuses_an_inverted_machine_by_name`

## Gate (quick, debug, this worktree)

- Merged origin/main (#354 one-WCS) cleanly; app suites green after the merge: axis_direction 11, machine 32, tormach_machines 5, posting 17, conformance 6, golden_cl 23, fanuc_post 8, project_roundtrip 69, fixtures 14, setup_sheet 7. The goldens are unchanged.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all suites) green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` run from `crates/ui`: 297 passed, 2 ignored (after merging origin/main; on the pre-merge base, `egui_shell_snapshot_light` and `tool_editor_snapshot` failed the same way without this change - #354 regenerated those snapshots)

Not tested: the editor's combo by hand (the GUI was not launched), and posting itself for an inverted machine, which is #374.

Changelog: The machine file states a per-axis direction (`"direction": -1` on a linear part, shown on the machine editor as "X+ moves: right / left"). Travel limits are judged through an inverted axis. Posting for a machine with an inverted axis is refused by name until #374.

Fixes #373

body:
This is the first slice of #287: a read-only **Machines** pane that browses machine configurations and validates them, naming each refusal. Create, edit and save, and "Use for this setup", are follow-ups (#287 stays open).

## What changed
**App layer** (`crates/app/src/machine/`):
- `library.rs` builds the machine catalogue: the built-in machines, plus the `.mch` the document mounted through Load other.
  - Each entry carries its kind, axes, rotaries and units.
  - It also lists the posts that can drive the machine: the built-in posts for which `posting::post_serves` is true.
  - A `scan_dir` hook is ready for a user folder.
- `validate.rs` returns named refusals as `key: rule`, read from the raw JSON (`parse_mch` silently drops a backwards travel). It checks:
  - travel min < max;
  - stated feeds and speeds > 0;
  - codes are well formed;
  - the keys each machine kind requires are present.
  - A malformed file is refused by name.
- `sheet.rs` builds the read-only property sheet, grouped as General, Axes, Spindle, Tool station, Coolants and Posts, in the file's own unit.

**UI:**
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/machines_pane.rs`: a dockable pane opened from the ribbon's View dropdown, with a list, a sheet and the validation result.
- Opening the pane and selecting a machine are view state, never commands, following the existing panel convention. No project data changes, so nothing goes on the undo history.

`docs/decisions/287-machines-pane.md` records the slice boundary and the user-folder decision, which is posted on #287.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine_library`: 11/11 pass.
- `--test machine`: 32/32 pass.
- `camcraft-ui --lib machines_pane`: 3/3 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`:
  - app: all pass.
  - ui: only the known reds that also fail on upstream main:
    - the GPU headless tests `headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` and `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`;
    - the `egui_shell_snapshot_light` and `tool_editor_snapshot` goldens (#255).
- After that gate, the branch merged upstream/main again; the narrow tests still pass.
- All 10 registered shipped machines validate clean. `3axis-vmc.mch` is the post's static `DEFAULT_MCH` and is not a registered machine, so it is not listed.

## Pinning tests
- **App:**
  - `every_shipped_machine_lists_and_validates_clean`
  - `every_machine_file_in_assets_is_in_the_library`
  - `backwards_travel_refuses_naming_the_axis`
  - `non_positive_feeds_and_speeds_refuse_by_name`
  - `malformed_codes_refuse_by_name`
  - `required_keys_per_kind_refuse_by_name`
  - `other_stated_values_refuse_by_name`
  - `malformed_files_refuse_by_name_and_never_panic`
  - `a_user_file_lists_by_its_model_and_an_unreadable_one_by_name`
  - `the_catalogue_adds_the_documents_machine_file`
  - `a_good_crafted_mill_validates_clean`
- **UI (structural, no golden PNGs):**
  - `the_view_door_opens_the_machines_pane_beside_properties`
  - `selecting_a_shipped_machine_shows_its_sheet_and_a_clean_validation`
  - `a_refused_machine_file_shows_each_refusal_by_name`

## Not exercised
- No GUI hand test yet; a test binary has been built for the maintainer.
- There is no user machines folder yet (decision posted on #287).
- An AGENTS.md (`assets/machines/AGENTS.md`) changed, so run `/graphify . --update` after merge.

title: feat(tools): judge a modelled tool body by its revolved envelope
body:
First slice of #361 (vendor STEP tool models): milling.

## What changed
- **`SetToolBody` (new, undoable: set / replace / clear).** It attaches a holder or assembly mesh (STEP, STL or OBJ, through the existing importer) to a milling tool.
  - **Placement** is numeric: which model direction is the tool axis, and the model origin's height above the tip.
  - **Validated at command creation, refusals by name:** non-finite, empty or degenerate meshes; a body whose XY bounds don't contain the axis; a body reaching below the flute top; lathe insert kinds (that is #369).
  - `ChangeTool`, generation and the post gate also refuse a body that would sit over the flutes.
- **The revolved envelope** (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`):
  - Each triangle is clipped exactly to every band it crosses, and the band takes the farthest clipped vertex. It is exact, so a facet crossing a band with no vertex in it still counts.
  - Bands are cut at 0.25 mm or more (at most 2048), then merged down to at most 32, each merge keeping the larger radius. The envelope can only grow.
- **How the checks read it:**
  - **Fixture collision laws** (upright and posed, `sim/laws.rs`, `posed_steel.rs`, `workholding.rs`) take a `HolderStack` of real bands. `HolderStack::cylinder(geom)` reproduces the old float sums, so a tool without a body is bit-identical.
  - **Every one-cylinder check** (rest reach, solid law, multi-axis shank dodge, drill reach, cross-drill holder, machine max tool length) sees the tool with its holder replaced by the cylinder enclosing the body (`HolderProfile::enclose`). It is swapped in at three world reads: `collect_job`, the post gate's fixture walk, and the machine check. It can only over-report.
- **The body is part of the operation stamp** (it can change the generated path). It adds bytes only when present, so existing stamps are unchanged.
- **Project file v54.** An optional `body` key on the tool row holds the placed facets and placement. The envelope is re-derived on load, never saved, and a bad body refuses the file by name. The bump stops a v53 build from silently dropping the body and judging the smaller cylinder.
  - **Conflict note:** #354 also takes v54. Whichever merges second renumbers to v55, one line in the ladder plus the `51..=54` rung in `apply.rs`.
- **Deleting the tool** (`DeleteTool` / `DeleteEntity`) frees the body, and undo restores it.
- `docs/decisions/368-tool-body-step.md`

## How tested
- New `holder_profile` unit tests (7), including a facet crossing a band with no vertex in it, and a randomized check that no point on any facet lies outside its band.
- New `crates/app/tests/tool_body.rs` (8):
  - A 40 mm collar turns a move the 22 mm cylinder passed into a named holder collision, in generation and in the post gate.
  - A stepped body (narrow nose, wide flange) passes a post beside the nose that the enclosing cylinder would have hit.
  - With no body, the stamp and toolpath are identical to before.
  - Undo/redo walk set, replace and clear.
  - Save → load → save is byte-identical.
  - Deleting the tool frees the body, and degenerate input refuses by name.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` (macOS), after merging upstream/main: tools, sim and app suites all green. That includes every existing golden_cl, fixtures, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo and drill suite, unchanged.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests` is clean, and `cargo check -p camcraft-ui` passes.

## Not exercised
- No UI: attaching a body is reachable from the command and the project file only. The picking UI and display are #371; ISO 13399 auto-alignment is #370 (stacking on this branch).
- Not yet in the tool library file (#348).

Changelog: Tools can carry a modelled holder body (STEP/STL/OBJ) placed by axis and tip offset; collision checks judge its revolved envelope (#368)

Fixes #368

title: feat(import): read named tool coordinate systems from a vendor STEP
body:
This is the STEP side of #370. It follows the split agreed on the issue with the #368 holder: a reader that returns a vendor tool STEP's named coordinate systems as plain data. It adds no tool-body component, command, project field or UI. Turning a found system into #368's numeric placement is the next round, which stacks on `issue/368-tool-body-step` once that branch is pushed.

## What changed
- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs`:
  - `read_tool_csys(&[u8])` returns every named `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` with its name, entity id and role, its origin in mm (scaled by the file's length unit), and its unit z and x axes.
  - `CsysRole::classify` maps the ISO/TS 13399 names below, ignoring case. Any other name is `Other` and is never used for alignment.
  - `find(role)` returns the single system with that role, or the named reason there isn't one (missing, refused or ambiguous).
  - `none_found()` returns the named reason a caller falls back to numeric placement.
  - Refusals are by name, never a panic:
    - a zero or non-finite direction;
    - a non-finite origin;
    - a reference direction parallel to the axis;
    - a dangling or wrong-kind reference;
    - one name used for two different placements.
- `step_units.rs`: three helpers are now visible inside the module (`pub(super)`).
- Three original, hand-written fixtures in `testdata/models/tool_csys_*.step`.
- `docs/decisions/370-tool-csys-align.md`

## Names, confirmed before any code
The names come from public ISO/TS 13399 preview pages (iTeh samples of parts 303, 401 and 405) and are cited in the provenance comment and the decisions file:
- PCS (primary coordinate system)
- MCS (mounting coordinate system)
- CIP (coordinate system in process)
- CSIF (coordinate system interface)
- CSW / CSWx / CSWx_y (coordinate system workpiece side)

CRP is a point, not a coordinate system, so it is not read.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys`: 6/6 pass. The existing `import` suite and the `step_units` unit tests still pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`: every app suite passes except `scripting`, which SIGSEGV'd once under concurrent load.
  - This branch touches nothing on the scripting path.
  - The same binary passed 45 of 45 reruns alone.
  - Filed as #379 (P1).

## Pinning tests
- `iso_13399_coordinate_systems_are_found_and_classified`
- `a_file_without_tool_coordinate_systems_says_so_by_name`
- `degenerate_or_ambiguous_coordinate_systems_are_refused_by_name`
- `origins_read_in_the_files_length_unit`
- `iso_13399_names_classify_and_others_do_not`
- `unreadable_input_is_a_clean_error_never_a_panic`

## Not exercised
- No real vendor STEP package was tried; the fixtures are hand-written.
- Assembly transforms are not composed: coordinates are in the frame of the part that holds them. Same-named systems in different frames give the ambiguity refusal, not a silent pick.
- The issue's "aligns with no manual offsets" waits for #368's body model, so this PR is `Refs`, not `Fixes`.

Changelog: none (reader only; no user-visible behaviour until the #368 wiring)

Refs #370

title: docs: add machine onboarding checklist and software examples
body:
## Summary

- Add a contributor-facing machine onboarding checklist covering sourced facts, units/coordinates, axis and spindle limits, controller/post fit, and manual citation/redistribution boundaries.
- Point to the actual `.mch` parser/checker/mirror, machine and post registries, and existing test seams rather than inventing a new configuration API.
- Provide a milling/turning operation and fixture matrix plus seven reproducible existing-test commands. Reuse `Milling-test.step` and the original synthetic turning fixtures; distinguish missing knurl and end-to-end lathe-tapping coverage.
- Document current JSON-comment, unknown rigid-tapping, and headless-interface limits. MCP can verify machine data in an opened project, but has no direct `.mch` loader.
- Keep physical-machine acceptance separate: software fixtures are not machine certification. No machine, post dialect, UI, schema, verifier, dependency or toolpath change.

Readings: `AGENTS.md`, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, the current machine/post/MCP/project source and the linked existing tests. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/298-machine-onboarding.md`.

## Validation

Seven selected Windows tests executed successfully, each with native exit 0 and one passing test:

- `machine::every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`
- `posting::machine_limits_block_the_post_and_within_limits_does_not`
- `tormach_machines::every_tormach_machine_states_its_manuals_figures`
- `tormach_machines::a_tap_job_posts_on_the_1100mx_and_is_refused_on_the_770m`
- `lathe_post::an_axial_drill_posts_through_the_document_with_the_lathe_post_chosen`
- `lathe_post_g76::a_g76_thread_posts_to_the_lathe_golden`
- `lead_approach::every_lead_option_on_the_users_part_verifies_silent` (imports the existing STEP model)

These ran on `205eeaa4b0c09035193f4f569a881d0ce9fe5285`; the final commit changes only one documentation paragraph and adds the already-exercised STEP command. Runtime inputs are unchanged, so those results are reused, not represented as a new run.

On final head `7127a273ec990d570cc673309af0c51c96cc098d`, `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -Base 51b80a5d362dc0b2bcf8a4592fb8a8dfa427c35a` exited 0. Its docs-only mapping selected **zero Rust steps**; this is not additional runtime-test evidence. Local link/line-target and exact-test-name checks passed (36 links, seven targets); `git diff --check` passed. Independent static technical/documentation review passed after correcting the MCP wording.

## Limits

No new all-operations qualification job is introduced. The guide explains which existing fixtures are useful and what remains unsupported/unverified. No real machine execution, NC transfer, physical acceptance, Linux/macOS run, full/release campaign or hosted workflow dispatch was performed. Hosted checks are intentionally absent under the repository's local-gate workflow policy, not reported as green CI. Maintainer review/merge remains manual.

title: fix(motion): rotary Adaptive sorts the leave-limit level as material and names a narrowed helix before planning
body:
## What changed
- **Float noise at the leave limit** (the root cause of the red heavy test `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`). On the r7 bar the wrap's ladder level comes out as 6.500000000000001, one ulp above the leave limit `air_above` = 6.5. `pocket3d_air_split` split with a bare `>`, so it sorted that level as an air level (one lap) and the plan read 19.9 % D against the 19.7 % law. The new `machining3d::entry::air_levels` counts a plane within `EPS` of the limit as a material plane, as the function's doc already said ("at or below"). `pocket3d_air_split` is only called by the rotary wrap.
- **Narrowed helix refused by name before planning.** On the wrap only (seam present), `hsm::plan_level` now asks the planner's own entry rule (`machining2d::choose_entry`, now `pub(crate)`). If that rule would narrow the requested helix, Offset rings cut the level, with a note: `adaptive: the developed level is too narrow for the helix entry (radius 1.000 asked, 0.900 fits with room to spiral out) - Offset rings cut ... instead`. The note text is exported as `machining3d::NARROW_HELIX`. Before, the narrowed spiral overloaded (15.7 % D).
- **r6.2 travel refusal: kept and recorded as final.** The 5.7 and 5.2 levels are ~78 × 7.8 and ~78 × 5.8 mm bands round the neck. The variant with lifted returns breaks the planner's own 47.5 deg bound (48.0), and the plain spiral travels 3.2× and 3.9× its cut length out of cut (budget 1.5×). Refusing by name, and cutting with Offset rings, is the safe answer. Planning thin bands properly belongs to #44 and #47. Pinned by name.
- `rotary_adaptive.rs` (474 lines) is split: fixtures and the level reader move to `crates/motion/tests/rotary_adaptive_fixture/mod.rs`, a module with no binary of its own.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/55-rotary-adaptive-levels.md`.

## Readings (release; D6 ball, leave 0.5, helix r1, limit 19.7 % D)
| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| r7 bar, radius 6.5 | 19.9 % D (red) | 19.5 % D, two laps |
| r7 bar, radius 6.0 / 5.5 | 19.5 / 18.8 % | unchanged |
| r7 bar, posted world program | - | 160,989 moves, 0 in-cut breaks > 5 deg |
| 10 mm window, stepdown 2 | helix narrowed to 0.9, then 15.7 % overload; radius 5.0 refused after 197 revolutions | both levels refused by name, 0.4 s debug |
| r6.2 bar, radius 5.7 / 5.2 | refused for travel (8,208 / 8,828 mm out of cut) | still refused, now pinned by name |

The load margin on the r7 bar is still thin (19.5 against 19.7).

## Posted output
This changes posted G-code for **rotary-wrap programs only**: a wrap level at the leave limit is cleared over two laps (as in round 2), and an Adaptive wrap level too narrow for the helix is cut by Offset rings. Planar 2D and 3D pockets are unaffected. The OffsetRings golden digest on the r6.2 bar is unchanged. The PR stays a **draft** for a PathPilot Hub run.

## Pinning tests
- `rotary_adaptive::a_window_too_narrow_for_the_helix_is_refused_by_name_before_planning` (debug)
- `rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_refused_for_travel_by_name` (heavy lane)
- `rotary_adaptive::adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` (heavy lane, red on main, green here)
- `machining3d::hsm::tests::a_band_too_narrow_for_the_helix_is_named_before_planning`
- `machining3d::tests::a_plane_at_the_leave_envelope_is_a_material_plane`

## Gate
- Quick gate on the merge with upstream/main: motion suites green except the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (#351).
- Worker runs: release `rotary_adaptive --ignored` 4/4, motion lib 151, the rotary and pocket motion suites, and the app rotary suites, all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: Rotary Adaptive: the level at the part's leave limit is no longer sorted by float noise, and a developed band too narrow for the helix entry is cut by Offset rings with a note naming it instead of an overloaded plan (#55)

Fixes #55

title: feat(sim): the scallop flank reads to the ball diameter, between contact passes only
body:
## What changed
The scallop verifier's flank reach grows from `band + 3·tol` to `max(2r, band + 3·tol)` (`ridge::reach`). It now reads a cusp at any stepover up to the ball diameter, which is the generator's own ceiling (#37 `scallop_ceiling`). Before, it stopped at 4·tol past the ball. In #37 a plain widening convicted crowns, corners and box walls as scallop. Three cusp-geometry rules in the new `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/ridge_scan.rs` keep those false cusps out:
1. **Nearest feet only.** Only segments within `max(cell, 3·tol)` of the nearest distance count. A cusp stands equally far from both passes.
2. **One foot per pass.** Segments group into passes (joined runs, merged by closed iso-Z ring). Each pass counts once, at its nearest point. A free end gives no side.
3. **Both feet in contact** (`Access::touches`). A pass riding air or skimming stock flanks nothing.

The M13.8 `Flank` struct is retired. The ridge pass moved out of `scan.rs` (431 → 359 lines) into `ridge_scan.rs` (276 lines, with a provenance header). The full decision record is in `docs/decisions/212-scallop-reach.md`.

## Readings
- Flat raster at s=4 on an r3 ball: scallop 0 before (unread), **0.606** now (the analytic cusp).
- All 88 finish3d release-lane verdict fixtures stay clean. `morphed_spiral_dome_bites_nothing` goes from 0.1321 to 0. Flow 15/15.
- **One existing heavy-lane assertion changed:** `verify::envelope_verdict_follows_the_stated_tol` (app, `--ignored`). Its tight half (tol 0.01 on cone rings laddered for tol 0.1) used to expect silence. It now expects exactly one **non-blocking** `Scallop` note, for the rings' real ~0.085 mm cusp. That is over the 0.01 budget and under the 0.1 the rings were laddered to. The envelope (gouge/rest) half is unchanged.

Nothing generated or posted changes. Only the verifier's notes change, and the Scallop note stays non-blocking.

## Pinning tests
`crates/sim/tests/ridge_reach.rs`:
- `a_flat_raster_past_the_near_reach_is_judged_at_its_cusp`
- `the_wider_flank_never_softens_the_old_reading`
- `a_crown_above_the_top_lap_stays_rest_not_scallop`
- `a_wall_top_edge_the_rings_run_beside_stays_rest_not_scallop`
- `a_pass_clear_of_the_part_flanks_nothing`

## Gate
- Quick gate on the merge with upstream/main (51b80a5): sim suites green; app suites green except the known `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag` (#344, fixed by #345).
- Worker runs: sim release with `--ignored` green, app release heavy lanes green, motion green (apart from the known `swarf_pose_continuity`, #351).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: The scallop check now reads cusps from spacings up to the ball diameter (it used to stop at 4·tol past the ball) and no longer reports false cusps at crowns, corners or air passes (#212)

Fixes #212

title: fix(setup)!: one WCS per setup; G54-G59 is only the setup's post label
body:
## What changed
- **One WCS per setup.** `SetupDef.wcs` is now one entity name (was a six-slot list); `SetupDef.work_offset` is only the `G54`..`G59` word the post writes for it. Relabelling moves no origin and no height. `setup::wcs_entity` / `wcs_entity_name` take no slot; new `setup::wcs_label` ("WCS (G55)").
- **Commands.** `SetWcsOrigin::new(world, location)` places the active setup's one WCS (slot argument removed). A new setup's WCS is `<setup>/WCS`; the materialized first setup keeps pointing at the legacy `G54` entity (nothing renamed). Datum transfer clones the one WCS; DeleteSetup takes its own WCS with it.
- **Browser.** The Setup section shows a single row labelled plain **WCS** (the posted word as its faint suffix). The G55-G59 / "not placed" rows are gone. Clicking it opens the WCS page (`UiTarget::Wcs`), which edits the active setup's origin through the undoable `SetWcs` (numeric origin, turns, anchors, vertex/face origin chips, 3-2-1 align, Origin ribbon cell). The Setups-page dropdown is the only place the word is chosen.
- **Wording.** The WCS page heading, setup sheet (`WCS` section, `WCS (G55)` line), rotated-WCS refusal, Heights page read-only row, viewport height chip (`(WCS G55 +25.00)`), status lines and MCP `get_job` (`wcs` is now one object: label/word/placed/entity/origin/rotation) all speak of the setup's WCS.

## Migration (project v54, `project::wcs_one`)
- Each v53 setup keeps the entity (name and placement) of the slot it posted (its pick, else G54) as its one WCS, so single-WCS documents post byte for byte.
- Placed slots that no setup posted are dropped, each with a **load note** naming the entity and where it sat. `project::open_noted` / `load_noted` return the notes, the shell shows them in the status line, and they are logged.
- A document without setups keeps `G54` as its WCS and drops the rest with notes.
- An operation naming a setup the file does not hold posted at `<setup>/G54`. That entity is renamed `<setup>/WCS`, so the operation keeps its zero.
- Two origins inside one setup only arise from v51-or-older files. The existing v52 rung refuses those by name before this rung runs, so the migration never picks an origin. A v54 file that still lists slots is refused as corrupt. A malformed old offset row is still refused by the validator, not dropped.
- The two-setups-same-word-different-origin post refusal (#196) is unchanged.
- Stamp shape unchanged (the work-offset word is still digested), so migrated stamps stay fresh. Relabelling therefore asks a work-offset-height op for one regenerate, which produces the same path.

## Readings and tests
- New `crates/app/tests/one_wcs.rs` (7):
  - single placed slot posts identically;
  - several placed slots keep the posted one and drop the rest with notes;
  - a no-setup document keeps G54 and drops G55, and resaves byte-identical;
  - two setups keep their own posted origins;
  - an operation in a missing setup keeps its zero;
  - v54 with a slot list is corrupt;
  - a WCS edit undoes inside its own setup and a relabel spawns no origin.
- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/one_wcs.rs` (2): the browser shows one WCS per setup with no slot rows, and the WCS row edits the active setup's origin undoably.
- Rewritten for the new model: `setup_wcs` (relabel = word only, placing moves coordinates, undo), `setup_defines_wcs` (v51 fixtures built as JSON; conflicting v51 setups still refused by name), plus setups, heights, lathe_spindle_law, commands_undo, posting, rotated_wcs, project_roundtrip, setup_align and the ui shell/law/chip tests.
- Shell snapshots regenerated (`egui_app.png`, `egui_app_light.png`, `egui_tool_editor.png`). I checked them: the six G5x rows became one `WCS G54` row, and the chip reads `(WCS G54 +0.00)`.
- Gate results:

title: fix(multiaxis): a swarf raster line rises off the blade on a rapid under its lying pose
body:
## What changed
A swarf raster line used to turn upright on its exit rise, which forced an air link (retract, swing, re-plunge) at every raster end. Now, where it is proved safe, the rise posts as a **rapid that keeps the lying pose the line cut with**; the pose carries through the clearance rapid and the next line plunges under that same pose, so there is no head swing at all. New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp_rise.rs` decides it; `stamp.rs` calls it during posing. Every condition must hold, otherwise the rise stays the old upright feed and the existing link law handles the turn:
- a feed going straight up Z with no XY travel;
- the program has already leaned, and the held pose is a lean not below level;
- the end of the rise is in air (beyond the contact band);
- the ball never gets closer to the part on the way up than at the start (the same floor the link retract uses);
- the held pose's flank is proved clear (`flank_clear`) at every half-radius sample up the rise.

The ball travels exactly the path the plan already gave it; only the flank differs, and it is checked. The rotaries don't move during the rapid. A rapid claims no contact, so the posed-contact law that flagged #17's in-air posed feed has nothing to judge; the posed-rapid solid law still checks it like every link retract. **No verifier law changed**; the other option (excusing a feed that leaves along the surface normal) was dropped.

## Readings
`swarf_pose_continuity` was **already red on main** (3 pass / 2 fail) in the same ratchet: the advanced count had drifted to 53 (pin 51) and the advanced full band to 86 (pin 84). This PR brings every count well under the old pins and sets the pins to the new counts:

| run | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| swarf, debug band | 34 | 23 |
| advanced, debug band | 53 | 34 |
| swarf, full band | 55 | 44 |
| advanced, full band | 86 | 67 |

- `swarf_pose_continuity` 6/6 (was 3/5); motion `--lib multiaxis` 57; `swarf_reentry`, `ruling`, `pivot5d` debug all pass; `pivot5d` heavy lane (release, `--ignored`) `the_envelope_reads_every_posed_kind_as_its_plan` passes (an envelope scan #17 left owed).
- app `operations::swarf_generates_blade_lying_axes_and_verifies_clean` and `advanced_swarf_adds_the_coarse_rungs` verify clean, as do their `_full_band` twins in the ignored lane; app `verify`, `area_controls`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, the swarf `project_roundtrip` test; sim `posed_rapids`, `posed_fixture_midpose` all pass.
- Quick gate (motion suites): green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests
`swarf_pose_continuity::every_raster_exit_rise_is_a_rapid_holding_the_lying_pose` (new; finds no lying rises on the old code), the lowered link ratchets in `swarf_pose_continuity`, and `stamp_rise` unit tests (rapid when the flank is clear; stays a feed when a wall blocks the flank; rejects anything that isn't a straight rise from a lean into air).

## Needs the maintainer's hands (why this stays a draft)
**Posted swarf G-code changes**: each raster end was retract, swing, re-plunge, then an upright G1 rise; it is now one G0 rise at the lying A/B/C angles, with the lying pose carried through the clearance move. No golden covers swarf output, so none moved. Please run a swarf program through Hub / a real machine (watch the G0 rise at the leaned pose) before marking ready.

Decision: `docs/decisions/48-swarf-exit-rise.md`.

Changelog: Swarf: each raster line now leaves the blade on a rapid that keeps its lying tool angle instead of turning upright through an air link, so a raster end no longer swings the head (air links 34 to 23 on the test blade)

Fixes #48

title: feat(probe): seed the Probe op from a picked face, edge, vertex or round wall
body:
## What changed
A pick on a Probe op now seeds the op's mode, touch directions, expected contact and (for round picks) radius, inside the same undoable `SetOperationGeometry` command, so one Ctrl+Z takes back the pick and the seeded values together. `operation::probe_from_picks(...)` + `CreateOperation` with that pick as the source creates a seeded probe directly.
- **Planar face:** Face touch against the face's outward normal (normal within 1 deg of +-X, +-Y or +Z). The target is the face centroid, or the nearest facet's centroid if the centroid falls in a hole.
- **Straight level top edge:** Edge touch on the one vertical X/Y-facing wall under it; target is the edge midpoint.
- **Vertex:** Outside corner, X/Y directions from the two walls below it. An inside corner is refused.
- **Round wall / closed round rim:** Bore or Boss centre, centre and radius from the same circle fit Circular uses, at rim height. Bore vs Boss: the walls' outward normals mostly point at the axis -> Bore (a hole's wall); away -> Boss.
- **Refused by name, op unchanged:** a face that looks down or is tilted off the axes; a bent, sloped or vertical edge; an inside corner, a corner with a sloped face, or a bottom vertex; a cone or tilted wall, or a rim that isn't round; more than one pick.
- The Geometry tab prints the seed under the pick chip ("Probe from the pick: Face touch toward -Z at (...)").

The seed is written once, at the pick; generation still reads only the typed fields, so a hand edit after the pick is kept until the next pick. No project-format change (the pick is the op's existing saved selection source; the values go into the existing Probe fields). The post logic is untouched. New code is in `crates/app/src/operation/probe_pick.rs` and `probe_pick_round.rs`; `probe_op.rs` (PR #335) and all UI files are untouched.

## Readings
- `probe_pick` 9/9; `circular_pick`, `pick`, `vertex_pick`, `commands_undo`, `area_picks`, `heights_selection` all pass.
- `a_probe_created_from_a_pick_generates_clean`: face, corner and bore probes generate with no stylus-gouge warnings.
- Quick gate (all app suites): green except `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`, red on main (#344 / PR #345).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not pinned: an open curved edge (refused as "not straight") has no fixture; the pick doesn't check a wall is taller than the touch depth - generation's stylus check judges that.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/probe_pick.rs`)
`a_planar_face_seeds_a_face_touch_against_its_normal`, `a_straight_top_edge_seeds_an_edge_touch_on_the_wall_under_it`, `a_vertex_seeds_an_outside_corner_from_its_two_walls`, `a_round_wall_or_rim_seeds_a_bore_or_boss_centre`, `picks_the_probe_cannot_touch_are_refused_by_name`, `the_pick_command_seeds_the_probe_and_one_undo_takes_both_back`, `a_probe_created_from_a_pick_generates_clean`, `other_kinds_are_not_seeded`, `an_inside_corner_is_refused_and_an_outside_one_on_the_l_seeds`

## GUI check (why this stays a draft)
1. Add a Probe op; on its Geometry tab set "Click selects" to Faces and click the top face: Find / Touch toward / Expected contact switch to Face, -Z and the face centroid, and the seed line appears under the chip.
2. Repeat with Edges on a top edge, Vertices on an outside corner, Faces on a bore wall: Edge / Outside corner / Bore centre with its radius.
3. Ctrl+Z once restores both the source and the previous values.
4. Clicking the underside face shows "geometry selection not updated: ... looks down ...".
Posted probe programs now carry the picked target/mode/directions; worth one Hub run of a seeded probe before merging.

Decision: `docs/decisions/171-probe-from-pick.md`.

Changelog: A Probe op seeds from one pick: a face gives a Face touch, a straight top edge an Edge touch, a vertex an outside Corner, a round wall or rim a Bore or Boss centre; picks it can't touch are refused by name

Fixes #171

title: feat(setup): lay the part on a G17/G18/G19 plane from a picked face or two edges
body:
Builds on #341 (merged; #326, per-setup part alignment) - base `main`.

## What changed
- **App, `pick::plane` (new):** `lay_on_plane(world, picks, PlaneLay { plane, flip, place })` reads one flat face or two straight edges in the document frame and returns the setup's part alignment (rigid transform, document -> setup frame). Face: the shortest turn from the outward normal onto +Z (G17) / +Y (G18) / +X (G19), negated with Flip; the antiparallel case is a half turn about the plane's first axis (bottom onto G17 equals the "Flip over X" preset). Two edges: frame to frame, the plane normal onto the axis (outward = away from the parts' centre) and the first edge along X (G17/G18) or Y (G19). Turned about the parts' bounds centre like the #326 presets; "Face to plane level" sets the face (or the first edge's plane) to level 0 on that axis. The landing is checked (turned normal within 1e-9 rad of the axis, by the sine) before anything is returned.
- **Command:** `AlignPartToSetup::lay_on_plane(world, setup, picks, lay)` -> `AlignPartToSetup::new` (#341's door): one undoable command, the stock follows as it does for the presets. The work offset (`setup::wcs_slot`) is never touched; rotated work offsets stay refused.
- **Refused by name:** a curved face (patch), a degenerate face / no area, a vertex, a closed or curved edge, parallel or coincident edges, any other pick count, a pick on the stock or a fixture ("is not the part"), a pick no longer in the model.
- **Shared readers:** `pick::align`'s outward-normal and straight-edge readers take the frame as a parameter (3-2-1 keeps the active setup's view; behaviour unchanged).
- **UI:** each Setups page row gets "Lay on a plane": *Pick face or edges* (arms a view-state draft `State::plane_pick` + Edge mode, so edges and faces both pick; a face replaces the draft, an edge toggles and keeps the last two; draft picks drawn in the violet pick outline), G17/G18/G19 combo, *Flip*, *Face to plane level*, *Apply* (enabled only when the app reads the picks as a plane; the disabled tooltip says why). Apply queues `CommandKind::LayPartOnPlane`; only Apply is a command.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/330-pick-to-plane.md` (absolute in the document frame; row's setup; no-setup = no row, matching #341; edge outward rule; tolerances).

## Readings
- New suite `plane_align`: 9 passed. Normal within 1e-9 rad of each target axis for G17/G18/G19 x flip, on a square block and a block tilted (20, 35, -50) deg; edges: first edge along the plane's first axis within 1e-9 rad; place-on-level: wall corners at level 0 within 1e-7 mm.
- App: setup_align 8, pick 9, wcs_align 5, commands_undo 32, project_roundtrip 68, golden_cl 23 - all pass.
- UI lib (CWD crates/ui): 293 passed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests
- `plane_align`: `a_face_lands_its_outward_normal_on_each_plane_axis`, `the_bottom_onto_g17_is_a_flip_over_x_about_the_centre`, `place_on_level_sets_the_face_onto_the_plane`, `two_edges_set_the_plane_and_the_first_one_runs_along_its_first_axis`, `the_command_writes_the_setup_alignment_and_undo_restores_it`, `a_second_setup_lays_a_different_face_down`, `the_top_face_onto_g17_is_already_how_the_part_sits`, `every_pick_that_sets_no_plane_is_refused_by_name`, `a_curved_face_and_a_curved_edge_are_refused_by_name`
- ui `egui_app::setup_plane_tests`: `the_row_picks_a_face_and_lays_it_on_g17_through_the_command`, `edge_picks_keep_the_last_two_and_parallel_edges_push_nothing`

Not covered by a test: the degenerate-face refusal (feature detection gives no easy fixture for a `FaceKind::Degenerate` face; the code path is guarded) and the viewport ray routing into the draft (the test feeds `plane_pick::take` directly).

title: feat(setup): align the part to a setup's own frame, separate from the work offset
body:
## What changed

A setup can now hold the part aligned - flipped, turned, or as modelled - separate from its work offset (#326, part of #308).

- **Storage:** `SetupDef.part_alignment: Option<Location>` - the rigid transform from the document frame into the setup frame. `None` = "As modelled" (never stored as identity). Only parts (models that are not fixtures) read through it; the setup's stock, work offsets and fixtures already live in the setup frame.
- **Command:** `AlignPartToSetup` (undoable, validated at construction). `new(world, setup, Option<Location>)` takes any rigid transform (the door #330's picks will use); `preset(..)` (As modelled, Flip over X/Y, Turn 90/180/270 about Z) and `angles(.., [x, y, z]°)` turn the part about the centre of its bounds. Quarter turns use exact quaternion components.
- **Stock follows** like it follows `MoveModel` (stock from a part, or a one-part document's stock): a box/cylinder is rebuilt square to the setup frame. A cylinder that would lie on its side, or a following stock shared with another setup, is refused by name. `MoveModel` moves an aligned setup's stock as that setup sees the move. A datum transfer (`CreateSetup` from a setup) carries the alignment.
- **Work offset untouched.** `setup::wcs_slot` and the G-word come from the setup exactly as before (#331); rotated offsets stay refused at post (#315/#325).
- **Generation / stock / sim / post in the setup frame:** op material, Top/Bottom of Model and source-selection heights, the program sim's part, Fit to Models / Fit sides, stock from model, the part-size readout, the viewport's part drawing and picks (active setup's frame).
- **Stamps:** an entity source's pose is digested in the setup frame, and an aligned setup's alignment enters every op stamp of that setup. Nothing is written when as modelled, so no existing stamp moves.
- **Project v53:** `setup.part_alignment {translation, rotation}`; absent = as modelled, so every v52 file loads unchanged; a non-rigid transform is refused as corrupt. Not breaking (nothing loadable before is refused).
- **UI:** Setups page row "Part alignment" - a quick-choice combo plus typed X/Y/Z angles with Apply, queuing `CommandKind::AlignPart`.

## Refused by name in an aligned setup (this slice)

Generation is wired and pinned for **Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive** over a whole model or the stock. Refused at `collect_job` (the one door every generation passes), so an aligned setup never cuts in the unaligned frame:
- every other kind (3D, drilling, multi-axis, turning, ...);
- picked faces/edges as the source; area controls; a 3+2 tilt;
- any non-mill machine (lathe, mill-turn).

The program sim refuses a program spanning setups that hold the part differently (carrying cut stock between alignments is #317). An op generated before an alignment change is Stale and never posts.

## Readings

- Fixture: 40 x 40 x 20 block with a 20 x 20 hole blind to Z 10, stock 60 x 60 x 22 from Z -2, 4 mm end mill, whole-model Contour Z 20 -> 12.
- As modelled the cut levels run the hole ring at 8 mm and the outer ring at 22 mm. Flipped over X (stored rotation exactly `[1, 0, 0, 0]`, translation `(0, 0, 20)` = about the part centre Z 10): only the outer ring at 22 mm - Z 12..20 is the former bottom, solid. Posts at G54.
- The stock follows square: 60 x 60 x 22 now from Z 0 (the 2 mm under the part is 2 mm over it). A Turn 90 about Z lays a 60 x 40 block 40 x 60.
- Flip then As modelled: the op is Ok again without regenerating, and the regenerated program is byte-identical.

`crates/app/tests/setup_align.rs` (new):
- `as_modelled_is_byte_identical_and_the_stamp_returns_fresh`
- `a_flipped_setup_contours_the_former_bottom_and_posts_in_its_frame`

- `two_setups_hold_the_part_differently_without_touching_each_other`
- `unverified_kinds_and_picks_are_refused_by_name_in_an_aligned_setup`
- `the_alignment_round_trips_and_older_files_load_as_modelled`
- `the_program_sim_refuses_by_name_across_differently_held_setups`
- `the_pocket_and_face_kinds_cut_the_flipped_part_and_post`

`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_align_tests.rs` (new):

title: feat(motion): the rotary wrap turns its seam clear of a D-flat instead of refusing it
body:
## What changed

Since #54 / PR #210, the rotary wrap refused by name a non-turned feature (a D-flat or keyway) that crossed its seam, so the user had to rotate the work. Now, when the default seam (the basis' ±π branch) is refused, the wrap looks for a seam angle itself:

- **Candidates** are the midpoints of the gaps between vertex azimuth columns. Each is judged by the unchanged #54/#228 seam law. A facet straddles a candidate when the candidate lies inside the shortest arc holding its off-axis vertices; one sweep hands every candidate its straddlers.
- **The pick** is the turned candidate farthest from any refused one, which on a D-flat is opposite the flat. Ties go to the candidate nearest the default seam.
- **The wrap** turns the azimuth basis about the axis by that angle and lays the development out again. The turned sheet is judged again before anything is cut. The world exit maps back through the same turned basis, so only the split moves and every point is cut at its true azimuth.
- **Unchanged outputs:** when the default seam is already turned it is kept, so existing wraps are byte-identical. No golden changed.
- **The refusal** happens only when no angle works (a feature all the way round), and says so by name. The search also refuses by name after handing out 20M straddler vertices, so a very dense mesh can't hang it.

Code: new `rotary_seam_angle.rs` (the search) and `rotary_sheet.rs` (the lap loop moved out of `rotary_offset.rs`, which shrinks from 401 to about 317 lines; plus `Basis::turned` and `polar`). `rotary_seam.rs` is split into `seam_columns` (the verdict) and `seam_refusal` (the error). Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/226-wrap-seam-angle.md`.

## Readings

- All 36 off-centre flat placements wrap with 0 cut tips inside the true cross-section. Channel tips stand at the flat's true azimuth.
- A facet spread over more than half a turn (for example a non-fan end cap) makes the search pessimistic. Such a part may still be refused, but never unsafely, because the full development is judged again.
- Only Offset rings is checked for tips on world output. The Adaptive case checks that the developed channel exists; the Adaptive heavy lane (`rotary_adaptive` ignored tests) was not run.

## Pinning tests (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_dflat.rs`)

- `an_off_centre_flat_across_the_seam_never_puts_a_tip_in_the_part`: all 36 placements now wrap.
- `a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement`: no refusal escape; tips at the flat's azimuth.
- `a_flat_channel_across_the_default_seam_develops_under_adaptive_and_rings` replaces `a_flat_channel_across_the_seam_is_refused_by_name_before_the_wrap`.
- `a_feature_all_the_way_round_is_still_refused_by_name` (new).
- Unit tests: `the_shortest_arc_runs_across_the_zero_azimuth`, `the_candidates_include_the_gap_across_zero`.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): motion suites green apart from the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (pre-existing). Also run: app `rotary_verify`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `project_roundtrip`, `operations` (green). clippy `-p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: The rotary wrap turns its seam clear of a D-flat or keyway, so a flatted bar roughs in any placement; only a feature all the way round is refused (#226)

Fixes #226

title: feat(turning): a large keyway or flat no longer refuses a turned part
body:
## What changed

The lathe axis fit claims an axis only when 90 % of the answering surface meets the plain least-squares line, and the #71 robust pass only ran after that gate. A large keyway or flat failed the gate before the robust pass saw it. Example: a 10 x 20 mm keyway 6 mm deep on a D20 shaft drags the plain line 0.57 mm off, about twice the 0.29 mm band. A 50 mm keyway takes 17 % of the surface. Both were refused with "the model's normals share no rotation axis".

- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_consensus.rs`. It is a fallback that runs **only when no candidate passes the plain gate**, so every part that already fitted gets exactly the same fit, and no golden changes. For each candidate direction, it keeps the facets whose normal lines meet the line within a cut scaled by the MAD (the kept facets' scatter). It refits on them and at least halves the cut each round, down to the sagitta band. The direction is held while the set settles, so a prism's single pencil of lines can't swing it (the #208 plate-with-boss case stays refused).
- The consensus line must be met by **75 %** of the answering surface (`CONSENSUS_SHARE`), against the plain 90 %. The coarseness and pencil gates are unchanged. It then takes the existing robust reweighting at the same share (`reweigh` / `judge_at` take the share as a parameter).
- `spindle_law.rs`: the refusal text moved into `refusal()`, so the untrusted ("biased fit") message is unit-tested.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/113-lathe-axis-fit.md`.

## Readings

- Deep 20 mm keyway: the plain line is 0.57 mm off and the consensus fit is exact, with 4.7 % set aside. Long keyway: 17 % set aside.
- An off-axis lump of 30 % of the surface and a box are still refused by name.
- **Owner's call:** the 75 % share sits between the robust pass's 50 % backstop and the plain 90 %.
- A block standing on a meridian passes, as it already did under the plain gate: its walls square to the axis meet it like flats. Turning follows the part's outline about the axis, so the block is left standing, and the note names its share.
- `axis.rs` is 411 lines, just over the ~400 guideline. Most of the new code is in the new module.

## Pinning tests

- motion (`axis_consensus_tests`): `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_fits_on_the_true_axis`, `a_long_keyway_over_a_tenth_of_the_surface_fits`, `a_shaft_with_a_large_off_axis_lump_is_still_refused_by_name`, `a_box_is_still_refused_by_name`
- app (`lathe_spindle_keyed`): `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_on_g54_passes_the_spindle_law_and_generates`, `a_deep_twenty_mm_keyway_off_g54_is_refused_as_misplaced`, `a_shaft_with_a_large_off_axis_lump_is_still_refused_by_name`
- app unit (`spindle_law_tests`): `an_untrusted_fit_is_refused_as_biased_naming_its_share`, `an_untrusted_fit_never_shows_a_zero_share`, `a_trusted_fit_off_the_spindle_is_refused_as_misplaced`

Both deep-keyway app tests fail with the motion change removed.

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): motion and app suites green apart from the known `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests, pre-existing). clippy `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Changelog: A lathe part with a large keyway or flat (over a tenth of its turned surface, or one that pulled the plain axis fit off) is read about its revolved surface and turns, with the set-aside share named; parts mostly not revolved are still refused (#113)

Fixes #113

title: feat(sim): judge the probe's stylus stem and body in the protected-move law
body:
## What changed

The probe op's protected-move law judged only the stylus ball (`probe_op::stylus_hits`). The stylus stem above the ball and the probe body were never checked. So a deep edge or corner touch beside a taller wall, or a touch under an overhang, could pass while the stem or body met the part.

- `probe_op::stylus_cutter(tool)` describes the probe as a stack the cutters' solid law can read. The ball is the cutting atom. The stem is the shank band at the ball's radius, up to the stylus length. The body and any holder form one band at the wider radius.
- `probe_op::stylus_reach_hits` runs the existing `verify::solid_hits` over every move, through its public seam with no copy. A stem or body meeting the part is a `ShankHit { part: true }`, and a rapid meeting it is `RapidInStock`. Both block the post. Only the ball may touch, so the expected contact excuses nothing above it, and a move the ball check already convicted isn't reported twice. The allowance is the existing `STYLUS_SLACK` (0.01 mm), so a stem riding tangent to the wall it touches stays clean.
- `generate_probe` adds these warnings to the ball check's.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/172-probe-shank-sweep.md`. No new warning kind: `ShankHit` is reused, because a new variant would change the project file format.

## Readings

- `Tool` has no stylus-diameter field, so the stem is modelled at the ball's radius. Real stems are thinner, so this can only over-report, never miss a hit. Body and holder share one band at the wider radius, which is also conservative.
- No clean-bore fixture: the shape primitives can't build a block with a hole. The faceted-bore tangent maths matches the ball check, which already passes there.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/probe_reach.rs`, new suite)

- `a_stem_that_meets_an_overhang_is_a_shank_hit`
- `a_body_that_meets_a_tall_wall_is_a_shank_hit`
- `clean_touches_stay_clean_under_the_reach_law`
- `the_stylus_stack_is_ball_then_stem_then_body`
- `a_short_stylus_deep_on_the_stock_edge_is_refused_by_the_op`

The existing `probe_op` suite passes 11/11. Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS) is green. clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: Probe op: the stylus stem and the probe body are judged against the part on every probe move; a touch whose ball clears but whose stem or body meets a wall is refused as a shank hit (#172)

Fixes #172

title: feat(post): comment the setup, operation and tool in posted programs
body:
## What changed

Every built-in post now writes three kinds of program comment, on by default:

- the **setup** name, once, where its first section opens;
- each **operation**'s name, kind and work offset, at its preamble;
- each **tool**'s number, name, kind, diameter and corner radius, just before its tool call.

Pieces:

- **Stream** (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs`): four optional PARAMs, `OperationKind`, `SetupName`, `ToolKind` and `ToolCornerRadius`. Each is written only when it has a value, so a legacy stream or a user's .cps script that doesn't know them behaves as before. Documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- **App** (`posting::op_streams`): fills them from the operation's kind label, its effective setup, and the tool's kind and corner radius.
- **Posts** (all seven under `assets/posts/`): a small, original "comments" block in each script. User text is cleaned per dialect: printable ASCII only, capped at 40 characters; `( ) % ;` become spaces, and Heidenhain also drops `*`. Every comment starts with our own keyword, so a user's name can't turn into an active comment such as LinuxCNC's `(MSG,`.

Sample lines:

| Dialect | Comments |
|---|---|
| Fanuc / Haas / Mazak / Tormach | `(SETUP: Setup1)` `(OPERATION: Contour1 - 2D CONTOUR - G54)` `(T01 EM-0600-4FL - FLAT END MILL D6)` |
| Sinumerik | `; OPERATION: Contour1 - 2D CONTOUR - G54` (unnumbered, like its machine-name line) |
| Heidenhain DIN/ISO | `N10 ; OPERATION: Plane arcs*` (numbered block; no work-offset word, since this post selects the active preset) |
| Fanuc lathe | `(T0101 TN-1600-0R8 - TURNING INSERT)` (no diameter for blades) |

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/257-gcode-comments.md`. The on/off post property is left to #258 / PR #302, which own the Post dialog. No UI is touched here.

## Readings

- 26 goldens regenerated (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`). A script check confirmed only comment lines were added (50 in all): stripping them gives back each old file byte for byte. The one other change is Heidenhain's block numbers shifting. The 78 legacy `.cl` conformance goldens are unchanged, because their streams carry no PARAM or TOOL records.
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` was already 491 lines and is now about 518. Not split in this PR.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/program_comments.rs`, new)

- `every_mill_dialect_comments_the_setup_operation_and_tool_in_its_own_syntax`
- `user_text_never_breaks_a_comment`
- `a_stream_without_the_commentary_params_writes_no_comment`
- `a_document_posts_its_setup_operation_kind_and_tool_kind`

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS) green (post + app suites); ui lib tests that post (egui_app::tests, after_op_tests) green except the known `headless_run_succeeds`. 65 post-related test binaries pass (549 tests). clippy `-p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Needs a check on a real control

Every posted program changes. Before ready: a Hub / simulator run and a dry run on a real machine. The Heidenhain `N.. ; text*` form especially hasn't been tried on a TNC; the decision file names the fallbacks.

Changelog: Posted programs carry comments naming the setup, each operation (name, kind, work offset) and each tool (number, name, kind, diameter, corner radius) in every built-in dialect's own comment syntax (#257)

Fixes #257

title: fix(post): refuse a non-finite work-offset placement by name
body:
## What changed

A work offset whose placement is non-finite (NaN or infinite origin or rotation, or a zero-norm rotation quaternion) used to slip past the rotated-offset post refusal: its measured angle came out as 0, so it posted as unrotated. Such an offset is now refused by name at every entry point:

- **Post check** (`posting_wcs_rotation.rs`): a new `offset_frame(&Location)` sorts a placement into `Square` / `Rotated` / `NonFinite`. A `NonFinite` offset gets its own refusal: `work offset G54 has a non-finite placement (origin or rotation) - re-place the offset before posting (operations: ...)`.
- **`SetWcsOrigin`**: it already refused these values; its messages now name the slot (`work offset G55: rotation must be finite ...`).
- **Project load** (`project/validate.rs`): a WCS row with a non-finite translation or rotation, or an all-zero rotation, is refused as corrupt by name. Before, the loader quietly turned an all-zero rotation into the identity.
- **3-2-1 align**: no change needed. It refuses a non-finite frame already and writes through `SetWcsOrigin`.
- **Setup sheet**: a rotated offset now gets a line under its translation, `rotated 90.000 deg about Z - the post refuses a rotated offset`. A non-finite one says so too. Unrotated offsets print exactly as before.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/327-nonfinite-wcs-rotation.md`.

## Readings

- A NaN rotation can't reach the world through the normal paths: the command refuses it, and `model::set_transform` replaces it with the identity. So the post-check refusal is a backstop, and its tests write the bad value onto the offset entity directly.
- JSON can't encode NaN or infinity, so the load test covers the all-zero rotation.
- Overlap with draft PR #331: it edits one line of `posting_wcs_rotation.rs` (the `wcs_slot(...)` call) next to lines this PR changes, and the "program offset" lines of `render_wcs`, which this PR leaves alone. Expect a small merge in `posting_wcs_rotation.rs`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/rotated_wcs.rs`)

- `set_wcs_origin_refuses_a_non_finite_placement_by_slot`
- `a_non_finite_offset_rotation_is_refused_by_the_post_gate`
- `a_non_finite_offset_origin_is_refused_by_the_post_gate`
- `project_load_refuses_a_degenerate_offset_rotation`
- `the_setup_sheet_states_the_offset_rotation`

Gate: `scripts/gate.sh quick` (macOS): every app suite passes. One run of `project_roundtrip` aborted (SIGABRT) while three gates shared the machine; it was then 30/30 green run alone, and this diff does not touch that suite (noted as a possible pre-existing flake). clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. Suites run: rotated_wcs, setup_sheet, setup_wcs, project_roundtrip, wcs_align, posting, commands_undo, setups, face_origin, app lib.

title: fix(setup)!: the setup defines the work offset, not each height
body:
## What changed
- **Model:** `HeightReference::WorkOffset` names no slot any more. It resolves through `setup::wcs_slot(world, setup)` (the setup's pick, else G54). That is the same law the post uses, so an operation can't disagree with its setup. `posting::wcs_context` and `wcs_slot` no longer take the op's params. The #196 post refusal for "height on another slot than the pick" is removed because that state can't be built any more. The one-file shared-word refusal stays.
- **Heights page:** the Work offset reference no longer has a WCS combo. It shows a read-only "Work offset" row, e.g. `G55 (setup Setup1 - set on the Setups page)`, with a hover hint.
- **Setups page / setup sheet:** the unpicked entry was "Auto (from heights, else G54)" and is now "G54 (default)". The sheet now says `program offset: G54 (the default - not picked)`. The viewport plane chip shows the setup's G-word.
- **Project v52 + migration** (`crates/app/src/project/wcs_migrate.rs`). It runs before any world write. For each setup it collects every slot in use: the pick, each op's v51 posted slot, and every height's slot (suppressed ops included).
  - **One slot:** the slot moves onto the setup's `work_offset` (G54 stays unwritten). Stamps and posts don't change.
  - **Several slots:** the load is refused by name (`ProjectError::WorkOffsetConflict`). The message lists each op with its slots, e.g. `setup Setup1: Face1 (G55); Face2 (G56)`.
  - **No setup to hold the pick:** documents without setups load if everything is G54; any other slot is refused by name.
  - **v52 files:** a height that carries a slot is refused as corrupt. The MCP params door refuses one too.
- **Stamp:** a work-offset height feeds the resolved setup slot into the stamp. Migrated ops keep bit-identical stamps, so goldens don't change.
- Why the load is refused rather than loaded with a post refusal is in `docs/decisions/329-setup-defines-wcs.md`. Loading would mean either keeping per-height slots in memory or re-pointing the op on its next regeneration.

## Readings / tests (debug, worktree target)
- New `crates/app/tests/setup_defines_wcs.rs` (4 tests):
  - agreeing v51 file (per-height G55): the setup picks G55, the post is byte-identical and the resave equals the v52 save; a G54 file stays unpicked
  - conflicting setup: refused by name (G55/G56, G55/G54, and a picked setup with another height slot)
  - document without setups: refused by name
  - v52 height carrying a slot: refused as corrupt
- `setup_wcs::work_offset_heights_follow_the_setups_pick_and_its_undo`: picking G56 moves every work-offset height and stales the op; undo moves them back and redo moves them again. This replaces the removed #196 conflict test.
- ui lib `egui_app::setup_wcs_tests::the_heights_page_shows_the_setups_offset_with_no_wcs_choice`: one combo only (From), and the row follows the setup's pick. Run from CWD `crates/ui`: 286 passed, 0 failed.
- Green: setup_wcs, rotated_wcs, wcs_align, posting, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl, fanuc_post, heights, heights_selection, setups, setup_sheet, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_post_refusals, heidenhain_block_form, mcp, operations, app lib, ui operations. No golden or snapshot changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not exercised: the GUI by hand, the release heavy lanes, and batch suites outside the list above.

Changelog: A height measured from the work offset now reads its setup's offset (picked on the Setups page); the Heights page no longer offers a per-height WCS choice, and older projects migrate their slot onto the setup, or are refused by name when one setup's operations used different offsets (project v52) (#329)

title: feat(setup): pick the work offset (G54-G59) a setup posts at
body:
## What changed

A setup now picks the work offset its program runs in (G54..G59), builds on #325 (merged).

- **Storage:** `SetupDef.work_offset: Option<usize>`. `None` = **Auto**, the inferred per-operation law every older document posted with (first slot the op's heights reference, else G54). New setups also start on Auto, so existing fixtures and goldens post byte-identically.
- **One law:** `posting::wcs_slot::wcs_slot(world, setup, params)` reads the setup's pick first. `wcs_context` and all of its callers follow it (generation, stamp, spindle law, machine travel check, single-file / per-op / script post, the #315 rotation clause).
- **Command:** `SetSetupWorkOffset`, undoable and validated at construction (setup exists, slot < 6, not the current value). A datum transfer copies the source's pick.
- **UI:** the Setups page has a "Work offset" combo under each setup (Auto, G54..G59). It queues the command and never writes the world itself.
- **Project v51:** the setup payload carries `"work_offset": "G55"`, left out when nothing is picked. v50 files step up with absent = Auto. An unknown word is a corrupt file. The version bump makes older readers refuse the file instead of posting a G55 setup at G54.
- **Refusals by name:**
  - In the verification gate: an op whose heights are measured from a different slot than its setup's pick (`Face1: its heights are measured from G56 but setup Setup1 posts at G55 - ...`).
  - In the one-file / script post: two setups posting the same word from different placements (`setups Setup1 and Setup2 both post at G54 from different placements ... pick another work offset for Setup2 ..., or post one file per operation`). Per-op files are exempt because each file belongs to one setup.
  - Note: the one-file refusal also catches documents that pick nothing. Before this change they posted that case silently.
- **Setup sheet:** WCS OFFSETS ends with `program offset: G55 (picked for this setup)` or `program offset: per operation - ... (not picked)`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/196-setup-wcs.md`

## Readings

- A G55 pick at (10, 20, 5) gives the same program as G54 at the origin except for the G-word and the coordinates. Every X/Y/Z in the program (not counting the G28 home lines) shifts by exactly (-10, -20, -5).
- Milling stamps do not read the program origin, so a pick leaves milling paths fresh. Turning kinds go stale through the spindle-origin stamp (#62), as they did before.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs` (new, 7 tests):
  - `a_picked_offset_posts_its_word_and_moves_coordinates_by_exactly_the_offset`
  - `the_pick_undoes_and_redoes_exactly`
  - `a_datum_transfer_carries_the_pick`
  - `the_pick_round_trips_and_old_files_read_the_inferred_law`
  - `a_height_on_another_slot_than_the_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `two_setups_on_one_word_from_different_placements_refuse_one_file`
  - `the_setup_sheet_names_the_program_offset`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_tests.rs`:
  - `the_picker_sets_the_setups_work_offset_through_the_command`: kittest; combo click, G55, then Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y.
  - `a_refused_pick_changes_nothing_and_says_why`
- `probe_op`: the version pin is updated from 50 to 51.

## Quick gate (local, debug)

- **App suites, all green:** posting, setups, wcs_align, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl (goldens unchanged), fanuc_post, rotated_wcs, setup_sheet, probe_op, lathe_spindle_law, machine, per_op_files, scripting, setup_wcs, plus the app lib.
- **UI lib (CWD crates/ui):** 287 tests, all green. No snapshot changed: the picker only draws on a document that has setups.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: A setup picks its work offset (G54-G59, default Auto = inferred per operation) on the Setups page; every op of the setup posts at it, the setup sheet names it, and conflicting picks are refused by name (project v51)

Fixes #196

title: fix(post): refuse a rotated work offset by name instead of posting it unrotated
body:
## What changed
- New verification-gate clause `posting::wcs_rotation::rotated_wcs_problems` (`crates/app/src/posting_wcs_rotation.rs`), called from `verification_report`, so the one-file post, the per-op post and the script API all refuse. It produces one line per rotated offset entity a posted op uses:
  `setup Setup1: its work offset G54 is rotated 90.000 deg about Z; posting a rotated work offset is not supported yet - re-align it without rotation or post from an unrotated setup (operations: Face1)` (in a legacy document with no setups it reads `work offset G54 is rotated ...`).
- The op-to-slot law moved into `wcs_rotation::wcs_slot`. `wcs_context` and the clause both read it, so the gate judges exactly the offset that gets posted.
- Tolerance: an angle (`2*atan2(|xyz|,|w|)`) of at most 1e-9 rad counts as unrotated, so identity offsets post byte-identical.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/315-rotated-wcs.md`. G68/G68.2, CYCLE800/ROT, PLANE/CYCL 10 and baking the rotation into coordinates were all set aside for now because none is trivially verifiable. That is step 3 of #315.

## Readings
- Reproduced first. With the clause disabled, a G54 turned 90 deg about Z posts without error (`a_rotated_work_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `a_setups_rotated_offset_names_the_setup` and `an_unrotated_offset_posts_exactly_as_before` fail at the `expect_err`). The record stream is identical to the stream for the square offset (`the_post_stream_carries_no_offset_rotation`).
- Quick gate, debug, all green: posting 17, conformance 6, fanuc_post 8, golden_cl 23, per_op_files 9, post_not_judged 4, setups 11, wcs_align 5, probe_op 11, tormach_post 10, lathe_post 7, scripting 17, machine 32, drilling_cross_stock 8, rotary_verify 9, rotated_wcs 4. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean. No golden changed.

## Pinning tests
`crates/app/tests/rotated_wcs.rs`: `the_post_stream_carries_no_offset_rotation`, `a_rotated_work_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `a_setups_rotated_offset_names_the_setup`, `an_unrotated_offset_posts_exactly_as_before`.

Fixes #315

title: feat(app): MCP detect_holes, through the app's own Detect holes rule
body:
A new MCP tool, `detect_holes {name}`, fills a Drill, Bore or Thread operation's hole list from its source model, through the same rule as the app's Detect holes button. Before, an agent's drill on a model with holes always refused "no holes to drill".

### What was wrong (`main` 8f30bee and 8cf3c90)

- The drilling kinds machine only the holes stored in their parameters. Only the UI's `State::detect_holes` filled them; the MCP tool table had nothing equivalent.
- Reproduced through `camcraft-cli mcp` on `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` (see #312).

### What changed

- `operation::detect_holes(world, name, params, setup, src)` (`operation/material.rs`): the rule moved out of the UI unchanged. It reads the source now (`holes_of`), fills whichever list the kind has, adds the drill's radial list on a turret machine (`cross_holes_of`), and refuses by name.
- `State::detect_holes` calls it: the same refusal texts and the same draft rule, with 55 lines of duplicated logic gone.
- MCP `detect_holes`: calls it and executes one undoable `EditOperationParams`. It answers `{operation, holes, radial_holes, status}`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/312-mcp-detect-holes.md`.

### Tests

- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs`: `detect_holes_fills_a_drill_from_its_model_and_undo_empties_it`. A 20 mm disc with a 6 mm blind bore, as STL (the bore suites' `common::bore::revolve`):
  - the drill refuses "no holes" before detection;
  - `detect_holes` finds 1 axial and 0 radial holes, stored in the drill's params;
  - the drill generates;
  - two undos (the generation, then the detection) empty the list;
  - a Face op is refused "not a drilling operation".
- `handshake_and_tool_list` now expects `detect_holes`.
- With the tool row taken back out (`git stash` of `tools.rs`), the new test fails: "unknown tool 'detect_holes'". The UI's `detect_holes_refuses_recognizes_and_undo_empties_again` passes through the shared rule.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8cf3c90 plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3`): app lib, `mcp`, `turning`, `turning_profile` (104 pass), and ui lib, `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell` (366 pass, 2 ignored).

title: fix(motion): distinguish concave returns from inter-hole gaps
body:
## Summary

Fix facing's false "two holes" refusal on concave cutouts. A missing scanline piece does not prove a narrow strip between separate holes: both crossings can belong to a return of the same boundary.

- Retain boundary-loop identity with each crossing and require distinct boundaries, a positive gap no wider than the cutter, and a missing row piece before issuing the inter-hole refusal.
- Preserve the existing radius-grown clipping, row geometry, swept-area leftover notes, and post-verification. Concave returns remain clipped; they are not driven through to manufacture a successful path.
- Retain genuinely narrow and exactly-tool-width inter-hole refusals. Add wide/narrow U-notch regressions in both cutting directions, including cutter-radius-clearance checks.
- Record the decision in `docs/decisions/260-facing-gap.md`.

## Readings and diagnosis

The #260 report and attached `cutouts.camproj`, the facing generator and hole clipping code, `Region`'s normalized-loop contract, and the repository contribution/test rules. The reported 15.15 mm gap and a later 2.65 mm gap are concave returns of individual cutouts, not separate holes. A width-only guard was insufficient; boundary identity is necessary. No vendor implementation or assets were consulted.

## Validation

Verified commit: `b3dd4934090d6d30e17a1130939f6789799f8f2a` (tree `3d36ac1b75e3224022cdead91dbd77ad22baa366`), based on `1e60b2399dff677d9f44b143a24e626d268340f0`.

Native Windows/MSVC checks:

- Canonical `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -Base 1e60b2399dff677d9f44b143a24e626d268340f0`: **173 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**, native exit 0. Motion library plus `center_cut_owed`, `face_blend`, `face_concave_holes`, and `face_holes`; gate-created logs and assertion summaries verified.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/motion/tests/face_concave_holes.rs` and whitespace checks: passed.
- Pinning tests: `a_wide_concave_gap_generates_and_reports_the_unfaced_return`, `a_narrow_concave_return_is_not_a_gap_between_separate_holes`, and `a_gap_exactly_one_tool_wide_still_refuses_when_no_row_piece_fits`. These are included in the quick-gate count above.
- Sensitivity: the exact narrow-notch regression fails against the prior diameter-only implementation, then passes with boundary identity restored.
- An asserted temporary app probe loaded the original public attachment and generated default Lift facing: **725 moves**, with the truthful **1653.05 mm^2 unfaced** and lift-over-holes notes. Trace, Through, and Contour controls also generated. The fixture's existing rotated-stock/rapid-law diagnostics were retained, not suppressed.
- Independent static review: passed, no actionable findings.

## Limits

This fixes false rejection, not complete facing coverage: material reported unfaced remains unfaced. No Linux/macOS execution, interactive GUI test, full batch/release/heavy lanes, or real-machine validation is claimed. No workflow was dispatched, release produced, or NC output transferred to a machine. Broader #241 selection/box-picking symptoms and #261 error-path visualization are outside this change.

Changelog: Facing distinguishes concave returns within one cutout from genuinely narrow gaps between separate hole boundaries, preserving clipping and unfaced-area notes.

Fixes #260

title: fix(app): STEP import reads the file's length unit
body:
STEP import now reads the file's declared length unit and converts to millimetres. A part saved in metres or inches imports at its true size, instead of having its numbers read as millimetres.

### What was wrong (`main` 8b0d784)

- `geometry/import/step.rs` tessellated the shells and kept every coordinate as millimetres. Nothing in `crates/` read a STEP `LENGTH_UNIT`.
- The repo's own `testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` (`CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('METRE', ..)`) imported 0.0647 mm wide. An inch export would import 25.4 times too small, then generate, verify and post at that size.

### What changed

- New `geometry/import/step_units.rs`: `mm_per_unit` reads every representation context's `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and resolves its `LENGTH_UNIT`:
  - an `SI_UNIT(prefix, .METRE.)` by its prefix (`$` is the metre; KILO through NANO);
  - a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT(name, #m)` by its `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` value times that measure's own unit, so `'INCH'` -> 25.4 x millimetre.
- `step::parse` reads the unit before tessellating and scales the facets to millimetres afterwards. That's safe because the tolerance schedule is relative to each shell's extent, so the mesh quality is the same in any unit.
- Refused by name (an `ImportError::Step`): a unit this reader can't convert, and contexts that state two different length units. A file with no unit context keeps millimetres, as before.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/306-step-units.md`.

### Tests

- `crates/app/tests/import.rs`:
  - `a_step_file_in_metres_imports_at_its_size_in_millimetres`: the AP214 sample is 60-70 mm wide.
  - `a_step_file_in_millimetres_keeps_its_numbers`: Milling-test's max corner is unchanged.
- `step_units::tests` (4): SI prefixes (milli, centi, none); an inch conversion through a measure is 25.4; no unit context keeps mm; two disagreeing contexts and an unknown prefix (`EXA`) refuse by name.
- With `step.rs` and `mod.rs` checked out from `main`, `a_step_file_in_metres...` fails ("the part is 0.06468733557556011 mm wide"), and the millimetre pin passes either way.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8b0d784 plus this branch)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (app lib, `large_models`, `stock_export`), plus the whole `import` suite: 92 + 22 + 3 + 2 pass, 1 ignored.
- Every other app suite that imports a STEP fixture: `area_controls`, `area_open`, `commands_undo`, `heights_selection`, `lead_approach`, `level_links`, `pick_agnostic`, `pocket3d_hsm`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `solid_law`, `wall_arc_entry`. 97 pass, 3 ignored. `box.step` and `Milling-test.step` both declare millimetres, so their sizes don't move.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- A note on how this was checked: the first gate run reused another worktree's build (a shared `target` folder with older file times) and compiled none of this code. I touched every source in this worktree and confirmed with `cargo test -- --list` that the new tests were built before the runs above.
- Not run: the windowed app, Linux, macOS, and a real inch STEP export. The inch path is covered by the unit test's conversion chain, not by an exported file.

Changelog: STEP import reads the file's length unit, so a part saved in inches or metres imports at its true size; a unit it can't read is refused by name (#306)

Fixes #306
