title: fix(cl): the text dump, is_prismatic and TiltedFrame keep the stated spindle C
body:
The CL text dump, `Toolpath::is_prismatic` and `TiltedFrame::world_path` now keep a move's stated spindle C (`Move::rotary`, #33). Before, all three dropped or ignored it.

### What was wrong (`main` 8b0d784)

- `cl::text::to_text` wrote a C-live path without its C angle, and `from_text` had no word to read one. A C-live cut written through the headless binaries' dump (#279) read back as a 3-axis path cutting somewhere else.
- `is_prismatic` looked only at the tool axis, so a C-live path counted as prismatic, and the dump wrote it as v1/v2.
- `TiltedFrame::world_path` rebuilt every move with `rotary: None`.

### What changed

- `to_text` writes ` SC<millidegrees>` after any pose letters, the spelling the app's golden writer (`crates/app/tests/common`) already uses. `from_text` reads it back through `Move::with_rotary`. The reader matches the two-letter `SC` before the one-letter words, so it can't be taken for the arc sense `S`. A path with no C dumps byte for byte as before.
- `is_prismatic` is false when any move states a C, so the dump (and the golden writer, which reads the same method) writes v4.
- `world_path` copies `rotary` onto every move it maps, chords included. No tilted kind is C-stamped today (the rotary kinds take no tilt, `OpParams::tilt`), so this keeps the angle rather than refusing. Why, and what was dropped, is in `docs/decisions/295-cl-text-rotary.md`.
- No golden holds an `SC` word, so none moved.

### Tests (`crates/cl/src/cl/tests.rs`)

- `a_stated_spindle_c_is_not_a_prismatic_path`
- `the_text_dump_round_trips_a_stated_spindle_c`: v4 header; ` SC-90500` / ` SC-450250` on the moves; read back to -90.5 / -450.25 deg; nothing else moves; a path with no C has no `SC`.
- `a_frame_keeps_a_stated_spindle_c_on_every_move_it_maps`: an upright frame and a 30-degree tilted one.
- With `path.rs`, `text.rs` and `frame.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of those files only), all three fail: "assertion failed: !c_live().is_prismatic()", "C None, want -90.5", and "a C-live path is not prismatic, so v4: ; HSMW-CL v1 ...".

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8b0d784 plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff, which for a `cl` change is every suite of every crate except the four slow binaries (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because other sessions had the CPU near 100%): 2472 pass, 29 ignored, 3 fail.
- The 3 failures are the ui pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), with the same pixel counts as clean `main` on this machine (1544, 1815, 2080). The owner's reviewer saw them pass on its own machine (#276's review).

title: fix(motion): a deburr leaves each edge run straight up before travelling
body:
A deburr now leaves each edge run straight up to the clearance plane before it travels to the next. It used to rapid diagonally from cutting depth, with the cone still in the break, up and across the part.

### What was wrong

- `finishing3d::deburr` opened every run with `Rapid` to `(next start, clearance)` from wherever the previous run ended: the tip `drop` below the edge, the cone touching the break it just cut. Only the last run got a vertical retract.
- On `main` 8f30bee, the brick from `operations.rs`'s deburr test (stock = the brick, `CM-0600-90`, width 2, window z 6..8) gives `Rapid (20,-10,8) -> (-20,10,25)`. Verify convicts `RapidInStock` at moves 3, 8 and 13, so the post is blocked.

### What changed

- `deburr::retract`: a vertical rapid from where the path stands to the clearance plane, or nothing when it's already there. It runs before every run's traverse and once at the end, replacing the old inline final retract, so the path's end is unchanged.
- Cut moves don't change. The existing deburr tests compare cut points and pass as before. No golden holds a deburr path.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/304-deburr-retract.md` (a feed retract, and a retract plane, were considered and dropped).

### Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs`: `every_run_leaves_its_cut_straight_up_before_the_next_traverse`. A closed box rides as several runs, and every rapid that starts below clearance is vertical and ends at clearance.
- New `crates/app/tests/deburr_links.rs`: `a_deburr_on_a_finished_brick_links_its_runs_without_a_rapid_in_stock`. Through the commands, on a finished part: no `RapidInStock`, and no diagonal rapid from cutting depth.
- With `deburr.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of that file only), both fail: "rapid 10 leaves cutting depth diagonally: (40, 0, -12) -> (0, 20, 20)", and "a link rapids through the part: [RapidInStock { at: 3 }, RapidInStock { at: 8 }, RapidInStock { at: 13 }]".

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 4`): motion lib plus `deburr` (157 tests), app `deburr_links`. All pass.
- Every app suite that creates a Deburr operation, too: `operations`, `area_controls`, `project_roundtrip`, `ribbon`, `tool_law`, `probe_op`. With `deburr_links`, 225 pass and 6 ignored (ignored on `main` too).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the windowed app, Linux, macOS.
- Not fixed here: the deburr's intended break still reads as a gouge to the post gate (#303), so a deburr still can't post until that's decided. This PR removes the part of the refusal that was a real motion fault.

title: fix(ui): the Post dialog opens where the document last posted
body:
The Post dialog now opens where this document last posted, proposing the same file, or beside the saved project as `<project name>.nc`. It used to open with no folder and `program.nc` every time.

### What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/post_file.rs`: `post_target(last_post, project)` is the rule, and `for_document(&State)` feeds it the G-code viewer's file (the last successful post) and `State::project_path`.
  - Folder: the last post's, else the project's, else none (left to the OS).
  - Name: the last post's file name, else `<project stem>.nc`, else `program.nc`.
- `state.rs::post_program_dialog` takes that target: `set_directory` when there is a folder, and `set_file_name` from the target.
- The remembered file is `PostView::path`, which New and Open already clear, so a new document never inherits another one's folder. A refused post writes nothing and doesn't move it.
- One change from my claim on #258: the last post's name comes before the project's, so posting again after an edit proposes the file the shop already loads. The project name is the fallback for a document's first post. Reasons and dropped options (saving the folder in the project file) are in `docs/decisions/258-post-output-file.md`.

### Tests (`post_file::tests`, ui lib)

- `a_new_unsaved_document_proposes_program_nc_and_no_folder`
- `a_saved_project_proposes_its_own_name_in_its_folder`
- `the_last_post_sets_both_the_folder_and_the_name`
- `a_documents_project_file_and_last_post_feed_the_dialog`: a real `State`, with the viewer's window closed.
- `a_bare_file_name_opens_no_folder`
- These test a new function, so there's no "fails on main" run. On `main` the dialog's arguments were the constants `program.nc` and no folder.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 4`): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell`, and `theme_files` too. 368 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail.
- The 3 failures are the UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`). They fail on clean `main` on this machine by the same pixel counts (1544, 1815, 2080; #255).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the native file dialog by hand (rfd can't run headless), Linux, macOS.

title: fix(ui): the G-code viewer lists every line from the left edge
body:
The G-code viewer now lists every program line from the left edge, and a line wider than the window stays on its one row.

### What was wrong

- `pages::gcode_listing` drew each line with `ui.add_sized([width, row_h], Label)`. egui lays that widget out in a centred-and-justified layout, so every line's text was centred in its row. On `main` 8f30bee, in the test program below, `M30` is painted at x 273 and the motion line above it at x 159.
- The same layout let a line wider than the window wrap onto a second row (30 px against a 15 px row). Every row below it was then off the scroll-cursor arithmetic, which divides by one fixed row height.

### What changed

- Each row is a left-to-right box exactly the listing's width and one monospace row tall (`allocate_ui_with_layout` plus `set_min_size`). The text starts at the left edge, and the row height is unchanged, so the cursor law (the clip rect's middle row is the published line) holds as before.
- A line wider than the window is truncated on its row, and egui shows the whole line on hover.
- Syntax colouring, the issue's second ("see about") ask, is not in this PR. It needs new per-word text colours that pass the contrast law on both built-in themes and every colour-vision mode, and maybe new theme-file keys, so I've left a proposal on the issue for the owner. Hence `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/256-gcode-left-align.md` (`Label::halign` inside `add_sized`, and a horizontal scroll bar, were considered and dropped).

### Tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/gcode_viewer.rs`, through the real shell layout)

- `every_gcode_line_starts_at_the_listings_left_edge`: `%`, `M30` and a long motion line are painted at the same x. It reads the painted text shapes from the frame output, because the accessibility rect is the row's box and spans the row either way.
- `a_line_wider_than_the_viewer_stays_on_one_row`: a 120-character comment is one row tall and starts at the same left edge.
- With `pages.rs` put back to `main` (`git stash` of that file only), both fail: "`M30` starts at x 273, the longer motion line at x 159", and "the wide comment is 30 tall, a one-line row 15.125". The two existing viewer tests (`the_viewer_window_publishes_the_scroll_cursor`, `a_successful_post_opens_the_viewer_and_new_document_retires_it`) pass with the change.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because another session was using most of the CPU): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `theme_files`. 283 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail.
- The 3 failures are the UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`). They fail on clean `main` on this machine by the same pixel counts (1544, 1815, 2080; #255). The viewer is closed in every snapshot, so this change can't move them.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the windowed app by hand, Linux, macOS.

title: fix(ui): a refused post keeps its reason in a window past the status line
body:
A refused post's reason now stays on screen in a "Post refused" window. A viewport click no longer erases it.

### What was wrong

- `State::post_program_path` put a refusal only on the status line ("post refused: <reason>").
- The status line is shared. The next viewport click (`interact::pick_model` writes "selected <name>" or "no model under the cursor"), face or edge pick, or command wrote over it, so the reason was gone before the user could act on it. Posting the seeded demo (refused for a shank hit) and clicking the viewport centre replaces the refusal on the status line with the pick's own line, and on `main` 8f30bee was the only place the reason was shown.

### What changed

- A refused post also keeps its reason in `State::post_refusal` (`PostRefusal { path, reason, doc_version }`). The status line is unchanged.
- New `egui_app/post_refusal.rs`: a "Post refused" window (an in-app `egui::Window`, like the G-code viewer) shows the reason in the error ink, and says nothing was written to the file and a program already there is unchanged. It closes by its ✖, like the G-code viewer. A long reason scrolls.
- The window goes when the user closes it, when a later post succeeds, or when the document is switched (New, Open).
- An edit or regenerate after the refusal keeps the window and adds "The document has changed since this post was refused - post again to check it.", so the reason is never shown as current when it may not be. A pick does not count as an edit.
- The window draws nothing while no refusal stands, so no shell snapshot moves.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/265-sticky-post-refusal.md` (sticky status line, closing on any edit, and putting the refusal in the G-code viewer were considered and dropped). PR #232's status-strip alert styling is separate and doesn't conflict: it makes a refusal stand out while it is on the line, and this keeps it after the line moves on.

### Tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/post_refusal.rs`, through the real shell layout)

- `a_refused_posts_reason_survives_a_viewport_click`: post the seed (refused), click the viewport centre. The status line moves on, and the window still shows the gate's exact reason. No changed-since note, and no file written.
- `an_edit_after_the_refusal_notes_it_and_a_successful_post_retires_it`: the skim edit and regenerate keep the reason and add the note; the skim then posts and the window is gone.
- `closing_the_refusal_window_retires_it` and `a_new_document_retires_the_refusal`.
- With the window call taken back out of `shell.rs` (`git stash` of that file only), `a_refused_posts_reason_survives_a_viewport_click` fails ("a refused post opens its window"). The other three read the new `State::post_refusal` field, so they don't build without the fix.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 8f30bee plus this commit)

- The quick gate's plan for this diff (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand with `-j 3` because another session was using most of the CPU): ui lib plus `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `feedback`, `fixtures`, `gpu_render`, `machine`, `models`, `operations`, `shell`, `theme_files`. 367 pass, 2 ignored, 3 fail (below).
- The only failures are the three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`). They fail on clean `main` on this machine by the same pixel counts (1544, 1815, 2080; #255). The new window draws nothing without a refusal, so it doesn't touch them.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the windowed app by hand (the tests drive the real `shell_layout` through egui_kittest, including the viewport click), Linux, macOS.
- `state.rs` is already far past the 400-line law; this adds one field, its init and four lines in the post and document-switch paths. The window and its type live in the new `egui_app/post_refusal.rs` (78 lines), and the tests in a child module of `tests.rs` so they reuse its shell harness.

Changelog: A refused post's reason stays on screen in a "Post refused" window until you close it, post successfully, or switch documents, instead of vanishing at the next click (#265)

Fixes #265

title: feat(kernel): union/intersect and edge blends on the kernel seam, benched (M12.1 stage 2)
body:
M12.1 stage 2 of the Solidcore retirement gate. Stage 1 (68efb11) put solidcore 1.0.1 (tangency-labs' Apache-2.0 pure-Rust port of NVIDIA's SMLib) behind a `Kernel` seam in `camcraft-kernel`, with truck as the reference impl, and benched subtract and offset. This PR adds **union, intersection and edge blends (round/chamfer)** to the seam and the bench. **No production path is switched**: nothing outside `camcraft-kernel` depends on it.

## What changed
- `Kernel` trait: `boolean_union`, `boolean_intersect`, `blend_edges(solid, picks, radius, Blend::Round | Chamfer)`. truck implements union/intersect through truck-shapeops `or`/`and`. Its `blend_edges` returns `Unsupported` (truck has no fillet), and a test asserts that.
- `src/solidcore_blend.rs` (new): picks resolve to edges (256 samples plus golden-section refinement, `PICK_TOL` 1e-3). A pick on two edges at once (a vertex, or a point on a cylinder's seam) is refused as ambiguous. Then the port's `fillet_edges`, followed by a result law: a manifold solid, inside the source box, whose volume actually moved.
- Seam guards: face-less boolean operands are refused (the port returns the **whole box** for `box & empty`, now pinned). The blend radius guard is conservative on purpose (decision 4).
- `tests/common/mod.rs` holds the shared `Want`/`verdict`. Stage 1's 8 tests are all kept, and the count goes to 16.

## Agreement numbers (debug, default tolerances: truck mesh 1e-3 + boolean 1e-2)
| fixture | solidcore abs. error vs closed form | truck abs. error | cross gap (default) | cross gap (heavy lane, 10x finer) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| box-union-box-corner (1875) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| box-union-cylinder-boss (1000+20π) | 2.6e-9 | 1.7e-2 | 1.7e-2 | 2.9e-3 |
| box-intersect-box-corner (125) | 2.8e-14 | 0 | 2.8e-14 | 2.8e-14 |
| box-intersect-cylinder (40π) | 7.6e-9 | 3.4e-2 | 3.4e-2 | 5.7e-3 |
| (stage 1) cylinder-through-box / blind-pocket | 2.8e-8 / 4.2e-8 | 3.4e-2 / 2.6e-2 | same | 5.7e-3 / 2.8e-3 |

All bounding boxes agree within 1.5e-5 (truck's chord), and solidcore's within 1e-14.

Blends (solidcore only, checked against closed forms at 1e-6 relative; **truck: not yet - no blend in truck**):
| fixture | abs. error |
|---|---|
| cube round 1 / 4 / all 12 edges r2 (12 = Steiner, spherical corners) | 4.7e-8 / 9.0e-9 / 4.7e-7 |
| cube chamfer 1 / 4 / all 12 edges d2 (12 = inclusion-exclusion + bevel tetrahedra) | 1e-13 / 2e-13 / 1e-13 |
| L-block concave round r2 / chamfer d2 (material added) | 1.2e-9 / 4.5e-13 |
| cylinder top rim / both rims round r1 (Pappus) | 3.1e-6 / 2.2e-6 |
| hole rim round r1 on a boolean result (Pappus) | 4.4e-7 |
| **NOT YET** cylinder rim chamfer d1, port default path | 5.3e-4 (1.9e-6 rel - fails), upstream WR-421; pinned as a finding |
| same with opt-in `fillet_chamfer_cone_on_arc` | 1.1e-5 (4e-8 rel) - passes |

## Port findings (pinned in `KNOWN_PORT_VERDICTS_STAGE2`)
- `box & empty` -> `Ok solid V=1000` (a wrong answer that looks like a valid solid). The seam refuses empty operands.
- `box & disjoint box` -> `Ok non-solid`. The seam's result check turns it into `Err`.
- `fillet r NaN` -> `Err`. `fillet r6 on a 10-cube edge` -> correct (922.743), but the seam still refuses it (conservative guard).
- solidcore never panicked on any degenerate input.

## Gate
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel`: agreement 2 + 2 ignored, blend 6, corrupt_input 6, all green
- `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel -- --ignored` (heavy lane): green
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p camcraft-kernel`: passes

Pinning tests: `boolean_fixtures_agree_across_kernels`, `boolean_fixtures_agree_at_fine_tessellation`, `cube_blends_match_closed_form`, `concave_l_blends_match_closed_form`, `rim_rounds_match_pappus`, `not_yet_rim_chamfer_default_path_stays_a_finding`, `rim_chamfer_agrees_with_cone_on_arc_fix`, `truck_offers_no_edge_blend`, `seam_refuses_degenerate_blends_and_empty_booleans`, `port_stage2_degenerates_never_panic_and_match_pinned_verdicts`.

title: feat(ui): machined mesh paints deviation classes and lights the hovered facet
body:
## What changed

The machined mesh in the viewer's stock slot (M13.1) now shows two things it did not before:

- **Deviation classes on the mesh.** Each facet is judged once per mesh, using the same rule the GPU eye uses: the model's `DistanceLattice` (`pack_target`) is read at the facet centroid, with the gate `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, view cell)`. The result is one of four classes: clean, rest, gouge or unjudged. The code is in the new `app::machined_classes` module. The classes are cached in `stock_export::MeshCache` (`classify` / `viewed_classes`) and computed in `ui::machined::prime` alongside the extraction. `world::collect_parts` expands them into the stock part's per-vertex class buffer, so the mesh uses the sheet's and the eye's legend colours. Nothing is computed per frame, and the STL export path does not pay for the classes.
- **Hovered facet highlight.** When the mesh answers a stock hover, `machined::filter_hit_facet` returns the triangle the ray hit. It is stored in `State::hover_mesh`, which is view state, not a command, and is cleared on every hover refresh. The shell draws it as a yellow translucent fill with an outline in the hover colour, projected through the camera each frame, so moving the pointer causes no GPU re-upload. If no mesh stands, or a corner projects behind the camera, nothing is drawn.

The extractor is unchanged. The sim crate is untouched, apart from public items it already exported.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/25-mesh-hover-deviation.md`.

## Results

- Faced fixture (12x12x20 box faced to z 18 over a 12x12x18 model): every up-facing facet on the faced top classifies clean. The class buffer has the same length as the vertex buffer, and only the four class values appear.
- A second `prime` reuses the same classes `Arc`, so nothing is judged twice.

## Tests

- `app::machined_classes::tests`: `the_boundaries_belong_to_clean`, `no_number_no_verdict` (NaN, infinite readings and a NaN tolerance give unjudged; nothing panics), `no_target_paints_every_facet_unjudged`, `facets_on_above_and_under_the_model_class_as_such`.
- `ui::machined_tests`: `nothing_before_a_view_and_one_extraction_after` (now checks the classes, which were previously asserted to be empty), `the_hovered_mesh_facet_is_the_one_the_ray_hit_and_projects`.
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick` fell back to the batch set, and every step passed: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app suites, the ui suites run from `crates/ui`, and clippy with `-D warnings` (19.5 min). No snapshots changed.

Not hand-tested in the GUI yet.

Changelog: The machined stock mesh paints the Deviate classes (clean / rest / gouge / unjudged) and highlights the facet under the pointer.

title: feat(multiaxis): continuous C-axis live tooling - stated C on cl moves, the C word in the lathe post
body:
Continuous C-axis live tooling, first shippable slice: the rotary kinds (Rotary Contour / Parallel / Offset) on a mill-turn whose spindle is C now generate, verify and post through the Fanuc lathe post, instead of refusing "pinned (M13.5 B)".

## What changed

- **cl**: `Move::rotary: Option<f64>`, the spindle's stated C in unwrapped degrees, beside the part-frame `to`/`axis`. `cl::stamp_c` (new `cl/rotary.rs`) stamps a radially posed part-frame path: C = minus the tip's azimuth (Rz(C) turns the tip onto the +X live-tool station), unwrapped move to move. Every move is split collinearly until the machine's X/Z/C-linear motion follows the verified chord within the op's tolerance. Refused by name: arcs, moves with no pose or a pose off the radial station, moves it cannot split near the spindle line, and paths carrying cycle/comp/thread/probe records. When the field is absent nothing changes: goldens, streams and project files stay byte-identical (the project field skips serialization).
- **app**: the rotary letter gate now returns 'C' for the spindle line, and the three rotary arms stamp their path (`rotary_gate::stamp_spindle_c`, the line must be world Z). `machine::check_document` checks a C move for a rotary named C and its stated travel, and no longer reads the part-frame axis as A/B for it. `MoveDto.rotary` persists the angle.
- **post stream/engine**: a C path writes `PARAM LiveTool radial` and `A 0 B 0 C <c>` on every move. The engine refuses that section by name for any script that does not declare `liveTooling = true` (same pattern as `coolantModes`), so every mill post refuses it.
- **.mch grammar**: `tool_station.live_tool { c_axis_on, c_axis_off, spindle_on, spindle_off }`, the builder-specific engage and live-spindle words (all four or none), mirrored to `machine.liveTool`.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps**: the C section. G98, the machine's C-on word, `<spindle_on> S<rpm>`. Every move is turned by C and must land on the station (5 um), otherwise it is refused and never projected. Output is `G01 X<2r> Z C F`, with F scaled for the control's composite rotary feed law (C degrees counted as mm). Rapids are G01 at the machine's stated max feed, never G00. The first move positions with `G00 C` and then `G00 X Z`. Arcs and cycles in the section are refused. Afterwards: spindle off, C off, G99. With no `live_tool` words stated, the section is refused by name.

## Readings

- The wrapped helix golden at r10, 30 deg chords, tol 0.01: each chord splits into 8 pieces. X dips to 19.318 at the chord midpoints, so the tool follows the planned chord, not an arc. F is about 2250-2370 for a 400 mm/min tip feed (composite degree-as-mm scaling).
- The Rotary Contour on the standing r6/r5 bar (mill-turn C) generates with every move on the station, posts with zero warnings, and contains no M03.

## Tests

- `cl::rotary::tests::*` (3): unwrap, winding, refusals.
- `c_axis_live.rs` (new, 4):
  - `a_rotary_contour_on_the_spindle_states_c_on_every_move_and_posts`: generate + post.
  - `the_wrapped_helix_posts_to_its_golden`: `golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_helix.nc`.
  - `every_post_without_c_or_without_the_machines_words_refuses_by_name`: mill post / no live_tool words / C disagreeing with XY.
  - `the_c_word_rides_the_stream_and_parses_back`: also proves a path without C stays byte-shape identical.
- `rotary_letter.rs`: the pinned test is replaced by `the_mill_turn_spindle_as_c_axis_answers_c_and_stamps_it`. `operation::rotary_gate` unit test updated the same way.
- Touched suites run: see the PR comment for the gate readings.

## Limits (owed on #33, see docs/decisions/33-continuous-c.md)

- The machine C-sense word.
- Unwinding C on links against a stated travel. The shipped millturn.mch states -360..360, so a multi-ring path is refused by the letter gate.
- Axial/face live-tool stations and G12.1 polar interpolation.
- Arcs on a C turn.
- The composite feed law is a stated assumption about Fanuc-style controls, to be confirmed on a real control.
- The shipped millturn.mch states no live_tool words, so in-app posting of a C op refuses by name until the user's machine file states them.
- Size: `post/src/post/mod.rs` (465 -> 483) and `fanuc-lathe.cps` (424 -> ~520) were already over the 400-line target and grew.

Changelog: Continuous C-axis live tooling: rotary kinds on a mill-turn's spindle C state the C angle per move, split to tolerance, and post through the Fanuc lathe post (X Z C under G98 with the machine's live_tool words); every post without liveTooling refuses by name

title: build(wasm): camcraft-app links for wasm32 via a pinned wasi-sysroot (#31 rung 1)
body:
Rung 1 of the app/UI-on-wasm work. **This is a partial PR**: the domain layer builds and links for wasm32. The UI does not yet.

## What builds
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh` builds `camcraft-app` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and links `camcraft-cli.wasm`. That covers flecs' C, boa, truck, clipper2 and rayon. Before this, only geometry, cl and post compiled for wasm32.
- flecs' C needs a libc, and this target has none. The script downloads the wasi-sysroot 34 tarball, checks its sha256, and passes its headers through `CFLAGS_wasm32_unknown_unknown`. It also adds `-D__COSMOCC__` (flecs' generic-POSIX path) and `-D__wasi__`. At link time its `libc.a` resolves malloc, printf, pthread, clock and the rest.
- flecs_ecs 0.2.2 and flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 do not compile for wasm32 as published; upstream says that support is still in progress. The script copies both crates and makes three edits to the copies:
  - `libc::FILE` becomes `c_void`.
  - The pre-generated bindings use `"C"` in place of `"C-unwind"`.
  - meta_fn_types' wasm-gated `WorldRef`/`Entity` import is no longer gated.

  The copies are used through `cargo --config patch.crates-io...` for this build only. Each edit checks that its patch point is still there, so a flecs bump that moves one fails the build instead of passing silently. The tracked `Cargo.lock` is restored when the script exits.
- The `wasm` job in `ci.yml` now runs the script. Like every job in that file it is `workflow_dispatch` only, so it adds no push, PR or schedule trigger.
- No Rust source, manifest or lock file changed, so the native build is unchanged.

## Readings
- Local run (Windows, Git Bash, clang 21.1.8): `web/build-app-wasm.sh` finished in 2m52s and printed `linked .../wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/camcraft-cli.wasm` (270 MB, debug). Afterwards `git status` was clean, which shows the lock was restored.
- The linked module has two groups of imports:
  - the wasm-bindgen placeholders;
  - nine `wasi_snapshot_preview1` functions: `clock_time_get`, `fd_close`, `fd_fdstat_get`, `fd_prestat_get`, `fd_prestat_dir_name`, `fd_seek`, `fd_write`, `poll_oneoff`, `proc_exit`.
- I have not run the CI job. It is manual and the Actions budget applies.

## What does not build yet, and why (#31 stays open)
`cargo build -p camcraft-ui --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, with the flecs patches applied, stops at:
```
error[E0407]: method `bytes` is not a member of trait `egui::DroppedFile`
  --> egui-winit-0.36.2\src\dropped_file.rs:19:5
error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: `bytes_async`
error: could not compile `egui-winit` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
```
egui-winit 0.36.2 is native-only, so the browser shell needs eframe's web runner in its place. After that, the following are still owed; details are in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`:
- Move `shell_layout` out of `shell.rs` so both shells call it.
- Bring up the GPU asynchronously. About ten `pollster::block_on` sites remain.
- Replace the synchronous `rfd::FileDialog` (9 sites) with an async version or an `<input type=file>` seam.
- Add a `web_time` seam for `std::time::Instant`, which panics on this target.
- Run work inline where the code calls `std::thread::spawn`.
- Write a JS shim for the nine wasi imports.
- Pin wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129.

## Tests
No Rust code changed, so there are no new pinning tests. The proof is the script itself, run locally above. `bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh` passes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`.

title: fix(motion): a plain two-ring bar fits its true axis and wraps; the seam refusal names its causes
body:
A plain bar meshed as two rings now wraps in every orientation. The cause was the axis fit leaning by rounding, not a feature on the seam. The seam refusal now names its real causes.

### What was wrong

- A bar meshed as two rings (long side facets, axis-fan caps; this is how CAD exports a plain cylinder) was refused by the rotary wrap: "a feature that is not turned (a flat, a keyway, a cross hole) crosses the rotary wrap's seam". On `main` 0015347, with the issue's fixture (R6, Z ±40, 2 mm tool, Ø13 stock), n 16 at turn 0, n 64 at turn 0 and n 64 at turn 0.3 are refused (15, 37 and 38 seam columns). Only n 16 at turn 0.3 wraps.
- The cause is the axis fit, as the issue guessed, though the size differs: the lean is tens of microradians, not 1e-9.
  - On a two-ring bar, every side facet is a long right triangle. Its circumcenter (where `axis.rs` anchors its normal line) is the midpoint of the long diagonal, which is the bar's mid-station. No normal line can see a tilt about that point.
  - The eigen direction came out exactly Z (residual 7.4e-14 mm). The Gauss-Newton refinement (`axis_refine::refine_dir`) then returned a tilt of 2.6e-5 rad at n 16 and 2.5e-6 rad at n 64, and the fit kept it because its residual was "lower" by rounding noise (7.4159e-14 vs 7.4196e-14). At turn 0.3 the noise fell the other way, so the same bar fit exactly and wrapped.
  - With the axis leaning, the cap centres sat about 1 µm off it at arbitrary azimuths. Every cap facet near the ±π branch then read as a seam straddler, and the seam check counted far more than two columns.

### What changed

- `axis_refine::worth_refining`: the fit does not refine an eigen line whose residual is already below `CONCURRENT = 1e-9` mm per mm of mean radius. That line meets every normal line to rounding, and a refinement can only add a tilt the rows can't see. A real lean (the #62 uneven cone, microns of miss) is far above that floor and is still refined.
- `rotary_seam::SEAM_TH_TOL = 1 / WELD` (1e-6 rad, was 1e-9): seam vertices within the weld grid's grain, read as an angle, share a column. That is the same relative quantum the column profiles are compared at, and coarser than a float32 STL's azimuth noise. A flat's ragged vertices stand whole degrees apart; every D-flat refusal test still refuses.
- The seam refusal also names a mesh whose diameters were tessellated with different column counts, and says what to do about each cause ("rotate a feature clear of the seam, or export the model with one column count"). The phrase "crosses the rotary wrap's seam" is kept.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/228-seam-columns.md`. Widening only the seam tolerances was dropped: with the axis 2 µm off at the bar's end, the column profiles also differed by 2 µm in radius.

### Tests (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_dflat.rs`)

- `a_two_ring_bar_fits_its_true_axis`: n 16 and 64, at turns 0 and 0.3. The fitted axis leans less than 1e-12 rad.
- `a_plain_two_ring_bar_wraps_in_every_orientation`: the same four bars wrap, with more than 50 cuts and no cut tip inside the true polygon cross-section (0.05 margin).
- `a_shaft_meshed_with_mixed_column_counts_is_refused_naming_the_tessellation`: a stepped shaft with 16 columns on the neck and 64 on the body is refused, and the message names the column counts. Wrapping it would also answer the issue, but nothing pins what such a wrap would cut, so the refusal is what this test pins.
- With `axis.rs`, `axis_refine.rs` and `rotary_seam.rs` put back to `main`, all three fail; the four existing D-flat tests pass either way.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 0015347 plus this commit)

- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier batch` (every debug suite minus the four slow binaries, the ui crate, and clippy over every crate): 2400 tests pass. The axis fit is shared by the rotary kinds, the turning frame and the lathe spindle law, so this is the run that matters. It includes `lathe_spindle_fit`, which pins the #62 uneven-tessellation lean that the refinement exists for.
- The only failures are the three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`). They fail on clean `main` on this machine by the same pixel counts (1544, 1815, 2080; #255).
- Clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets): clean.
- Not run: the release tier's slow binaries (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`), Linux, macOS. I did not drive the app through `camcraft-cli mcp` for this one; the motion and app suites above are the check.

Changelog: The rotary wrap no longer refuses a plain bar meshed as two rings: the axis fit stops leaning it by rounding, and the seam refusal names a mixed tessellation as well as a feature (#228)

Fixes #228

title: feat(sim): the hidden-rest scan answers past its holding budget
body:
## What changed

Past the 1.2 M-cell / 40 M-claim budgets, the hidden-rest scan (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_hidden.rs`) used to read `RestUnjudged` ("NOT JUDGED") and block the post. It now gives a real verdict there:

- **Streamed in row bands.** `cells` / `claims` now cap what one pass *holds* at once (the bins, ~1.6 GB at 40 M claims), not what the verdict can read. When a lattice doesn't fit, its claims are counted row by row, the rows are cut into bands that fit, and each band is judged by the **same** body. Every column sees the same claims, pairing and distance law, so the banded verdict matches the whole-lattice verdict bit for bit (rows go in ascending order and a tie keeps the first worst). Nothing is sampled coarser, because a skipped column could hide a ledge and a false clean is a gouge-class bug.
- **Bounded work.** `ScanBudget` gains `work` (shipped 1 G facet-column visits plus ball-center distances, about 10 s at worst). The scan still answers `OverBudget` / NOT JUDGED by name past that limit, or when a single row's claims cannot be held. It never hangs and never reports a stated zero.
- **Exact nearest-center query** (`scan_near.rs`, new). A uniform XY grid over the center path, walked ring by ring outward. The walk stops on the ring's XY lower bound combined with the path's Z-range gap. The previous query's segment is tried first. A top is let go early only when it provably cannot raise the worst rest, so the minimum is the same number a linear scan returns.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/24-field-scan-verdict.md`. A coarse lattice was dropped because it is not conservative. Per-column SDF parity was dropped because it costs O(columns x facets).

## Readings

- 21-plate stack over 100 x 100 mm, r = 0.5 ball: 1.07 M columns and 44.0 M claims, which is past the shipped 40 M. **Before:** NOT JUDGED. **After:** judged, 41.206 mm hidden rest at the deepest plate top between two passes (hypot(10, 40.5) - 0.5, as expected). In release the verdict takes 14.5 s, of which 2.2 s is everything except the hidden half.
- Ceiling fixture streamed at a 600-claim budget (it holds about 4096 claims): rest and location identical to the whole scan, bit for bit.

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/tests/hidden_rest_banded.rs`:
- `past_the_claim_budget_the_hidden_slab_is_still_found`: the hidden rest is found while streaming.
- `past_the_cell_budget_the_bands_answer_too`
- `a_small_hidden_ledge_in_one_band_is_not_skipped`: a localized ledge is found with tight bands.
- `a_clean_flat_stays_clean_when_streamed`: the clean case.
- `the_walk_stays_bounded_and_says_so`: the work cap still refuses by name.
- `a_stack_past_the_shipped_budget_gets_a_real_verdict`: `#[ignore]` heavy lane (release). The 44 M-claim model under `ScanBudget::SHIPPED`, with a time bound.

`crates/sim/tests/stock_sim.rs::hidden_rest_over_budget_says_not_judged` is updated: it now starves a single row (claims, cells) or the work budget.

## Gate

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- All camcraft-sim suites in debug: green.
- camcraft-motion `finish3d`, `flow`, `pivot5d`, `turning_blade`, `turning_form`, `turning_thread`: green.
- camcraft-app `posed_contact`, `turning_form`, `turning_thread`, `verify`: green.
- Release heavy lane: `hidden_rest_banded --ignored` green, motion `finish3d --ignored` 33/33 green (60.6 s).

Changelog: The hidden-rest scan gives a real verdict past its 1.2 M-cell / 40 M-claim budget (streamed in row bands, same verdict bit for bit); only its new work budget still reads NOT JUDGED

Fixes #24

title: docs: a claim comment is a claim - mirror it as a label, both ways
body:
Only collaborators can set labels, so a contributor's claim is a comment. This makes that explicit and keeps the `claimed` label in sync with it, both ways (user, 2026-11-08: "a comment should suffice ... if we come across a claimed issue thru comment we should just label it as such - and vice versa if they remove their comment, remove their claim label for em as part of maintenance.. Otherwise the comment stands as claimed.").

- **AGENTS.md** - "A claim comment is a claim" replaces "Outside contributors' claims count":
  - check the issue's comments before claiming; a claim comment by anyone but the owner account means the issue is taken, label or not;
  - mirror it: `claimed` + assignee (label alone if GitHub refuses the assignee) + one reply;
  - withdrawn = deleted: if the claim comment is deleted or the claimant comments `unclaim`, remove the label and assignment and say the issue is free;
  - a contributor's claim has no 4 h timer - it stands while the comment exists; agent claims keep the 4 h rule.
- **`/review-prs` step 4** - now "Mirror claim comments - add and withdraw": the add query also accepts `/claim` and looks back 7 days; a new withdraw pass checks every open `claimed` issue for the claim behind it and drops labels whose contributor comment is gone. A label set by hand by a collaborator (no claim comment, no "Claim recorded" reply) is left alone.
- `docs/decisions/comment-claims.md` records the choice and what was dropped (a `/claim` Action).

title: feat(sim): dual contouring for the machined-stock mesh
body:
## What changed

Dual contouring (Ju, Losasso, Schaefer & Warren, "Dual Contouring of Hermite Data", SIGGRAPH 2002) for the machined-stock mesh, on the same cell-centre samples marching tetrahedra reads.

- `stock_sim::iso`: sampling split out into a shared `Grid`; new `IsoMethod { Dual (default), Marching }` and `extract_with(field, step, method)`. `extract` / `extract_at` (the STL export and the viewer's `MeshCache`) now return the dual mesh. A dual mesh with any open edge is never returned: the marching mesh of the same samples stands in, and that is logged.
- `stock_sim::dual` (new): one QEF vertex per sign-changing cell, one quad per sign-changing lattice edge, wound from material to air.
- `stock_sim::hermite` (new): the Hermite data. Normals come from the slope of the crossing sheet across the parallel edges beside each crossing; the sampled gradient is the fallback. A crossing next to a ridge is marked untrusted (|va|+|vb| < 0.95·h·|n_k|), and a cell holding one solves from the trusted, same-facing planes of its 3x3x3 block instead.
- `stock_sim::qef` (new): a pseudo-inverse with singular values under 0.1 of the largest dropped, so an ill-conditioned direction keeps the mass point. The vertex is clamped into its own cell, a non-finite answer falls back to the mass point, and the Jacobi eigensolver has a sweep cap.
- `docs/decisions/23-dual-contouring.md`: why dual is the default (an API parameter, not a user op parameter) and why the plain-gradient normals were dropped.

## Readings (cell 1.0)

| fixture | dual | marching | truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| slot floor/wall edge, worst gap to the mesh | **0.0000** cells | 0.3606 cells | 0 |
| 10x8x6 box volume | **480.000** | 472.307 | 480 |
| ball-nose pocket volume | 949.775 | 948.013 | 957.458 |

Plain central-difference gradient normals gave a 0.35-cell corner gap, no better than marching. That is why the sheet-slope and trusted-plane estimators exist.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_dual.rs`: `dual_contouring_keeps_the_slot_floor_wall_edge_sharp` (dual < 0.05 cell, marching > 0.2 cell, both closed), `dual_is_the_default_extractor`, `a_fully_cut_field_extracts_nothing_without_error`, `a_body_under_one_cell_never_panics_and_never_opens`, `a_curved_ball_pocket_stays_closed_and_never_bulges`.
- Unit tests: `qef::tests::*` (corner, edge, ill-conditioned/empty/NaN, far intersection clamped), `dual::tests::*` (empty lattice, single cell, NaN and truncated lattice).

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: every suite green.

title: feat(build): a headless binary per crate
body:
Each library crate now ships a small headless CLI, shaped like `post` (a `USAGE` text, `--help`, `--version`, hand-rolled arguments, no new dependency). Bad input exits 1 with a `<bin>: <message>` line and never panics.

| binary | does |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-geometry <model.stl>` | reads binary or ASCII STL and prints triangles, bounds, size, degenerate facets, open edges, closed |
| `camcraft-cl <file.cl>` | reads a CL dump and prints move counts by kind, arcs, cycles, rapid and cut length, bounds, chaining (exits non-zero if the moves do not chain) |
| `camcraft-tools list` / `speeds <work> <tool-mat> <D> <z>` | lists the built-in catalog with its sanity check; prints the rpm and feed window from the cutting table |
| `camcraft-sim <file.cl> x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 <D> [--ball] [--cell]` | cuts a stock box on the dexel grid and prints removed volume plus a rapid/depth verdict (exit 2 when flagged) |
| `camcraft-motion face [-o f] x0 y0 x1 y1 <D> <stepover> <cut-z> <clear-z>` | runs the facing generator over a rectangle and writes a CL dump |

New module `cl::text`: a reader and writer for the golden CL dump grammar. Until now the writer lived only in app's test helpers and the reader only inside post, so cl, sim and motion could not reach either. Its output matches the golden writer byte for byte.

Layering holds: no bin depends on app or ui. The sim change is limited to a new `src/bin` file and its test. The binaries are **not** added to the release zip (decision in `docs/decisions/32-headless-bins.md`).

**Tests** (`tests/headless_bin.rs` in each crate, run through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`):
- geometry: `geometry_bin_reads_a_closed_cube`, `geometry_bin_reads_ascii`, `geometry_bin_refuses_bad_input` (missing, garbage, truncated, NaN, unterminated facet, no args)
- cl: `cl_text_round_trips_every_golden` (every `crates/app/tests/golden/*.cl` is read and written back byte for byte), `cl_bin_prints_move_stats`, `cl_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- tools: `tools_bin_lists_a_sane_catalog`, `tools_bin_computes_speeds`, `tools_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- sim: `sim_bin_removes_a_slot` (volume within 3% of analytic), `sim_bin_flags_a_rapid_through_stock`, `sim_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- motion: `motion_bin_faces_a_rectangle` (output reads back as a chained path), `motion_bin_refuses_bad_input`

All 14 pass. Also green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-{geometry,cl,tools,sim,motion} --bins --tests --lib -- -D warnings` and the cl lib unit tests.

Changelog: Headless CLIs per crate: camcraft-geometry, camcraft-cl, camcraft-tools, camcraft-sim, camcraft-motion (dev tools, not in the release zip); cl gains a CL dump reader/writer (`cl::text`).

title: fix(motion,app): a turning pass that ends inside a longer bar leaves its cut at feed
body:
A turning rough in a bar longer than the part now posts. Each pass that ends inside the bar's uncut end leaves its cut at feed instead of rapiding through it.

### What was wrong

- Each profile ride (`turning::prof::ride`) plunges in at the window's bottom, rides up the part, and leaves with a radial **rapid** out at the window's top.
- When the bar runs on past that top (a bar longer than the part, or a window that stops partway along it), the nose sits inside the bar's uncut end when the pass ends. The rapid out crosses that stock.
- The meridian law (#103) flagged it correctly: on `main` 0015347, the flanged bar from `turning_axial_rapids.rs` in a Ø20 bar 8 mm longer than the part gets 7 `RapidInStock` warnings, one per rung, and the post is refused.

### What changed

- `StockEnv` carries the bar's far end, `s_top`: the highest station the stock reaches along the part's axis. `operation::turning_stock::read` fills it from the stock in the part's own frame, the one the kernel walks.
- `StockEnv::runs_past` says when the bar goes on past a ride's end (by more than `LONGER = 1e-6`, the same float-noise reading as `WIDER`).
- `prof::ride` takes an `Exit`: `Rapid` as before, or `Feed` at the plunge feed (the ride's radial lead) out to the clear radius. Profile rough and profile finish pick it from the stock. The contour kinds (chamfer, taper, multi-pass) read no stock and keep `Rapid`.
- A bar that ends with the part, or no readable stock, keeps the exact old path.
- Facing already reads the bar's end (#122, merged), so this is the remaining half of the issue's "done means".
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/229-rough-bar-end.md` (always-feed and retract-along-the-cut were considered and dropped).

### Tests

- `crates/app/tests/turning_axial_rapids.rs`: `a_rough_in_a_bar_longer_than_the_part_posts_clean`. This is the issue's pin: the job above generates with no `RapidInStock` and `posting::post_setup` writes the program. Fails on `main` with the 7 warnings above.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_stock.rs`:
  - `a_pass_ending_inside_a_longer_bar_leaves_its_cut_at_feed`: rough and finish in a bar 8 mm longer. Every exit is a feed at the plunge feed, every move ends where it did in a bar the part's length, and that bar keeps rapid exits.
  - `a_pass_stopping_partway_along_the_bar_leaves_its_cut_at_feed`: the window stops at Z 20 in a bar that runs to Z 28.
- With `prof.rs` and its two contour callers put back to `main`, all three new tests fail, and the existing ones still pass.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 0015347 plus this commit)

- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: motion lib plus `turning_contour`, `turning_prof`, `turning_stock`; app lib plus `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_stock_approach`. 265 tests, all pass.
- Because a path change can move lathe goldens the gate map does not name, I also ran every lathe, turning and post suite by hand: 21 in app (`lathe_*`, `turning*`, `posting`, `fanuc_post`, `tormach_*`, `post_not_judged`), 6 in motion (`turning_blade`, `turning_bore`, `turning_face`, `turning_form`, `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_cycle`) and the sim's `stock_lathe`. 211 tests, all pass.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The headless MCP has no way to load a lathe machine yet (#181), so the app-level check is the integration test above. It drives the real commands (set stock, load the lathe, add the tool, create and generate the op) and the real post. Not run on Linux or macOS.

Changelog: A turning rough or finish in a bar longer than the part now leaves each pass at feed instead of rapiding through the bar's end, so the job posts (#229)

Fixes #229

title: feat(build): sign the Inno-embedded uninstaller when a certificate is configured
body:
## Change

The uninstaller Inno Setup embeds in the setup exe is now signed whenever a certificate is configured, along with the setup exe itself.

- `scripts/sign.ps1` gains `-Status`, which signs nothing: exit 0 = certificate configured, 10 = not configured, 1 = half-configured. It is still the only script that reads `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*` and the only place holding the signtool command and the timestamp URL.
- `scripts/installer.ps1`: when `-Status` says configured, it passes `/DSignToolName=camcraft` plus `/Scamcraft=powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $q<sign.ps1>$q -Path $f` to ISCC. It then checks that the setup exe carries a signature. When `-Status` says not configured, it passes neither switch and logs `installer signing: off (no certificate configured)`; the ISCC command line is otherwise the same as before.
- `scripts/installer/camcraft.iss`: `SignTool={#SignToolName}` + `SignedUninstaller=yes` sit under `#ifdef SignToolName`, so they are only on when installer.ps1 defines it.
- `scripts/release.ps1` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`: removed the separate `sign.ps1` pass on the setup exe, because ISCC signs it now. The installer step in release.yml now has `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_CERT_PASSWORD` in its env. It was missing before, so with the secret set the old `sign.ps1` call there would have failed as half-configured. No triggers changed.
- `scripts/README.md`: documents how the signing works and drops the "uninstaller not signed yet" note. The decision record is `docs/decisions/29-sign-uninstaller.md`.

## Verified, and how

ISCC.exe (Inno Setup 6) is **not installed on this machine**, so a real Inno compile was **not run**. What I ran instead:

- PowerShell parse check of sign.ps1, installer.ps1 and release.ps1 (0 errors), and a YAML parse of release.yml.
- `sign.ps1 -Status` in each state: no env → exit 10; `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_CERT_PATH` alone → exit 1; thumbprint set → exit 0. `sign.ps1` with a thumbprint but no `-Path` → exit 1. With no env, `-Path x.exe` → exit 0, same as before.
- Ran installer.ps1 end to end against a **stand-in ISCC.exe**: a throwaway console exe placed on PATH. It prints the arguments it receives, writes a setup exe and an `uninst.e32.tmp`, and, when `/Scamcraft=` is given, expands `$q`/`$f` the way Inno Setup documents and runs the result through cmd for each file:
  - No certificate: no `/D`/`/S` reached ISCC and both files were NotSigned, so the unsigned path is unchanged.
  - Self-signed code-signing cert (New-SelfSignedCertificate in CurrentUser\My, removed afterwards and confirmed gone), `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_THUMBPRINT` set: the expanded command reached `sign.ps1`, and signtool signed `uninst.e32.tmp` with a DigiCert RFC-3161 timestamp (Get-AuthenticodeSignature showed the test cert as signer). `signtool verify /pa` then rejected the untrusted self-signed root, so sign.ps1 exited 1 and the build stopped with `INSTALLER FAILED: ISCC exited with 1`. That is the intended loud failure for a certificate that is configured but unusable. Because of that stop, the setup exe was never reached in this run. I did not trust the test root, since that needs an interactive Root-store prompt.
- `release.ps1 -DryRun` stops at preflight on this branch: it needs a new version that matches RELEASE_NOTES.md. So only its parse check was run; the change there removes a post-ISCC sign call and nothing else.

**Not exercised:** a real ISCC compile, with or without signing; a real installer whose `unins000.exe` is checked after a silent install; a trusted certificate. The first CI release with `CAMCRAFT_SIGN_CERT_BASE64` set, or a local `-Installer` cut with a real certificate, is where this gets exercised end to end. Check there that `dist/*-setup.exe` is signed, then run `setup.exe /VERYSILENT /DIR=<tmp>`, check `Get-AuthenticodeSignature <tmp>\unins000.exe`, and uninstall with `unins000.exe /VERYSILENT`.

Pinning tests: none (build scripts only; no Rust test covers scripts/).

Changelog: Windows installer: with a code-signing certificate configured (CAMCRAFT_SIGN_*), the embedded uninstaller is signed too, along with the setup exe

Fixes #29

title: fix(ui): a ball nose's corner radius is its ball - shown, not edited
body:
A ball nose's corner radius is its ball, half the diameter. The tool editor now says so and stops offering a field that does nothing.

### What was wrong

- On a ball nose, every part of the code that cuts or checks already uses half the diameter as the corner, whatever the `corner_r` field holds: `Cutter::of` sets the corner to the radius, `Tool::profile` draws the full dome, and the stock sim sweeps the exact sphere.
- The tool editor still showed an editable "Corner radius" on a ball nose. Typing in it changed nothing that is cut, which is what the reporter saw.
- A draft retyped from an end mill saved a ball nose with `corner_r = 0`, and the library summary then read `corner r 0.00`.

### What changed

- `Tool::tip_corner_r` (tools crate) states the rule in one place: a ball nose's (or probe's) corner is `d / 2`; every other kind answers its own field.
- The editor shows a ball nose's corner as text (`3.000 mm` for a 6 mm ball, "half the diameter - a ball nose's whole tip is its ball") with no field to edit. Every other kind is unchanged, so the bull nose still edits its corner.
- `ToolUi::to_tool` saves a ball nose with `corner_r = d / 2`, so the document holds the radius that is cut. The kind mapping moved into `ToolUi::tool_kind` so the editor can name kinds instead of numbering them.
- The tool library summary reads `tip_corner_r`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/263-ball-corner.md`. It says why the field is not also hidden on the kinds that never read it (end mill, drill, lathe kinds): that changes the end-mill editor's pixel golden, which needs regenerating on the CI platform (#255).

### Tests

- `tools::tests::a_ball_noses_corner_is_half_its_diameter_whatever_the_field_holds`
- `egui_app::ball_corner_tests` (new file, egui_kittest over the real editor window and library page):
  - `a_ball_noses_corner_is_shown_as_its_ball_with_no_field_to_edit`
  - `applying_a_ball_nose_saves_its_corner_as_half_the_diameter`
  - `the_library_summary_reads_a_ball_noses_corner_as_its_ball`
  - `a_bull_nose_keeps_its_corner_field` (guards the other side)

With `state.rs` and `pages.rs` put back to `main`, the three ball-nose UI tests fail and the bull-nose one passes.

### What ran (Windows 10, local, built from upstream `main` 0015347 plus this branch)

- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: the tools lib and the ui lib plus 10 ui suites. Everything passes except the three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which fail the same way on clean `main` on this machine. `tool_editor_snapshot` (an end mill) is off by 2080 pixels both on `main` and on this branch, so the end-mill editor picture is unchanged.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I did not open the windowed app by hand; the editor checks are the kittest tests above, which draw the real window code. Not run on Linux or macOS.

title: feat(post): G41/G42 cutter compensation on Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D
body:
## What changed

Control-side cutter compensation (both COMP variants: control = part contour, wear = centre path) now posts on three more mill dialects, each in its own words:

- **Haas** - `G1 G41|G42 X.. Y.. Z.. D<tool> F..` on the lead-in, `G1 G40 ..` on the lead-out (D = the tool's offset row, the H word's row).
- **Mazak (EIA/ISO)** - `G01 G41|G42 .. D<tool>`, `G01 G40`.
- **Siemens 840D** - `G1 G41|G42 NORM ..`, no D word: the radius is the active edge the tool call already selected (`T n D n`); NORM is stated so a modal KONT can never move the engage point.

The Fanuc post's laws carry over unchanged: a comp word that would land on a rapid, an arc, or survive to the section end, or a comp record inside a canned cycle, is a named counted refusal that blocks the gate. Wear writes one register note per section.

**Heidenhain keeps its by-name refusal** (message now names the posts that do support it): the TNC's documented engage point ("perpendicular to the programmed position") is not stated against the next element the way the Fanuc start-up is, so a perpendicular lead's engage point would be a guess; and the TNC always offsets by R + DR, so wear's "register holds only the delta" has no TNC form. Tormach is out of scope and still refuses. Reasoning in `docs/decisions/39-comp-dialects.md`.

## Readings

Haas mill operator's manual (G41/G42 need a Dnnn; Setting 58 Fanuc/Yasnac changes outside-corner joins only), Siemens 840D sl Programming Manual Fundamentals ("Contour approach and retraction": NORM, perpendicular to the path tangent at the start point; T/D edge selection), Heidenhain TNC 640 ISO programming manual (G41/G42 in a G01 block, radius R + DR, comp effective at block end), RS-274 / ISO 6983. Behaviour only.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post --test comp`: `haas_mazak_and_840d_write_their_words_on_the_leads`, `haas_mazak_and_840d_refuse_a_comp_word_on_an_arc_a_rapid_or_the_section_end`, `every_wear_post_notes_the_register_once_and_control_writes_no_note`, `every_other_shipped_post_refuses_control_compensation_by_name` (now Heidenhain, lathe, Tormach)
- `camcraft-app --test control_comp`: `haas_mazak_and_840d_post_the_part_contour_under_their_own_comp_words_to_the_goldens` (goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/contour_control_comp.nc`, gate releases)
- `camcraft-app --test wear_comp`: `haas_mazak_and_840d_post_wear_over_the_centre_path_to_the_goldens` (goldens `golden/nc/{haas,mazak,sinumerik}/contour_wear_comp.nc`)

Gate: camcraft-post all suites green; app control_comp, wear_comp, conformance, fanuc_post, cli, arc_planes, drill_rplane, probe_op, heidenhain_arc_centre, heidenhain_block_form, vertical_arc_entry green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Comp-free goldens byte-identical.

Changelog: Haas, Mazak and Siemens 840D posts write G41/G42/G40 cutter compensation (control and wear); Heidenhain still refuses by name

Fixes #39

title: fix(app): the program sim sweeps a tap at its thread's minor diameter
body:
**Partial fix for #266.** This removes one of the two checks that refuse a tap on a normally modelled hole. The other one still blocks the post; see "What is left" below.

### What changed

- The program sim (the stock-sim clause of the post gate) swept a Tap-kind tool at its full major diameter. CAD models a tapped hole at the thread's minor (tap-drill) size, and a tap only cuts the thread band outside that wall. So the sim read the band as a gouge down the whole hole wall and refused the post.
- A Tap-kind tool now sweeps its thread's core: `diameter / 2 - 0.5413 x pitch`. That is the ISO 724 radial thread depth, the same constant the thread-mill generator already uses (`machining2d::THREAD_DEPTH_PER_PITCH`). For M6 x 1 the core is Ø4.917.
- The rule lives in one place, `operation::tool_law::cutting_radius`, so a later fix to the generator's verify can read the same number. Every other tool still sweeps half its diameter. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name.
- A tap over a hole smaller than its core, or over solid metal, is still a gouge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-minor-sweep.md`.

### Readings

| Case (M6 x 1 tap, plate with a blind hole) | Program sim before | Program sim after |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | gouge, worst 12.000 mm on the hole wall | clean, 0 gouge cells |
| Ø3 hole (too small) | gouge | gouge (still refused) |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`: fails on `main` (`worst 12.000 mm at (-0.31, -2.94, z 8.0)`), passes with the fix.
- `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge`: guards the other side; passes before and after.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

- Both pinning tests alone, with the fix, and with `stock_sim.rs` put back to `main` (the first one fails there as above).
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: app lib plus 13 suites (the gate map's `stock_sim` and `tool_law` suites plus `tap_sim`), 155 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The app, through `camcraft-cli mcp`, built from this branch (upstream `main` 897a820 plus this commit): imported a plate STL with a round Ø5 blind hole, added `TAP-M6` and a Drill/Tap op, generated, verified. The program gate now reports `ok` with no problems. With a Ø3 hole it still reports `gouge: program cuts below the model in 127 cell(s), worst 6.00 mm`.
- Baseline batch tier on clean `main` 897a820 on this machine: all suites pass except three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which also fail without this change. Not run on Linux or macOS.

### What is left (why this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`)

With this fix the Ø5 tap job still does not post. The op's own verify flags `move 1 cuts past the finish surface` and `move 2 cuts past the finish surface` (the tap feeding in and out). That verify hands one tool radius (`tool.geom()`) to every law, including the rapids laws, where a tap's full diameter is the right envelope: a tap must never rapid into the thread band. I tried shrinking only the containment solid law's cutter; the tangency law still flags the same two moves, so I dropped that. Fixing it means splitting the cutting radius from the rapid envelope in the verifier's inputs, and it meets the convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs` that a tapped hole is modelled at the tap's major diameter. I left that for you to decide on the issue.

title: feat(app): explain operation tops below remaining stock
body:
## Summary

Explain an operation's height mismatch at generation instead of leaving only a rapid-move index to diagnose it.

- For upright 2D/3D milling, compare authored Top against declared stock facets clipped to the operation's controlled region.
- Credit earlier same-setup facing/pocketing through the existing lazy prior grid for analytic box/cylinder stock. Partial or unknown removal keeps the advisory. Sampled model-stock history is conservative because it can miss sub-cell raised features.
- Store the advisory in existing toolpath notes and show it as a warning in the operation status banner. Existing move-level collision checks and post refusal remain unchanged; no NC moves, serialized warning variant, project-format version, or dependency is changed.
- Retain current-main UI changes and update three real-rendered snapshots for the new visible warning count and named stock-top footer.
- Keep the decision in `docs/decisions/104-top-stock-warning.md`. Existing entry/digest tests still prohibit entry/inert-word notes and require unchanged moves while allowing exactly the new independent Top warning.

## Readings and pinning tests

The implementation follows the repository's Issue Law, Prime Directive, local quick-gate policy, existing same-setup prior-stock laws, and polygon intersection/linear-facet height geometry. No vendor implementation or proprietary material was used.

- `generation_names_top_below_stock_and_keeps_the_rapid_gate`
- `facing_to_top_removes_the_height_warning_but_a_shallow_face_does_not`
- `top_at_the_stock_surface_has_no_height_warning`
- `a_narrow_mesh_stock_feature_is_not_acquitted_by_an_unsampled_prior`
- `stock_top_is_local_and_disjoint_stock_is_silent`
- `a_sloped_stock_cap_is_read_at_the_region_not_its_far_vertex`
- `prior_credit_is_regional_and_partial_removal_keeps_the_highest_cell`
- `a_prior_with_no_finite_surface_is_unknown_not_clearance`
- `the_top_stock_note_is_a_visible_warning_not_an_entry_fallback`

## Validation

Native Windows/MSVC validation, integrated with main `a89ed46d679c22ef9736cfdc1ea015a37f7f3615`; final tested tree `fbdc1f6244358146ab1ef69184772cc783c6082f`:

- `cargo test --locked -j6 -p camcraft-app --lib --test top_stock -- --test-threads=6`: 84 library tests and all 4 Top/stock integration tests passed. This source integration differs from the final tree only by the three subsequently reviewed snapshot PNGs.
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -Base a89ed46d679c22ef9736cfdc1ea015a37f7f3615`: exit 0, both selected steps passed. App: 848 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored; UI: 378 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo clippy --locked -j6 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0 on the final tested tree.
- Independent static review and bounded current-main integration review passed. The three final goldens are exact copies of actual native renders; every changed row was visually inspected and their hashes bound to the tested tree.

The initial two named-warning regressions executed and failed before the fix. Earlier partial/failed attempts are not counted as final passing evidence. No hosted workflows were dispatched; this repository gates locally.

## Limits

This is an advisory, not a new safety certificate or a new post blocker. Tilted, rotary, and turning frames do not receive a world-Z diagnostic; drilling keeps its existing named R-plane refusal. Model-stock history and boundary-cell padding may conservatively retain warnings. No machine execution, release, or hosted workflow dispatch is part of this contribution.

Changelog: Explain below-stock operation Top heights during upright 2D/3D generation, with regional stock comparisons and credit for earlier cuts on analytic stock.

title: feat(post): machine files for the other Tormach mills; belt ranges and rigid tapping from the .mch
body:
Follow-up to #131 / PR #162. This adds machine files for the other Tormach mills whose operator's manuals were available, and lets each machine file state the two spindle facts the PathPilot post had hard-coded for the 770 family.

### Machines
Each file uses its own Tormach operator's manual (public Tormach documentation, § Machine Specifications / Performance Expectations). All are inch machines with Flood M8 and Mist M7 (every manual documents M07/M08/M09). Travel is ± the full stroke in program coordinates, as on the 770MX.

| Machine (Setup pane) | Manual | Travel X/Y/Z in | rpm | belt ranges | kW | XY/Z IPM | rigid tap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tormach 770MX *(existing, MF serials)* | UM10587 | 14 / 7.5 / 13.25 | 175–10000 | 175–3250, 525–10000 | 1.1 | 300 / 250 | yes |
| Tormach 770MX (ML) | UM10864 | 14 / 7.5 / 13.25 | 250–10000 | one | 1.5 | 450 / 420 | yes |
| Tormach 770M | UM10539 | 14 / 7.5 / 13.25 | 175–10000 | 175–3250, 525–10000 | 1.1 | 135 / 110 | **no** (R8) |
| Tormach 1100MX | UM10586 | 18 / 11 / 16.25 | 70–10000 | 70–2000, 250–10000 | 1.5 | 300 / 230 | yes |
| Tormach 1500MX | UM10811 | 19.7 / 13.8 / 14 | 250–10000 | one | 3.0 | 1200 / 600 | yes |
| Tormach PCNC 440 | UM10372 | 10 / 6.25 / 10 | 300–10000 | 300–4500, 650–10000 | 0.56 | 135 / 110 | **no** (R8) |

The ML-serial 770MX (EtherCAT) has a different spindle from the MF one, so it is its own entry.

**Not included:** the non-MX 1100 and the plain 770, because neither manual was available. That is why this PR says **Refs** #170: the issue stays open for those two.

### `.mch` additions (both optional; unstated = today's behaviour)
- `spindle.ranges: [{min_speed, max_speed}, ...]` → `machine.spindleRanges`. The Tormach post's belt note now uses the machine's own ranges, not the 770's hard-coded numbers. A machine with fewer than two ranges gets no note.
- `spindle.rigid_tapping: false` → `machine.rigidTapping`. On such a machine the Tormach post refuses a tap cycle by name (one counted warning, which blocks the post) and never writes `G84`.

Golden change: `synth_tormach.nc` (posted against the generic metric VMC, which states no ranges) loses its 770-family belt comment. The 770MX goldens are unchanged.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/170-tormach-machines.md`.

### Tests
New: `crates/app/tests/tormach_machines.rs`:
- `every_tormach_machine_states_its_manuals_figures`
- `the_script_sees_the_ranges_and_the_tapping_word`
- `the_belt_note_follows_the_machines_own_ranges` (for example, 2500 rpm names HIGH on the 1100MX and nothing on the 770MX)
- `a_rigid_tap_is_refused_on_a_machine_that_cannot_rigid_tap`

`machine::every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration` now lists the new entries.

Quick gate on the final tip (rebased on main at f4e4eac): post, sim, geometry, cl and tools ok; clippy ok. The failures are the same as on `main` without this PR:
- `drilling_cross_box` / `drilling_cross_spindle` (#151)
- `swarf_pose_continuity`
- `headless_run_succeeds` and the window tests (headless GPU on this Mac)
- `tool_editor_snapshot`: fails on current `main`, because #178's new `PRB-0400` catalog tool lengthens the catalog list and the scrollbar thumb shrinks (20 px). That is a stale snapshot, unrelated to this PR.

### Still to do before ready (draft until then)
- PathPilot Hub simulation of a program posted for the 1100MX and the 770M (belt note, and the tap refusal on the 770M).
- GUI check that the new machines appear in the Setup pane's machine list.

Adds a 'Labels' step to `/review-prs`:
- green `merge-ready`: review clean and the PR merges cleanly;
- red `needs-rework`: the review found blockers;

title: fix: Fit to Models' cylinder is snug - the part's radius plus the allowance
body:
## What changed

#230 (from the review of PR #190): Fit to Models' cylinder took its diameter from the padded footprint's **diagonal**, so a round part of radius R got a ~1.41 R bar - and since #130 the turning kernels rough from the bar's OD, so every auto-fitted lathe setup cut many passes in air.

- `camcraft_geometry::stock::fit_cylinder_about(bounds, r_max, margin)`: a cylinder about the vertical axis through the bounds' XY centre with radius `r_max + margin` (height and placement as before).
- `camcraft_app::model::solid_world_radius_about(world, c)`: the models' largest horizontal distance from the vertical line through `c` (stock and WCS excluded, as `solid_world_aabb`) - a turned part's revolved max radius.
- The Stock page's StockFit (cylinder) uses them. The cylinder still contains every vertex and is never larger than the old diagonal bound, so it applies to every cylinder fit, mill included.
- Existing documents keep their stock numbers on load; only a new Fit is snugger. Decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` (#230).

Note: PR #238 (#198) refactors the same StockFit handler a few lines away (`apply_stock_fit`); whichever merges second takes a small merge.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry`: green.

Every issue branch appended to the end of `RECOMMENDED.md`, so each merge re-conflicted every other open PR on that file. Now:

title: fix(motion): a D-flat that faces the axis vouches for its roundness
body:
## What changed

`rotary_dflat::a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement` has been red on main since #223 (bisected: `c9a9fb3^1` passes): the through-flat bar read "the model's normals share no rotation axis".

**Cause.** #223 rightly stopped an off-axis boss lending its bearings: the coarseness gate (and the point-share rule's pencil skip) read only facets whose normal lines meet the axis within the concurrency tolerance. A D-flat's facets miss that line by part of the flat's width (0.2-0.4 mm on this bar, tol 0.18), so they were set aside too - and a single-band D-flat bar is one wall pencil with a ~39 degree skip at the flat (0.69 rad vs the 0.49 budget).

**Fix** (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_point.rs`, `axis.rs`):

- `faces_axis(d, ax)`: a facet square to the axis (`|n . u| < 0.05`) whose centroid's normal line misses it by less than half the facet's own size (`sqrt(area) / 2`) faces the axis - the axis's foot falls on the face.
- Its normal now counts in `judge`'s coarseness gate and in `borne_out`'s point-share pencil skip.
- A boss's facets miss the part's axis by its offset (millimetres), far more than half their size, so they still lend nothing - every #208 / #223 boss and prism pin stays green.
- Decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` (#246).

Note: PR #247 (#237) also edits `axis_point.rs`, in a different function (`borne_out`'s fold check / new `folded`); whichever merges second takes a trivial merge.

## Gate (own worktree build, current main)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests`: `rotary_dflat` 4/4 (red on main); only `swarf_pose_continuity` x2 fails (known on main).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --tests`: only `drilling_axial::a_drill_where_the_model_has_no_hole_is_convicted` fails (known on main).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests

- `multiaxis::axis_point::tests::a_single_band_d_flat_bar_reads_its_axis` - four flat azimuths read Z (fails on main with "share no rotation axis").
- `rotary_dflat::a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement` (back to green).

Changelog: A single-band bar with a D-flat fits its axis again (regressed in the point-concurrency guard)

title: fix(motion): the axis fit reads flats hiding in a fine ball's latitudes
body:
## What changed (P0)

#237: a ball r30 UV-meshed at 120x60 or finer, with a 10x10x100 square rod (or a 6x6x80 rod, or a 40x4x100 flat bar) through its centre, read a **trusted** X or Y axis - turning about it would sweep the rod into a disc. The ball's facets all meet at its centre, so they share a pencil with the rod's faces; their latitudes run continuously about a cross axis, one "wide" class that #223's per-class ring check leaves to `off_cone`, and the rod's faces hid inside it.

`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_point.rs`:

- new `folded(ds, u)`: each wide latitude class is cut into `LAT_BIN` = 0.02 latitude bins; per bin, the area-weighted resultant of the 1st-4th bearing harmonics. A revolve's bin cancels them; a rod's two opposite faces keep nearly all of the 2nd harmonic, a flat bar's sides and end caps (a quarter turn apart) the 4th. A bin past `FOLD` = 0.5 counts `fold * area`.
- `borne_out`: a pencil whose folded area passes `FOLD_SHARE` = 2 % of the inlier area does not bear the axis out. The 10 % bias budget was not enough: the 6x6x80 rod's faces are ~7 % of the inliers. The measure reads only wide classes, which a turned part's narrow rings never are.
- Known consequence (fail closed): a square section inside a dome, judged about its true axis, is refused too (4th harmonic); a hex (6th) is not.

AGENTS.md Issue Law (user, 2026-11-08):

- `gh pr create` gains `--draft`: every PR opens as a draft and stays one while work, gating and review fixes land on it.

title: feat: a tool's own controller number, posted as T/H
body:
## What changed

A tool had no number of its own: the post wrote `T`/`H` as the tool's 1-based **position** in the document's tool list. On the contributor's 770MX the cutter is T31 in PathPilot's tool table, but the program said `T1 M6` / `G43 H1`. It applied tool 1's length and ran about 1.5 in high. That failed safe, but a shorter H1 would have cut too deep.

- **`ToolDef` gains `number: Option<u32>`.** `ChangeTool` keeps it (apply and undo); `DeleteTool` and `DeleteEntity` restore it on undo.
- **New `SetToolNumber` command** sets or clears it, undoably. It refuses:
  - an unknown or non-tool name;
  - a number outside 1–99999 (0 means "no tool" on most controls);
  - a number another tool already has;
  - a no-op.
- **Project file:** an optional `"number"` on the tool record, written only when set. Absent means unnumbered, which is what every older file means, so there's no version step. A stated number outside 1–99999 is refused on load, by name.
- **`app::tool_numbers`** holds the one numbering rule used by the post: a tool's **own number**, otherwise its **list position**, so unnumbered documents post exactly as before and no golden moves. It also holds the **clash rule**: when two tools of one program would post the same number (for example an explicit 2 and another tool sitting at position 2), the post refuses and names both. With an ATC, `T2 M6` for two tools loads one of them for both.
- **Tool editor:** a "Tool number (0 = list position)" field. *Apply* or *Add tool* queues a `SetToolNumber` when it changed, as its own undoable command. The `egui_tool_editor` snapshot is updated (reviewed: only the new field is added).

Renumbering doesn't make operations stale: their stamps digest the tool's geometry, and the number doesn't change any path.

## Readings

- `scripts/gate.sh quick` (batch mode) on f441d38. Clippy with `-D warnings`: clean. geometry, cl, tools, post and sim: ok. All the new and touched tests pass. Failures that also occur on this branch's upstream base (c9a9fb3) without the change:
  - motion: `rotary_dflat::a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement`, plus `swarf_pose_continuity`'s two tests;
  - app: `drilling_cross_box` / `drilling_cross_spindle` (#151);
  - ui: the three headless-GPU tests (no fallback graphics adapter on this macOS machine).
- Merges cleanly with current `upstream/main`.

## Pinning tests

- `tool_numbers::a_number_is_set_cleared_and_walked_by_undo_and_redo`
- `tool_numbers::bad_numbers_are_refused_by_name`
- `tool_numbers::change_and_delete_keep_the_number`
- `tool_numbers::the_post_writes_a_tools_own_number_and_positions_for_the_rest` (T31 and H31 through the default post)
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name`
- `tool_numbers::the_project_file_carries_the_number_and_only_when_set`
- `egui_app::tool_number_tests::setting_a_tool_number_is_a_command_with_undo`
- `egui_app::tool_number_tests::the_editor_draft_shows_the_tools_own_number`
- `egui_app::tests::tool_editor_snapshot` (updated image)
