## Summary

Fixes cross-drill topology depending on floating-point roundoff: a stock radius of `next_up(10.0)` previously produced 14 moves rather than 13 for `10.0`.

- Leave the shared CL builder, cutting moves, stock measurements and stock/holder/part safety proofs unchanged.
- Replace raw-float hashes with fixed ordered numeric reference chains captured before the correction. Counts, kinds, feeds and poses stay strict; only endpoint coordinates receive tolerance.
- Cover near-equal radii, real clearance movement, stationary indexing and multiple G54 translations on lathe and mill-turn.

## Review follow-up

title: fix(app): a fresh depth operation bottoms out at the part's floor, not the G54 plane
body:
## What changed

A new depth operation (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Offset…, quick-added from the ribbon) took its default **bottom** from `Carried::of`'s fallback, `WorkOffset(0) + 0`: the G54 Z0 plane. With G54 Z zeroed on the **part's top**, which is a common shop habit (Tormach users in #131 do it) and what *Set origin* on a top face produces, that bottom resolved level with the default top (`TopOfModel + 0`). `CreateOperation` then refused the zero-depth operation ("must cut downward…") before the user could open its Heights tab, so the only way through was to move G54 temporarily.

The fallback is now **`BottomOfModel + 0`** (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, one line). A fresh operation's numbers still show where the material is, which was the intent of the old default ("issue 2"'s contract in the test comment), but without depending on the shop's work-offset convention.

**This reverses a deliberate default.** `fresh_depth_operations_default_to_the_part_and_g54` pinned the G54 bottom. It is renamed to `fresh_depth_operations_default_to_the_part_top_and_bottom` and updated, with the reason in its comment.

**Edge case, unchanged by this PR:** a model with zero thickness (top = bottom) still seeds a zero-depth operation. It did before too, whenever G54 sat on that plane.

## Readings

- `scripts/gate.sh quick` ran in batch mode, because the comparison base was older than upstream. **Clippy with `-D warnings`: clean.** geometry, cl, tools, post and sim: all ok. Failures that also occur on this branch's upstream base without the change:
  - `motion::swarf_pose_continuity`: `advanced_swarf_poses_never_flip_between_consecutive_cuts` and `no_swarf_pose_under_the_equator_is_upright_and_every_flank_clears_the_blade`. Checked on the base commit e607ca1; no open issue tracks them.
  - `app::drilling_cross_box` / `drilling_cross_spindle`: #151.
  - `ui`: the three headless-GPU tests (`headless_run_succeeds`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`). There's no fallback graphics adapter on this macOS machine.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 239 passed (the headless one aside), including the new and updated tests. App suites that seed through `Carried`/`retype_params` (`mill2d_b`, `area_open`, `whole_model_pocket`, `shoulder_adaptive`, `roughing2d`, `pick_doors`, `heights`): all pass.
- Merges cleanly with current `upstream/main`.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::fresh_op_tests::a_fresh_depth_operation_is_created_with_g54_on_the_part_top`: the ribbon's own `quick_params` for kinds 1–4, created through `CreateOperation` on a part with G54 placed on its top. This fails with the old default.
- `egui_app::fresh_op_tests::a_bottom_on_the_g54_plane_is_refused_when_g54_sits_on_the_part_top`: the old default reproduced explicitly, still refused ("must cut downward"), documenting the failure #214 reported.
- `operations::height_row_tests::fresh_depth_operations_default_to_the_part_top_and_bottom`: updated (it was `…_part_and_g54`).

Changelog: A new depth operation's default bottom is the part's floor (Bottom of model), not the G54 plane, so it is created even when G54 Z is zeroed on the part top

Fixes #214

title: fix(app): a new operation posts after its setup's existing ones, not in name order
body:
## What changed

`CreateOperation` never set an explicit order, so ops with no order sorted by **name** in the program: a 'Finish' created after a 'Rough' posted first, and since #103/#109 that order also decides the prior laws' verdicts.

- `CreateOperation` now appends the op at the end of its setup's program order with an explicit index - the same append `PasteOperation` already did, shared as `append_position` (crates/app/src/commands/operation/create.rs). Siblings with no stored position (older projects) are pinned at their current name-order position, so nothing already in a program moves. Undo restores each sibling's previous `OperationMeta` (an old `None` comes back as `None`).
- Old projects keep their name order on load (no load-time migration).
- Tests that pinned the old behaviour:
  - `remachining::program_order_is_the_posts_order_not_the_creation_order` pinned the documented "Operation10 runs before Operation2" wart; it is now `program_order_is_the_creation_order_not_the_name_order` - the op made first runs first, the other goes Stale naming it, Regenerate All masks it.
  - `setup_sheet::sheet_orders_ops_by_the_program_law` now reorders explicitly (still "the sheet follows the post, not history"), and the sheet header reads "setup rank, then position".
  - `operation_metadata::version_49_operations_keep_legacy_name_order` strips the stored positions from its downgraded fixture (a real v49 file never had them).
- Decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` (#167).

## Gate (own worktree build, rebased on 0aa542f)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --tests`: 113 of 114 binaries green; only `drilling_axial::a_drill_where_the_model_has_no_hole_is_convicted` fails (known on main, a 0.0006 mm lathe axis tolerance).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui`: green except the lib's `egui_shell_snapshot_light` (Diff 1) and `tool_editor_snapshot` (Diff 4) - software-GL diffs, same counts on main.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests

body:
## What changed

Requested in #192: "features that are blocked seem to fail for no reason, until you realise there's feedback in the bottom left you've missed."

title: fix(motion): the axis fit refuses normals that only meet at one point
body:
Stacked on #204 (issue/152-short-bar-axis). Retarget to main before #204 merges; the two merge back to back, never #204 alone.

## What changed

The axis fit no longer trusts an axis whose inlier normal lines all meet at ONE point (P0: a trusted wrong axis = every turned or cross-drilled feature about the wrong line).

- New `multiaxis/axis_point.rs`, called from `judge` in `axis.rs`. It finds the least-squares point where the inlier normal lines meet, then refits on the half of the area that misses it least. If lines through that point carry ≥ half the inlier area, those facets alone must pass the coarseness gate about the axis. Lines through one point carry no direction, so they can stand for a turned part only if they themselves cover every bearing.
- A box's faces give 2–4 bearings about any axis, and a single-band wall gives 2 about a cross axis: both are refused. A single-band wall about its OWN axis gives every bearing, so the common one-band CAD cylinder still fits. Multi-band walls are untouched.
- On isotropic parts, an axis read off a facing flat is no longer tilted by the direction refinement.
- The bearing-gap gate moved into the new module; `axis.rs` is 385 lines.
- Known cost: a single-band shaft whose keyway or D-flat leaves a bearing gap over about 28° is refused rather than read. It fails closed.
- Options dropped (RECOMMENDED.md):
  - sub-sampling faces, which breaks the exact meeting point coarse turned meshes rely on;
  - axial spread or a refusal for any point-concurrency, which would refuse the single-band cylinder;
  - a second-moment symmetry test, since a square plate is symmetric about its own normal.

## Pins (`axis_point_tests.rs`), each failing on the base 7fff05c

- `a_plate_with_a_boss_off_its_centre_line_is_refused_by_name` (100×100×10, r5 boss at (10,0), 1 and 5 bands): was trusted at (0.707, 0, 0.707)
- `a_single_band_shaft_with_a_flat_and_a_cross_hole_is_not_read_across` (r10 h150): was trusted X
- `a_cube_with_an_off_centre_boss_is_refused_by_name` (60 mm cube, r5 boss at (10,10), 1 and 5 bands): was trusted, tilted 15°
- Guard: `a_single_band_bar_still_fits_its_true_axis` (h20 and h150, off-origin)

All earlier pins stay correct: turned bar, short bars, keyed shafts, the #116 punched bar, noisy shafts, plate with a centred hole, cube, sphere, prism and #204's plate with a boss.

## Readings

motion lib axis 47; multiaxis*, rotary* and turning_* green; app drilling_cross* (all), lathe_* and turning* green (21 suites); clippy on motion and app is clean.

Changelog: The lathe and rotary axis fit refuses by name a part whose normals only meet at one point (a plate or block with a turned boss, a single-band shaft read across) instead of trusting a wrong axis

- Events at the seams the issue names:

The cross-drill holder check on box stock reads the stock along the holder's own swept footprint on each station, not the corner circle.

title: feat(motion): the scallop ceiling - a stepover at the ball diameter is refused by name
body:
## What changed

The scallop law's reach ceiling (#37), decided and documented. The generator half is built.

- The scan (`sim/stock_sim/ridge.rs`) looks only within band + 3·tol of the passes, so on flat ground it sees a cusp only up to about 4·tol past the ball (s ≈ 2.9 on an r3 ball at tol 0.1). A stepover of 4 left a 0.606 mm cusp that verified clean. The "missing-pass law" the comments relied on doesn't exist.
- **Built:** `finishing3d::params::scallop_ceiling`, called from the shared `validate`, refuses by name ("the scallop ceiling"):
  - a stated `stepover` or `steep_stepover` at or past the ball diameter, where h = r − √(r² − (s/2)²) stops describing a cusp;
  - a tolerance at or past r/2, where the automatic stepover √(8·r·tol) reaches 2r.
  It's a refusal rather than a clamp, so the generator never uses a number the user didn't give.
- **Not built:** a wider second scan read flat rasters exactly up to s = 5.9, but falsely flagged crowns and corners in 11 finish3d verdict fixtures, so it was reverted. The reach's valid range is documented in `ridge::reach`; the follow-up is #212.
- One test changed: `the_authored_ladder_spaces_the_rings_and_says_nothing_elsewhere` had steep stepover 8 on a 6 mm ball, now 5.

## Pins (`crates/motion/tests/scallop_ceiling.rs`, 4)

Stepover and steep stepover at, just past and well past the diameter are refused; just under generates. Tolerance at and past r/2 is refused; just under generates. Degenerate diameters, tolerances and stepovers are refused by name.

## Readings

- **Release:** finish3d 88/88 (heavy lane included), flow 15, scallop_ceiling 4.
- **Debug:** ridge_rest 4.
- **App suites that use 3D finishing, after merging main:** area_controls, center_cut_multiaxis, golden_cl, operations, posed_contact, project_roundtrip, ribbon, tool_gate, tool_law, verify, posting. All green.
- **Clippy:** clean on motion and sim.

Changelog: 3D finish refuses a stated stepover or steep stepover at or past the ball diameter, and a tolerance at or past half the ball radius, by name ("the scallop ceiling"), instead of generating a path whose cusp verified silently

The Fanuc Lathe post can write threads as a two-block G76 cycle.

title: fix(motion): the rotary wrap closes a D-flat bar's seam and refuses open meshes by name
body:
## What changed

The rotary wrap roughs a bar with a D-flat across the seam instead of refusing it as an open mesh.

- Cause: the wrap closed its cover ends with a flat wall at the outermost seam column, sized from the widest radius at each station. A D-flat across the seam leaves the seam column jagged, so the wall touched none of its edges and left loose chord ends ("mesh is open").
- New `multiaxis/rotary_seam.rs` finds the real seam edges: edges whose two triangles sit a full lap apart. It hangs a curtain from each one down to the floor radius, on both copies of the lap. On a plain turned bar this rebuilds the old wall exactly, so the Offset rings output is unchanged.
- Edges held by only one triangle (real holes) get no curtain. An open mesh is now refused by name before the wrap: "the rotary wrap needs a closed solid, but the mesh is open: N edges bound one facet only". On main, a hole no level crossed wrapped silently.
- `rotary_offset.rs` drops the old wall code and is now 390 lines.

## Pins (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_dflat.rs`, all fail on main)

- `a_d_flat_bar_wraps_in_every_placement`: flat through both ends and flat over the middle only, at 4 angles each. No cut tip lands inside the part, and the flat's channel gets cut.
- `a_bar_with_a_hole_in_its_skin_is_still_refused_by_name`
- `a_flat_channel_across_the_seam_is_refused_adaptive_by_name_and_rings_cut_it`: #9's seam law end to end (about 36 s in debug).

- **motion:** rotary 10, rotary_offset 9, rotary_adaptive 1, rotary_links 7, multiaxis 7, multiaxis_avoid 5, multiaxis_rough 5, lib 130, rotary_dflat 3.
- **app:** rotary_verify 9, rotary_fixtures 4, rotary_letter 3, rotary_field_parity 3, golden_cl 23, operations 117, tilt 8.

- **Clippy:** clean on motion and app.

title: fix(motion): the cross-drill station hop clears off-centre mouths
body:
## What changed

The radial cross-drill hop between quarter-turn stations was sized by a closed form that assumes each mouth sits on its station's centre line. An off-centre pair - (8,-6) along -X and (-6,8) along -Y on an r10 bar - chorded 10.757 mm from the spindle, the r2 drill's rim 1.24 mm inside the bar, and #77's rapid proof refused the op (safe, but an ordinary pair of cross holes could not be drilled).

- `traverse_s` (crates/motion/src/drilling/cross.rs) now takes the two holes. It keeps the closed form `hop_s * sqrt(2 / (1 + cos dtheta))` whenever that plane already clears - every on-centre pair, so existing chains and goldens do not move - and otherwise measures the chord between the two real hop points (new `chord_reach`, segment-to-spindle distance in XY), grows the plane until the closest approach reaches `hop_s`, then bisects back to the smallest clear plane. Opposite stations still take the end-face detour.
- Decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` (#81).

## Readings

The pair now drills: no post-blocking warning, every rapid keeps the r2 rim outside the r10 bar. No golden file changed.

## Gate (own worktree build, current main)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests`: green except `swarf_pose_continuity` x2 (known pre-existing on main).
- Every app binary touching cross/lathe/mill-turn drilling (drilling_cross*, lathe_*, stitch_cross, golden_cl, solid_law_goldens, ...): green except `drilling_axial::a_drill_where_the_model_has_no_hole_is_convicted` (known pre-existing on main).

title: fix(motion): the lathe axis reader reads short turned bars from their facing flats
body:
## What changed

The lathe axis reader reads a short turned bar about its true axis instead of refusing it as "every axis fits".

- Cause: the r10×40 bar alone sits just under the isotropy threshold. One modelled radial hole tips it over, and even with the check skipped it drags the plain least-squares line 0.39 mm off the axis, so it's refused anyway.
- New `multiaxis/axis_poles.rs`: facing flats as candidate axes. Facets sharing one normal (a normal and its opposite count as one axis) that carry ≥ 5% of the area become candidates, up to 3. They're always offered beside the two eigenvector candidates, which are unreliable near isotropy, and they're the only candidates when the moment is isotropic. Eigen candidates win ties. The existing concurrency and coarseness tests still decide which passes.
- Hole drag: if the plain line about a flat-end candidate fails, it's refit on the half of the normal lines that miss it least, iterated until that half stops changing. It must then pass the full test over every facet.
- A sphere has no flat and a cube's faces fail coarseness, so both are still refused by name.
- `axis::try_axis` and `axis_robust::dist` are now visible to sibling modules. `axis.rs` is 399 lines.

## Pins

- `drilling_cross_spindle::a_short_punched_bar_reads_as_turned_about_its_axis` (r10×40 with one hole, axis within 1e-6): **fails on main**
- `axis_poles::tests::an_l_d_1_5_bar_fits_its_true_axis_lying_down`: **fails on main**
- `an_l_d_2_bar_fits_its_true_axis`, `a_cube_is_still_refused_by_name`, `a_sphere_is_still_refused_by_name`

## Readings

- motion: lib 134, multiaxis*, rotary* green
- app: drill_reach, drilling_cross* (all), lathe_cross_drill, lathe_spindle_*, turning and turning_* green
- clippy on motion and app is clean

title: feat(sim): one eikonal pass re-normalises the stock view's band before the render
body:
## What changed

One local eikonal pass re-normalises the stock view's narrow band before the render.

- New `FieldLattice::renormalize()` in `stock_sim/preview/eikonal.rs`. It's one round of fast sweeping (Zhao, Math. Comp. 2005; also Sussman–Smereka–Osher and Russo–Smereka): the eikonal update applied once in each of the 8 sweep orders, over band texels only.
- It's called in `PackedBase::of` (`app/src/stock_view.rs`) before the GPU upload. A refusal is logged and the lattice is used as it was.
- The surface stays put:
  - texels next to an opposite-sign texel are frozen, bit for bit;
  - every other texel keeps its sign and never reaches 0;
  - texels at or past `cap` are untouched, and new values are capped at `cap`.
- Only the mesh layer is rewritten; the cut layer is unchanged, so later playback frames stay sign-correct.
- Display only: the verdict paths (`march`, `deviate_field`) still read the sparse field. The CPU `preview()` is unchanged.
- Cost: one classification pass, then 8 updates per band texel. It's deterministic, and bounded by the 8M-texel pack limit; the CSG test froze 3,837 and solved 15,211 texels.

## Pins (`crates/sim/tests/stock_eikonal.rs`, 6, plus a unit test)

- After cuts (cylinder pocket, ball slot, flat slot): mean ||∇φ|−1| drops from 0.367 to 0.048 (bound < 0.08), and texels within 0.1 of a unit gradient rise from 2% to 83%. A second round changes nothing.
- Every sign is kept, and every zero-crossing edge's ends are bit-identical.
- The cylinder pocket is within 0.21 of the exact distance at a 0.5 cell. Under the uncut top face the field reads exactly 5 − z.
- Out-of-band texels are untouched, the cut layer is unchanged, nothing exceeds `cap`, and results are deterministic. A malformed lattice is refused.

## Readings

`cargo test -p camcraft-sim` all green except overhang_laws (3), which fails identically on main (#202). app stock_view 4 and stock_play 7 pass; clippy on sim and app is clean; no snapshot changed.

Changelog: The stock view's narrow band is re-normalized by one eikonal (fast-sweeping) pass before the render, so shading reads a true distance gradient; sign and surface unchanged

Fixes #22

title: feat: align a work offset 3-2-1 from a face, an edge and a vertex or bore
body:
## What changed

A 3-2-1 (plane-line-point, CMM-style) work-offset alignment from picks, so a model no longer has to be rotated to fit the WCS.

- `camcraft_app::pick::align_321(world, picks)` (new `crates/app/src/pick/align.rs`) reads the open operation's picks as datums:
  - exactly one **flat face** → WCS **Z** (its outward normal, from the facets' winding),
  - exactly one **straight open edge** → **X** (projected into that plane; refused when it stands within 5° of square to the face),
  - at most one **origin**: a vertex, or a curved face / bore (its centre) - projected onto the face. X runs from the edge end nearer the origin; with no origin pick, the origin is the edge's start.
  - The frame becomes roll/pitch/yaw (Shepperd matrix → quaternion → `quat_to_euler`), finite-checked.
- UI: an **Align WCS (3-2-1)** button under the Geometry picks queues the existing undoable `SetWcs` into the WCS pane's slot (`vertex_pick::queue_wcs_321`). It is dark until the picks qualify, with the app's refusal as its tooltip.
- No new command: `SetWcsOrigin` already carries a rotation.
- Snapshots `egui_app.png` / `egui_app_light.png` move by the new (dark) button only. **They overlap PR #188's snapshot change** - whichever merges second regenerates them.
- Decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` (#187).

title: feat(sim): lathe stock sim cuts groove, part and form tools with their true blade profile
body:
## What changed

The lathe stock sim cuts groove/part and form tools (and axial, meridian thread passes) with their true blade profile instead of refusing them (`LATHE_BLADE_REFUSAL` is gone). A helical program - the Threading op's half-turn passes - is refused by name at plan time (`LATHE_THREAD_REFUSAL`; any other tool arcing about the spindle: `LATHE_HELIX_REFUSAL`), never revolved into rings of cut crests.

- New `stock_sim/field_blade.rs`, `LatheProfile`:
  - **Nose:** inserts and boring bars, unchanged.
  - **Blade:** a rectangle of `width` with `corner_r` corners.
  - **Thread:** a V at `tip_angle`, truncated at `width` (the crest).
  - **Form:** the crown arc of `nose_radius` across `width`, as straight segments with ends on the arc, under-reading by at most 1e-4 mm and never over-cutting. A form band wider than its crown, or a NaN/oversize blade corner, refuses by name at plan time (no clamp, no rectangle stand-in).
- The same reading as #103's rapid law: the tip sits at the centre of the width and the body extends outward. Body height is the tool's `flute_len` (the field is finite).
- An exact swept distance per move; a part-off past the centre is handled.
- New `Stock::simulate_lathe_profile`; `simulate_lathe`/`_about` call it with the nose shape. Entry points moved to `field_lathe.rs` (`backend.rs` 455 â†’ 410).
- App: `LathePlan` carries the profile from the tool; a blade's display cell is sized from half its width. The column verdict still refuses lathe programs by name.

## Pins

- Decisions: `docs/decisions/21-blade-sweep.md`.
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_lathe_blade.rs` (5): every cell is checked against a fine-stamped true profile. Plunge groove with corner, part-off past centre, two-pass 60Â° thread and form sink each have **0 under-cut, 0 beyond resolution** (13kâ€“22k cells each). Nonsense profiles are refused by name.
- `lathe_field_tools::a_generated_threading_op_refuses_the_field_by_name`: a generated Threading op through `field_view_with` gets the named thread refusal, not the "skewed chord" error (fails without the gate).
- `lathe_field_tools::a_generated_form_op_cuts_its_crown_on_the_field`: a generated FormTurning op cuts its valley at every azimuth and leaves steel beside and under it.
- `lathe_field_sim::a_grooving_blade_cuts_its_rectangle_and_the_verdict_refuses_the_lathe` replaces the old refusal test: 0 sign misses over 439k cells.

## Readings

- **sim:** lib and all stock suites green.
- **app:** lathe_field_sim, lathe_field_tools, every turning_* suite, and the stock_*/sim suites green after merging main (75d1b30).
- **Clippy:** clean on sim and app.
- **Goldens:** none changed.

title: feat(sim): state and optionally enforce the rotary flute-rotation bound
body:
## What changed

The rotary stock sim states, and can enforce, its flute-rotation bound.

- In `stock_sim/field_rotary.rs`, the rotary chord pre-pass cuts each sub-chord with the whole tool at the sub-chord's mid pose while the real pose keeps turning. The old chord count bounded only the sag at the tool's far reach; the flank error, which grows with distance up the tool, was never stated.
- New `RotaryChordStats::flute_shift = L·2·sin(half/2)`: the rigid-rotation chord bound (Craig, *Introduction to Robotics*, ch. 2). `L` is the distance from the tip to the field box's farthest corner (plus r for a ball), capped at shank + r. Together with `center_sag` it gives a two-sided bound, so any point farther than that from the true surface reads steel or air correctly.
- New `Stock::simulate_rotary_bounded(.., Some(tol))` / `ChordLaw::flute_tol` adds sub-chords until `flute_shift ≤ tol`. Past `MAX_SUBCHORDS` it refuses by name rather than coarsening.
- `simulate_rotary` and its app callers are unchanged in cost and output. Enforcing by default would cost 3×–1000× the sub-chords for a precision no current consumer reads.
- "Never smaller than the reference" can't hold: a chorded solid is neither a superset nor a subset of the true sweep. RECOMMENDED.md has the reasoning.

## Agreement tests (`crates/sim/tests/stock_rotary_flute.rs`)

A d6 end mill turning 30° around a d20 bar, checked at every cut cell against a 4,001-pose brute-force reference:

- Unenforced, beyond the stated bound: 0 wrong of 17,144.

title: fix(app): a boring bar's body is judged on its cutting feeds
body:
## What changed

A boring bar's body is now judged on its cutting feeds, not only on its rapids.

- New `operation/turning_feeds.rs` walks each feed of a bore op. title: feat(cli): camcraft-cli mcp - a stdio MCP server for AI agents
body:
## What changed

First slice of #128: `camcraft-cli mcp`, a stdio MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0: initialize, tools/list, tools/call) that lets an AI agent drive one document headless, with no GUI and no GPU.

- 17 tools, each with a JSON input schema:
  - `open_project`, `save_project`, `import_model`, `get_job`
  - `list_operation_types`, `list_tool_catalog`
  - `add_tool`, `set_stock`
  - `add_operation`, `edit_operation` (a JSON merge patch on the `.camproj` param shape; a field the kind doesn't have is refused by name), `delete_operation`, `set_tool`
  - `undo`, `redo`, `generate`
  - `verify` (findings as data: op, move, kind, message, whether it blocks; plus the post gate's problems)
  - `post`
- Every change is a real command through the document's History, so undo/redo walk exactly what the agent did, and refused commands never enter it.
- It reuses the job-script engine's document and History, and calls the existing script commands directly, without the JS engine.
- Errors come back as tool errors, never panics; each call is wrapped so a generator panic becomes a tool error.
- No new dependency: the protocol is about 150 lines of serde_json. `rmcp` (MIT) was passed over because it pulls in tokio.
- New `crates/app/src/mcp/` (mod, tools, job, edit) and `project/json.rs`.

## Pins (`tests/mcp.rs`)

- `handshake_and_tool_list`
- `a_whole_job_over_the_tools`: import STL → stock → tool → Face op → edit → generate → verify → post Fanuc → undo/redo → save → delete → reopen

title: fix(app): cross-hole entry reads an unwelded round at its true surface
body:
## What changed

The chord-sag allowance moved out of `cross_entry.rs` into a new `operation/cross_sag.rs`, which now welds vertices before matching edges. A non-conforming STL round whose facets share no vertices gets the same allowance as a welded one, so the cross-hole mouth and the #84 shank reach read the true surface, not the chords.

- Weld tolerance: 1e-6 × the model's bounding diagonal, with a floor of 1e-9 mm. The only importer weld tolerance is the user's `RepairModel` parameter, so there's no default to reuse.
- Spatial hash: cells the size of the tolerance, a 27-cell lookup, and the earliest vertex in input order wins. It's O(n), deterministic and saturating, so nothing can panic. Edges that collapse to one point are skipped.
- The dihedral and width rules are unchanged; a larger allowance only moves the entry outward, into air.

## Pins

- `operation::cross_entry::tests::an_unwelded_round_is_entered_and_reached_as_the_welded_one`: entry and reach match the welded mesh within 1e-9 and sit at or outside the true surface. **Fails on main**: 4.283 unwelded against 4.948 welded.
- `operation::cross_sag::tests::an_unwelded_round_edge_carries_the_allowance_and_an_open_edge_none`: the unwelded half fails on main; a real open edge still gets 0.

## Readings

app lib 68; drill_reach 6, drill_reach_fit 3, drilling_cross 9, _box 7, _part 3, _rapids 2, _spindle 6, _stock 8, lathe_cross_drill 4; clippy on app is clean.

Changelog: Cross-hole entry and shank reach read a non-conforming (unwelded) STL round at its true surface, not its chords

title: feat: Probe operation - face, edge, corner and bore/boss centre finding
body:
## What changed

A touch-probe tool type and a **Probe** operation that finds a face, an edge, an outside corner, or a bore/boss centre, then sets a work offset (G54-G59) or stops for the operator. A found position outside the tolerance stops the program with a message.

- **Tool:** `ToolKind::Probe` - `diameter` is the stylus ball, `flute_len` the stylus length, corner = ball radius. The starter catalog gains `PRB-0400` (4 mm ball, 30 mm stylus).
- **Operation:** modes face (+-X/+-Y/-Z), edge, outside corner (two touches), bore centre and boss centre (four touches each). Every parameter has a default: approach clearance, probe distance (overtravel), back-off, seek and measure feeds, depth, corner inset, tolerance, result action. Created and edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`, so edits undo.
- **Stable ids:** Probe is appended as kind id 38, so no existing op type id, digest tag or ribbon pin moves. The project format stays v50 and old projects load with no op going Stale. The menu lists Probe in the Drilling section by display order; the ribbon laws now ask for table order within a section instead of a contiguous run.
- **Motion:** each touch is a fast seek, a back-off and a slow measuring re-probe, after an opening positioning rapid. The moves stay the nominal truth; `Toolpath::probes` (`cl::ProbeTouch`) marks which feeds are probing moves, their probe target and the measurement number. The project file saves them, so a reloaded op can never post a probe move as a plain feed.
- **Post:** neutral stream records `TOUCH` / `RETREAT` / `FOUND` and hooks `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult`, with no prelude default.
  - `fanuc.cps` writes G31 skip blocks with custom macro B. The trip is read from `#5061`-`#5063` and kept in `#100+3k`.
  - Each skip block is followed by a no-contact alarm (`#3000=2`).
  - The back-off is incremental (G91), so a part nearer than the model is never driven into.
  - Then the tolerance stop (`#3000=1`), and `G10 L2 Pn` from `#5221 + 20 x slot`, or `#3006=1` to stop for the operator.
  - A probe section starts no spindle and no coolant.
  - Every other post refuses the op by name (`probing: operation "Probe1": this post script does not define onProbeMove ...`).
- **Verify/sim:** probe moves are protected moves. The stylus ball is swept along every move against the model, and coming nearer than its radius anywhere is a `Gouge`, which holds the post. Probe ops skip the cutting and turning laws and remove no stock in the sim or the rest masks.
- **UI:** the op appears in the operation menu with an original icon (`assets/ui/probe.png`, recorded in `LICENSES.md`) and a parameter page.
- Decisions are recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md` under "#108 - Probe".

## Caveat: G31 on a real control

The G31 / custom macro B output is unverified on a real control. The skip-position variables (`#5061`-`#5063`), the work-offset variables (`#5221 + 20 x slot`) and the `#3000` / `#3006` stops come from Fanuc's public operator documentation as I understand it; no controller or simulator has run this code. **Check the control's manual before running it on a machine.** The golden locks the text, not the machine behaviour.

## Pins (`crates/app/tests/probe_op.rs`, 10 tests)

- `each_mode_lays_down_its_touches` - generation for all five modes, with the expected touches.
- `bore_centre_posts_g31_skips_on_the_generic_dialect` - golden `tests/golden/nc/fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc`; also checks the stream round-trips.
- `a_dialect_without_probing_refuses_the_op_by_name` - the Heidenhain refusal.
- `the_probe_round_trips_through_the_project_file`
- `a_probe_param_edit_undoes_and_redoes`
- `a_stylus_driven_through_material_is_a_gouge`
- `a_face_touch_on_the_stock_top_generates_clean_and_cuts_nothing`
- `degenerate_probe_numbers_are_refused`
- `the_probe_row_appends_and_lists_in_drilling`
- `every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag`

Also `ribbon::the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`.

## Readings (after merging origin/main)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-app lib (incl. registry and `turning_rapids` tests) | 74 passed |
| probe_op | 10 passed |
| ribbon | 11 passed |
| project_roundtrip | 68 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| operations | 117 passed, 6 ignored (heavy lane) |
| vertical_rapid_stock | 4 passed |
| camcraft-sim vertical_rapids | 16 passed |
| camcraft-post post_engine / comp | 30 / 6 passed |

Clippy `-D warnings`, all targets, on tools / cl / motion / sim / post / app / ui: clean. Before the merge, all camcraft-app test binaries except the slow `center_cut_multiaxis` passed, as did cl, tools, the motion lib and `one_descent`, and the sim lib and touched tests. UI test binaries compile but were not run, because they open the GUI.

## Owed

- #171 - create the op from a picked face, edge, vertex or cylinder (the contact point is typed today)
- #172 - include the stylus shank and probe body in the collision check
- #173 - probing hooks for the Haas, Mazak, Siemens and Heidenhain posts
- #174 - a stop-on-contact (G38.3-style) protected descent before each touch

Changelog: Probe operation: face, edge, outside-corner and bore/boss-centre finding with a touch probe - G31 skip touches on the Fanuc post with a no-contact alarm, set G54-G59 or stop for the operator, out-of-tolerance stop; posts that cannot probe refuse it by name (#108)

title: feat(post): one NC file per operation
body:
Stacked on #161 (issue/110-pause-home) → #147 (issue/112-coolant). Retarget each to main before its parent merges.

## What changed

A post "Output" option: **One program** (the default; byte-identical output, goldens unchanged) or **One file per operation**.

- Per-op files are named `<program>_<nn>_<op>.<ext>`. The program part is the project file name, or `program` if unsaved. `nn` is in program order with at least two digits. The op part keeps letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 48 characters. The extension comes from the post script.
- Each file is the op posted on its own through the same post: header and units, its own tool change, safe start (G90, the work offset, G40/G49/G80, that op's spindle and coolant) and its own end (M9, M5, home, M30). There's no extra retract ahead of the op's own clearance move, the same as op 1 in the combined program (RECOMMENDED.md).
- Suppressed ops get no file. Fanuc, Mazak and Fanuc Lathe count O0001, O0002…; Haas, Siemens and Heidenhain write no O-word, as today.
- A refusal anywhere writes nothing: the job checks run once, and every op's own post must come back with no warnings. Files go to a temp folder and are renamed into place, and a failed rename rolls back the files already moved.
- `PostOptions.per_op`, set via the existing undoable `SetPostOptions`. It's saved as `per_op_files` only when it's on.
- UI: with per-op chosen, Post asks for a folder, and the NC viewer shows the first file.
- New `posting_per_op.rs` and `state_per_op.rs`.

## Pins

- `per_op_files` (9):
  - `a_two_op_job_writes_two_standalone_programs`
  - `a_suppressed_op_writes_no_file`
  - `file_names_are_sanitised`
  - `a_numbering_dialect_counts_its_o_word_per_file`

title: fix(motion): the lathe axis fit tightens its band so one cross hole no longer leans it
body:
## What changed

`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_robust.rs`: once the robust lathe axis fit settles, its inlier band shrinks from 3% of the bar's radius (0.3 mm on r10) to 4× the kept facets' median miss, with a floor of 1e-9 × the radius, and the line is refitted. This repeats while the band keeps shrinking.

- Facets of a true cylinder, cone or end face meet the axis exactly, so they stay in. A cross hole's mouth ring and its floor strip sit near the axis plane but not in it, so they drop out.
- Every tightened refit must pass the same checks as before, including the full judgement over all facets. A refit that fails isn't taken, and the last trusted fit stands. A fit that can't be trusted is still refused by name.
- An exact revolve keeps its plain fit bit for bit. The spindle law's 0.0005 mm is untouched.
- `tests/punched_bar`: #117's mirror-hole workaround is removed. The helper that merges duplicates and joins opposite holes stays, renamed `merged`.

## Pins

- `lathe_cross_drill::a_bar_with_one_modelled_cross_hole_fits_on_the_spindle_and_drills_clean`: an r10 bar with one modelled cross hole and no mirror reads exact (worst about 3e-17 mm) and the cross drill posts clean. It **fails on main** (worst 0.00088 mm, over 0.0005).
- `axis_robust::a_near_meridian_strip_is_set_aside_by_the_tightened_band`: **fails on main** (offset 3.3e-4 mm).
- `axis_robust::a_rectangular_prism_is_still_refused_as_not_revolved`: guards against regression.

## Readings

- Cross-drill suites green without the mirrors: drilling_cross_box, _spindle, _stock, drill_reach, drill_reach_fit, lathe_cross_drill 5, drilling_cross, _part, _rapids.
- lathe_spindle_* green; motion lib 128 plus the multiaxis, rotary and turning suites green; clippy on motion and app is clean.
- Only red: the 7 known #159 lathe tests, which fail the same on main and are fixed in PR #135.
- Not fixed by this change: #113 (a 90° keyway still fails the plain fit's 90% check before the robust pass) and #152 (the short-bar isotropy check).

title: fix(app): a stock edit stales every op that read the stock
body:
## What changed

A stock edit after generation now marks every op that read the stock Stale, so the post refuses them until they're regenerated.

- The stock reaches every generator through `job::collect_job`, which hands its facets and bounds to every op whose source isn't the stock itself. That feeds the clearance top, the rapid-in-stock checks (vertical, footprint), the prior acquittal, the plunge-solid checks, the cross-drill standoff, the axial drill's reach and R plane, and the lathe meridian bar. The set is made explicit and tested as `operation::reads_setup_stock`: every op with a part or selection source.
- Those stamps carry a stock term: whether a stock exists, its placement, its mesh hash, and its shape kind and size. Offsets land in the placement or the size. Ops sourced from the stock already digested it; that code moved byte-for-byte into the new `operation/stamp_stock.rs`, so those ops don't go Stale. The old Drill-only stock term is replaced by the general one. `stamp.rs` is down from 400 to 356 lines.
- The term is separate from PR #153's digest of the ops ahead.
- **One-time effect:** saved projects show every op with a part or selection source as Stale once. Regenerating clears it.

## Pins (`crates/app/tests/stock_stamp.rs`)

- `enlarging_the_stock_over_a_contours_dive_stales_it_and_blocks_the_post`: fails on main
- `moving_the_stock_stales_the_contour`: fails on main
- `undoing_the_stock_edit_returns_the_contour_to_ok`, which also checks the post goes through again: fails on main
- `the_work_material_is_not_a_stock_input`

## Readings

All app test binaries except the slow center_cut_multiaxis: 965 passed, 7 failed, 17 ignored. The 7 are #159's lathe failures, identical on main and fixed in PR #135. Clippy on app is clean.

title: feat(post): Tormach PathPilot post and 770MX machine; machine units reach posts
body:
## What changed

Adds Tormach support for #131: a **Tormach PathPilot** post and a **Tormach 770MX** machine. This first PR is 3-axis only. The contributor's own MicroArc 4th axis is left for a follow-up.

### The post, `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (registry name `Tormach PathPilot`)
It's built on `haas.cps`'s structure, with the PathPilot/LinuxCNC rules from Tormach's and LinuxCNC's public documentation (sources are in the file's provenance header):
- **Program framing:**
  - No `%` fence, as Tormach's post guidelines ask, and no `O` program number, because LinuxCNC reads an O word as a subroutine label.
  - The program opens with a `( )` name comment and ends with `M30`.
- **Header:**
  - The modal state: `G20`/`G21`, `G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`. Incremental arc centers are stated explicitly rather than assumed.
  - Path blending on its own line, `G64 P0.001` (in) or `P0.025` (mm). A bare `G64` means no tolerance at all in plain LinuxCNC.
- **Units come from the machine:** an inch `.mch` posts `G20`, with every length divided by 25.4 at 4 decimals and every feed divided by 25.4 at 2 decimals. A metric machine posts `G21` and mm, as before.
- **Tool changes:**
  - `G53 G0 Z0`, then `G30`, before every `T.. M6`. Tormach recommends the G30, and none of its documentation says M6 moves to a safe position by itself. A bare G30 can move X, Y and Z together, so Z goes straight up first, the same Z-first order PathPilot's own programs use between tools.
  - Then `G43 H..`, which picks up the length the tool table holds (measured by the electronic tool setter).
  - Tool numbers outside PathPilot's 1–1000 table are refused by name.
  - **X/Y first:** X and Y are unknown at program start and after every G30. So the first move after a tool change is preceded by `G0 X.. Y..` alone, at the Z-up height (a rapid's target, a feed or arc's start point, or a cycle's first hole), and only then does Z come down. This is PathPilot's own XY-first order. Then, for a first move that is a feed (a face plunges from its clearance start), it rapids Z down to the stream's start height, so the feed runs only the planned stretch instead of the whole stroke from the top of Z at the plunge rate (85baabe). It was found by the PathPilot Hub v2.14.4 simulator, which warned: "Axis XY not specified by this or previous motions, end point will depend on current position".
- **Belt range:** the 770 family has a manual belt (low 175–3250 rpm, high 525–10000 rpm) and no G or M code can change it. When a speed fits only one range, the program says which in a comment before the spindle starts.
- **Canned cycles:**
  - G73, G81, G82, G83, G86 and G89, with G98.
  - Dwell `P` in **seconds**, as LinuxCNC reads it; Fanuc-family controls read milliseconds.
  - `G84` tapping with no P: Tormach documents G84 for PathPilot, PathPilot sizes the bottom dwell itself, and the MX mills tap from the spindle encoder.
- **Program end:** `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `M30`. Z goes straight up to the top of travel in machine coordinates, then the machine moves to the operator's preset G30 location. That is the order PathPilot's own Conversational programs end in.
- **Refused by name, like the other non-Fanuc posts:** cutter compensation in the control, and tilted (RTCP) moves.

### The machine, `assets/machines/tormach-770mx.mch` (library entry `Tormach 770MX`)
- **Values:** all in inches, from Tormach's "UM10587: 770MX Operator's Manual" (0626A), §2.1–2.2:
  - travel X 14, Y 7.5, Z 13.25 in, stated as bands in **program coordinates**, the full stroke each way (X ±14, Y ±7.5, Z ±13.25 in). The machine check reads travel relative to the work offset, and where G54 sits is the operator's choice. A machine-style band (Z −13.25..0) blocked every clearance move above G54 Z0; the first real GUI job refused to post that way. Fixed in b189c96 and pinned by `tormach_post::a_face_job_on_the_built_in_770mx_passes_the_gate_and_posts_inch`;
  - spindle 175–10000 rpm, 1.1 kW;
  - 300 ipm on X and Y, 250 ipm on Z;
  - a 10-tool ATC;
  - Flood M8 and Mist M7.
- **Not stated:** the spindle body size and tool-length limits. Tormach doesn't publish them, so the machine check doesn't test against them.

### Small core change: the machine's units reach the post
`.mch` files could already be in inches, but the parser scaled everything to mm and dropped the unit, so a post couldn't tell an inch machine from a metric one.
- `Machine` gains `units: Option<String>`: `Some("inch")` when the file states inches. It's skipped when `None`, so project files don't change.
- The post mirror and `script_props` expose it as `machine.units` (`"inch"` or `"mm"`), the prelude defaults it to `"mm"`, and `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents it.
- The other shipped posts ignore the field, so their goldens don't move.

## Readings

- **Suites that pass:**
  - `conformance` (6, with the new `nc/tormach/` goldens)
  - `tormach_post` (7, new)
  - `machine` (32)
  - `posting` (17)
  - `fanuc_post` (8)
  - `control_comp` (4)
  - `arc_planes` (8)
  - `vertical_arc_entry` (3)
  - `camcraft-post` (all)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets`: clean.
- `scripting` (17): `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` is regenerated for the post-name list.
- **Failing, but also failing on `main` without this PR:**
  - `lathe_post::facing_posts_to_the_lathe_golden` (the posted program now carries verify warnings)
  - 3 tests each in `turning_bore` and `turning_contour`, all reporting `RapidInStock`
  - the two cross-drill tests in #151
  - on this Mac, the three headless-GPU UI tests (no fallback graphics adapter)
- **PathPilot Hub v2.14.4 (simulator):** all five samples load.
  - `01-face`: its X/Y warning is fixed by 9cb46a6. A "Y exceeds machine maximum" warning came from where the simulator's G54 sat, not from the post.
  - `02-contour`, `03-pocket`, `04-peck-drill`: clean.
  - `05-tap`: `G84` is accepted, but the simulator stops every rigid tap with "Spindle reversal exceeded maximum overshoot". It stops at a constant ~9 spindle turns at both 300 and 800 rpm, with the simulated spindle not running, so this is the simulator's limit; the real machine (below) taps clean.
- **Real Tormach 770MX (contributor's machine), air cuts, PathPilot 2.14.4:**
  - `01-face`, `02-contour`, `03-pocket`, `04-peck-drill`: run to the end, including the real ATC tool changes (Z up, `G30`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, X/Y first) and the `G73` peck.
  - `05-tap` (`G84`, 600 rpm, `F15`, high belt): runs to the end with no overshoot error, so rigid tapping works as posted.
  - Its "Program exceeds machine maximum on Z" warnings came from where G54 Z and the tool length sat in the air-cut setup, and cleared as G54 Z was lowered.
  - `05b-tap-300rpm` (low belt only): PathPilot refused S300 in the high range, then timed out reaching 300 rpm when the range setting didn't match the belt's pulley position. That's an operator setup step, and it's exactly what the post's "NEEDS THE LOW BELT RANGE" comment flags.
- **First real job (GUI → post → 770MX):** Face + 2D Contour, G54 Z0 on the stock top, T31 measured by the tool setter. It ran correctly with two hand edits to the posted file: T/H renumbered to 31 (#221), and a rapid to clearance before the face's first feed (now done by the post, 85baabe).
- **Known limit (separate issue #221):** CamCraft has no per-tool number, so `T`/`H` are the tool's position in the document's tool list. For ATC jobs, keep the document's tool order the same as the PathPilot tool table until #221 lands.

## Pinning tests

- `tormach_post::the_machine_file_states_inches_and_the_script_sees_them`
- `tormach_post::a_pathpilot_program_has_no_fence_and_no_o_or_n_words`
- `tormach_post::an_inch_machine_posts_every_length_and_feed_in_inches`
- `tormach_post::a_dwell_posts_in_seconds`
- `tormach_post::a_tap_posts_g84_with_its_feed_and_no_dwell_word`
- `tormach_post::the_belt_range_is_named_and_a_stray_tool_number_is_refused`
- `tormach_post::the_registry_ships_the_tormach_post_for_mills`
- `tormach_post::every_tool_change_lifts_z_before_g30` (two tools)
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up`
- `conformance::every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` (new `nc/tormach/` goldens) and `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`
- `machine::every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration` (the new library entry)
- The Tormach post joins the existing refusal tests: `non_rtcp_dialects_refuse_a_tilted_stream`, and the two control-compensation refusal tests in `control_comp` and `crates/post/tests/comp.rs`.

## Notes for review

- **Checked against PathPilot's own output:** the contributor shared programs written by PathPilot Conversational: rectangular and spiral facing (2.12), and circular drilling and external thread milling (2.14.4), all with defaults and in inch. They were used to check behaviour only; no text was copied. The post matches them on:
  - no `%` and no O word;
  - `G20` and `G17 G90`;
  - Z lifted before the `G30` that precedes `T.. M6`, then `G43 H..`;
  - drilling: `G98`, `G81` and `G83 … Q`, bare X Y lines for the following holes, and `G80`;
  - `M9`/`M5`, then ending at the G30 preset, then `M30`.

  Where it differs, on purpose:
  - **Blending:** PathPilot's default is `G64 P0.005 Q0`. This post writes `G64 P0.001`, a tighter tolerance for CAM finishing paths, so it is a little slower at corners and easy to loosen if hardware tests say so.
  - **Order and layout:** coolant and spindle come in the other order, and T/M6/G43 sit on separate lines. Both are equivalent to the controller.

- **Specs from the manual:** the 770MX operator's manual settles two figures the web pages disagreed on: 250 ipm on Z, and belt ranges of 175–3250 / 525–10000 rpm.
- **The dialect checked against the manual:** chapter 10 (G-codes, canned cycles, M-codes) and the G30 sections confirm what the post writes: dwell P in seconds, `G91.1` as the default arc mode, `G64 P~ Q~`, `G84` with an optional P (the manual's own example has none), a G30 right before tool changes, and `Txx M06` loading from the ATC or pausing for a manual change. The post's provenance header cites the manual.
- **G84 on non-MX machines:** non-MX 770s (R8 spindle) may not rigid-tap. Telling those machines apart needs a capability flag in the machine file, which is a possible follow-up.
- **`post` CLI:** given a checker-layout `.mch` (like `vmc.mch` or this file), the CLI reads the units but not the machine name or coolant codes. That limitation already exists for `vmc.mch`; the app path (`posting::machine_value`, parser then mirror) reads all three.

Changelog: New Tormach PathPilot post and Tormach 770MX machine; a machine file in inches now posts inch (G20) programs through posts that read `machine.units`

Refs #131. Partial on purpose: the issue stays open until the contributor's PathPilot Hub and on-machine checks report back, and for the MicroArc 4th axis.

title: feat(post): pause or home after an operation, suppress, skip pauses; one NC file per operation
body:
Carries #175 (one NC file per operation, merged into this branch), so this PR closes both #110 and #111. Base is now `main` (its old base #147 has merged), and current main (1da9695) is merged in.

## What changed

**#110: pause or home after an operation, suppress, skip pauses**
- **After this operation** (per op): Continue (the default), Optional stop, Program stop or Go home. Continue writes nothing, so goldens don't change. Any other choice adds one `PARAM AfterOperation optional-stop|stop|home`. The post writes it after the op's spindle stop:
  - Fanuc, Haas, Mazak: M1 / M0 / `G91 G28 Z0`, `G28 X0 Y0`, `G90`. On Fanuc, `G49` comes first when TCPM is armed.
  - Siemens 840D: `G0 G53 Z0`, then XY.
  - Fanuc Lathe: M01 / M00 / `G28 U0` then `G28 W0`.
  - Heidenhain: M1 / M0. Go home is refused, naming the op.
- **`afterModes = true`** (review B2) is a manifest flag, set in the six posts that write `afterOp()`. If a script doesn't declare it, the engine refuses any stop or home ask and names the op: `operation X: asks a program stop after it, but this post script does not declare afterModes ...`. Tormach (new on main) doesn't write after-actions yet, so it refuses the ask instead of running past it.
- **Suppress** (per op) leaves the op out of the NC and keeps its toolpath. A suppressed stale op doesn't block the post. If every op is suppressed, the post refuses.
  - New (review B1): `verification_report` refuses when a posted op that reads the program ahead has a suppressed op ahead of it in its setup, and that op cut something: `operation Rest2 was generated against the cut of suppressed Rough1; unsuppress Rough1 or suppress Rest2 too`. Suppressing an op that nothing later depends on still posts.
- **Skip pauses and homes** is a document switch that removes every after-action. It is undoable.

**#111: one NC file per operation**
- An Output choice: One program, or One file per operation, written as `<program>_<nn>_<op>.<ext>` into a folder. Each file is a standalone program. Files are written all-or-nothing, and suppressed ops get no file. It now also posts with the document's post options (#34) through `engine::run_numbered_with`.

**Merge with main**
- Main's `PostOptions` (#34, threading) and this branch's version are merged into one singleton `{ threading, skip_stops, per_op }` with one `SetPostOptions` command. The project reader lands all three fields in one write; before, a second write wiped `threading`.
- The posts keep main's coolant, wear comp, threading, probe, C-axis live tooling and Tormach changes.
- Cycle anchors in the combined stream use main's motion count (Move, Touch and Retreat).
- This branch's RECOMMENDED.md entries moved to `docs/decisions/110-pause-home.md` and `111-nc-per-op.md`. The review-fix decisions are recorded there too.

## Pins
- `suppressed_rest::suppressing_a_cut_a_later_op_was_generated_against_refuses_by_name` (B1). It checks the combined and per-op posts and the way out.
- `suppressed_rest::suppressing_an_op_nothing_depends_on_still_posts` (B1)
- `post_engine::a_stop_asked_of_a_script_without_after_modes_is_refused_by_name` (B2)
- `after_op` (10), `per_op_files`. `a_suppressed_op_writes_no_file` now suppresses the last op, since suppressing the first one is refused now.
- ui `after_op_tests`, `state_per_op`

## Readings (worktree, debug, after the merge)
- camcraft-post: comp 9, post_engine 33. All green.
- camcraft-app, 66 suites, all green: after_op, per_op_files, suppressed_rest, posting, conformance, golden_cl, fanuc_post, lathe_post (+g76, refusals), tormach_post, coolant(+followups), wear_comp, control_comp, c_axis_live, probe_op, heidenhain_*, commands_undo, project_roundtrip, operations, remachining, setups, scripting, solid_law(+goldens) and every other suite that calls the post gate.
- ui lib: 282 passed, 2 ignored. No snapshot changes.
- clippy `-D warnings`: clean on post, app and ui.

Changelog: Pause or home after an operation (optional stop, program stop, go home) in each post's own words; Suppress an operation (refused by name when a later op was generated against its cut); a "Skip pauses and homes" post option; and "One file per operation" output (#110, #111)

Fixes #110
Fixes #111

title: fix(sim): judge sideways rapids along their whole length
body:
## What changed

`crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs`: a sideways rapid under the clearance plane is judged along its whole length, not only at its start, mid and end. Each station uses #106's footprint test (8 rings at d·k/8, each judged at the inner ring's tip lift).

- Step: d/8 (the ring spacing; d = r − gouge_tol), floored at 0.01 mm; stations = ceil(len/step), both ends included. The footprint reaches d ahead of and behind each station, so no wall can slip between stations. What's left is the footprint's own sampling bound from #106, which the module doc states.
- It runs whether or not there's a model, since it's independent of `hidden_along`'s early return.
- Cost: 73 samples per station. A rapid that would need more than 2^18 stations (about 98 m for a 6 mm tool) is refused as RapidInStock, not checked coarser, and the doc says so.

## Pins (`crates/sim/tests/sideways_rapids.rs`)

- `a_floor_link_through_a_4mm_wall_between_two_pockets_is_a_rapid_in_stock` (the issue's scenario): fails on main
- `a_floor_link_through_a_1mm_wall_is_a_rapid_in_stock`: fails on main
- `a_long_floor_link_over_a_fully_cut_slot_is_clean`: no warnings at all, guarding against false refusals

## Readings

Green: sim lib 54, vertical_rapids 16, radial_rapids 15, sideways_rapids 3; motion finish3d 55, flow 13, pivot5d 7 (no real link rapid refused); app center_cut_multiaxis 6, verify 21, golden_cl 23, posting 17, vertical_rapid_stock 4; no golden changed; clippy on sim and app is clean.

title: fix(app): a cross drill is judged against the finished part
body:
## What changed

A cross (radial) drill is judged against the finished part, the way the axial drill already is (`drilling::axial_warnings`).

- New `operation/cross_part.rs`: `part_clear()` sweeps the finished chain through the part solid with the solid law (`verify::solid_hits`). Each move is swept along its tool axis with the point cone, shank and holder, within GOUGE_TOL. A hit refuses the op by name. Bisection finds the tip depth at first contact: under one drill radius reads "the model has no hole there", deeper reads "the drill runs past the modelled hole's floor".
- It's called at both return points of `cross_spindle::cross_drill`, in world coordinates, after the reach, holder and rapid checks. It refuses at generation, so nothing reaches the post.
- Fixtures: 22 existing tests drilled bars that had no modelled hole, so the check was right and the fixtures were wrong. The new helper `tests/punched_bar` models real holes:
  - The bar is lengthened to z -80..20, with the top kept at z20. On the old r10 × 40 bar, any modelled cross hole tipped the lathe axis fit into "every axis fits". That's filed as #152.
  - Each modelled hole gets an undrilled mirror hole, so the axis fit doesn't lean past the spindle law's 0.0005 mm (the #116 band). Two holes that meet on one line become one through hole.
  - The mesh is coarser, so every suite stays under 20 s.
  - Off-centre holes the bar can't hold run over a small core, and `drilling_cross_box`'s on-line lump is split into four corner lumps. Both are recorded in RECOMMENDED.md.
  - No asserted number in any existing suite changed.

## Pins (`drilling_cross_part`)

- `a_cross_drill_into_a_solid_bar_is_refused_by_name`: generates on main
- `a_cross_hole_deeper_than_the_modelled_hole_is_refused`: generates on main
- `a_cross_hole_matching_its_modelled_hole_is_clean`

## Readings

Green (debug):
- Cross drilling: drilling_cross 9, _box 7, _part 3, _rapids 2, _spindle 6, _stock 8; lathe_cross_drill 4; stitch_cross 6.
- Other drilling: drill_reach 6, drill_reach_fit 3, drill_prior 10, drill_prior_kinds 4, drill_rplane 8, drilling_axial 7, blind_floor 6, center_cut_owed 3, solid_law 4.
- Everything else: machine 32, lathe_post 5, lathe_spindle_fit 3, lathe_spindle_law 8, posting 17, operations 117.

Clippy on app is clean.

title: fix(ui): ribbon pins go through an undoable SetRibbonPins command
body:
## What changed

Pinning a ribbon cell wrote the `RibbonPins` singleton straight from the pane (`panes.rs` `toggle_pin` → `ribbon::pinned_set`). Pins are saved in the project file, so this was a document change the history never saw: it couldn't be undone and couldn't mark the document unsaved, against AGENTS.md's "Everything Is a Command".

- **New command `SetRibbonPins`** (`crates/app/src/commands/ribbon_pins.rs`, modelled on `SetTheme`). It records the previous and next pin lists, cleans the new list the way `pinned_set` does (duplicates and out-of-range indices dropped), and refuses a no-op, so nothing empty lands on the undo stack.
- **`toggle_pin`** runs the command through `state.history` instead of writing the world directly. The fifth-pin refusal (`MAX_PINS`) still happens before any command is built, so it pushes nothing.
- **Comments:** the M6.2 "pins are layout, not a command" comments in `ribbon.rs`, `schema.rs`, `panes.rs` and the `ribbon` suite header now describe the new behaviour.

**The "goes dirty" half:** PR #141 (#107, unmerged) tracks unsaved changes from the history depth (`History::is_dirty`). Once it lands, a pin marks the document unsaved with no further change. This PR is based on `main`, not stacked on #141, so it can merge on its own. The tests pin the history half now (`can_undo` after a pin). After #141 merges, an `is_dirty()` assertion can go next to them; I'm happy to add it in a follow-up.

## Readings

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test ribbon`: 11 passed (one new).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 237 passed (two new, one updated). The one failure is `headless_run_succeeds`, which also fails on `main` here (macOS: "No suitable graphics adapter found … metal had no fallback adapters", an environment issue).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`: the remaining failures exist without this change too:
  - the three headless-GPU tests (`headless_run_succeeds`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`): no fallback adapter on this Mac
  - the two cross-drill tests in #151

## Pinning tests

- `ribbon::a_pin_is_a_command_undo_restores_the_previous_pins` (app): apply, undo, redo, the cleaned list, and the no-op refusal.
- `egui_app::pin_tests::pinning_a_ribbon_cell_is_undoable` (ui): the real `toggle_pin` gesture walked by Undo/Redo.
- `egui_app::pin_tests::a_refused_fifth_pin_pushes_nothing` (ui).

title: fix(app): ops that read the program ahead go Stale when it changes; one Regenerate All converges
body:
Stacked on #135 (issue/103-turning-axial-rapids). Retarget to main before #135 merges.

## What changed

- **#109:** an op whose rapid verdict reads earlier ops now digests the ops ahead into its generation stamp. That covers verify's prior acquittal (`acquit_by_prior` / `PriorPlan`), the drill prior, and #103's lathe pilot and facing credit; the set is `drill_prior::reads_prior`, matching `job::collect_job`. Editing and regenerating, deleting or reordering an earlier op marks the dependent op Stale, the reason names the op that moved, and the post refuses it. 3+2-posed ops keep their stamps.
- **#145:** Regenerate All runs in rounds. Each round generates every Stale op in program order, writes the results so the next round sees them, and stops when nothing is Stale (capped at the op count; leftovers are reported in `skipped()`). The world is restored after the batch is built and `apply` replays it, so it stays one undo unit. Note that building the batch writes to the world briefly, which is main-thread only (recorded in RECOMMENDED.md).
- The `turning_bore` fixture moved to `tests/common/bore.rs` (the suite was over 400 lines); `stamp.rs` is 399.

title: feat: per-operation coolant (off / flood / mist / through tool)
body:
## What changed

Per-operation coolant choice.

- Each operation gets a coolant mode: Off / Flood (default) / Mist / Through tool. Flood is what every built-in post already emitted, so existing programs post byte-identical.
- The motion stream carries it only when it isn't Flood: a `PARAM Coolant off|mist|through-tool` line before the op. Old streams and `.cl` files post as Flood.
- All six built-in posts take the code from the mounted machine's coolant list (`.mch`), not a hard-coded M7; Heidenhain included. If the machine has no code for the chosen coolant, the post is refused by name (Mist and Through tool; Flood on a machine without a flood code still posts silently - see the follow-up issue). For example, Through tool on the default VMC is refused, and the mill-turn's Through-spindle posts M88.
- Switching is unchanged: coolant comes on per op, and M9 goes out before each tool change and at program end. An Off op writes neither code.
- The edit goes through `EditOperationParams::with_coolant` as one undo step. The op stays generated, since coolant doesn't change the toolpath.
- UI: a Coolant dropdown sits under Tool on the operation page.
- Project files write `"coolant"` only when it isn't Flood; old files load as Flood.
- Docs: RECOMMENDED.md, assets/posts/AGENTS.md, docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md.
- About 30 test files that build an op by hand gain `coolant: Default::default()`.

## Readings / pins

- New app `coolant` suite (7): Flood→Mist across the five mill posts gives M8, M9, the tool change, M7, M9. Off writes no codes. Through tool is refused on the default VMC, and a machine with Through-spindle posts M88. Also the project round trip, an old file loading as Flood, and undo/redo.
- Green: conformance 5 (every golden byte-exact), posting 17, project_roundtrip 68, commands_undo 30, fanuc_post 8, lathe_post 5, lathe_post_refusals 5, machine 32, operations 117, post_engine 31, ui lib 237. Clippy on app, post and ui is clean.

title: feat(ui): track unsaved changes and ask before closing over them
body:
## What changed

Unsaved-changes tracking and a save prompt.

- `History::mark_clean()` / `History::is_dirty()` (`crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`) record the history position at the last save or load. Undo back to that point is clean, and a redo past it is dirty again. A new command after undoing past the save point leaves the document dirty for good. New and Open start clean, and selection, camera, hover and layout never dirty the document.
- The window title gets a leading `*` while dirty.
- The window X now queues a Quit, the same as Ctrl+Q. Quit, New or Open over unsaved changes is held behind a Save / Don't Save / Cancel modal (`crates/ui/src/unsaved.rs`, `egui_app/unsaved_prompt.rs`). Escape or an outside click counts as Cancel. Save on an untitled document asks for a path first, and a failed or cancelled save keeps the app open with the reason on the status line. If the GPU failed at startup, the X still closes at once.
- The shell runs on winit, not eframe, so it simply stops exiting on `CloseRequested`. The scripted file commands (`OpenProjectFile` / `SaveProjectFile`) skip the prompt, so headless runs never hang.
- Changed tests: `file_ops_round_trip_through_commands` now expects the `*` in the title; two New-document tests now answer Don't Save.

## Readings / pins

- app `dirty_flag`: `dirty_tracks_the_saved_point_through_undo_and_redo`, `a_new_branch_makes_the_saved_point_unreachable`
- ui `egui_app::tests::unsaved`: `close_over_unsaved_changes_prompts_and_does_not_exit`, `save_from_the_prompt_saves_then_quits_and_a_failed_save_stays_open`, `new_over_unsaved_changes_asks_and_a_clean_document_never_does`, `undo_back_to_the_saved_point_clears_the_mark`

## What changed

`crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs`: the sideways rapid law and #96's vertical dive law now check the tool's whole footprint, not just its centre column. The footprint is a disc of radius r − gouge_tol, sampled at the centre, 8 points at half radius and 16 on the rim. That's the same sampling `rapids_radial.rs` and `hidden_along` already use. A sample is convicted when it lies inside the stock and below what earlier cuts left (`surface_before`). title: fix(app): judge turned axial rapids in the meridian plane against the revolved stock
body:
## What changed

Replaces #96's turning-rapid exemption with a rapid check in the lathe's own cross-section (the meridian plane).

- `operation/turning_rapids.rs`: for a turning op, every axial rapid (no XY travel) is judged in the meridian plane against the fitted spindle axis. Turning/Bore inserts sweep their nose disc (nose radius − GOUGE_TOL); groove, thread and form tools are judged at their tip, because a form tool's `nose_radius` is its crown. Material = part + setup stock revolved about the axis, minus this op's own earlier feeds (signed radius, so a facing pass across the axis counts), minus the stock faced off ahead (#89's prior read, revolved), minus any axial Drill ahead (a cylinder plus a cone point). A hit is `RapidInStock` and blocks the post. If the axis fit fails, the column law's verdict stands.
- `operation/turning_outline.rs` (new): reads material per station as an annulus [r_in, r_out]. r_out comes from the turned outline; r_in comes from rays cast out from the axis. So a bored part or tube stock reads its hole as air, and a solid Cylinder stays solid to the axis.
- `job.rs` collects the prior for turning ops too. The costly read only runs once a rapid is already convicted.
- Fixtures: the lathe suites declared a 40 mm box stock around a 12 mm bar, and their approaches really were inside it. They now use a bar-sized Cylinder. No NC golden changed. `turning_bore` runs an axial pilot drill (`AX0`, which sorts ahead in name order, with a 70 mm-flute `DR-0400-L`) ahead of the bore.

## Readings / pins

- `turning_axial_rapids::an_axial_approach_inside_a_wider_bar_is_named_and_blocks_the_post`: fails on origin/main (`the approach into the bar went unnamed: []`) and passes here.
- `turning_axial_rapids::the_same_approach_beside_a_bar_the_parts_size_is_clean`
- `turning_bore::a_boring_approach_into_a_solid_bar_with_no_pilot_is_convicted_and_blocks_the_post`
- Unit tests: meridian convictions, the annulus reading and the pilot cone.
- Suites green (debug): lib, turning_bore 8, turning_axial_rapids 2, turning_contour 10, lathe_post 5 (goldens unchanged), drill_prior 10, drill_prior_kinds 4, turning / profile / blade / form / thread, lathe_field_sim, vertical_rapid_stock, posting, golden_cl. Clippy -p camcraft-app is clean.

## Follow-ups

- #130: turning kernels approach from the part, not the stock.
- #109: a turning op's stamp doesn't digest the drill/facing ops ahead.
- #127: rest.rs is over 400 lines.

Changelog: A turned path's axial rapids are judged in the meridian plane against the revolved stock (the bore as air, a pilot drill ahead credited); one into the bar blocks the post

body:
**Stacked on #120** (issue #85; itself stacked on #118, issue #80). Before #120 merges, retarget this PR to `main`; merge order #118 -> #120 -> this.

Drilling reads the stock the setup's earlier operations left (issue #89).

**What changed**
- New `crates/app/src/operation/drill_prior.rs`: a `PriorCell` simulates #96's `rest::PriorPlan` lazily, once per job - the Drill arm builds it only when `axial_reach` against raw stock refuses; verify's #96 acquittal shares the same cell.

title: fix(app): cross holes on box stock enter at the face, not the corner radius
body:
**Stacked on #118** (issue #80) - both change the cross-drill path. Before #118 merges, retarget this PR to `main` (`gh pr edit <this> --base main`), then merge #118, then this.

Cross holes on box stock enter at the face, not the corner radius (issue #85).

**What changed**
- New `crates/app/src/operation/cross_entry.rs`: per cross hole, the entry where the drill first touches stock - stock facets clipped to a square tube of half-width d/2 around the hole's own line (spindle frame), outermost point; the tube contains the round drill, so the entry is never nearer the axis than the real first contact (#77's edge rule kept). The shank's extra reach (#84) is read the same way at its half-width.
- Round bars stay bit-identical: the mesh reading replaces the corner circle only when the crossing sits more than `raw·(1−cos(π/16))` (~1.9% of the radius) inside it - chords of a 16+-sided polygon never trigger it. No facet in the tube -> corner circle (documented).
- `rapids_clear`: a rapid along a hole's own line is proved against that per-line entry (drill at the tip, a wider shank one flute behind); every other rapid (station hops, swings, start/end) still stands off the corner radius + rim.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 60x60 box, on-axis hole | mouth r42.43 | r30 |
| 44 square bar, hole to x -8 | read 39.11 mm deep, 35 mm flute refused | 30 mm, posts |
| 60 box, 30 mm flute | refused at 35.43 mm | drills |
| 60 box, off-centre 6 mm drill | refused at 38.10 mm | mouth at the x=30 face |

**Pinned by** `drilling_cross_box::{a_30_deep_hole_from_the_face_of_a_44_square_bar_posts_on_a_35_flute, a_60_box_mouth_sits_at_the_face_not_the_corner_radius, an_off_centre_hole_on_a_box_face_enters_at_the_face, the_station_change_hop_still_clears_the_box_corners, a_cylinder_stock_chain_is_unchanged_bit_for_bit}` (all failed before) + a unit test; `drilling_cross_stock`'s box test now asserts per-line entries.

title: fix(motion,app): the lathe axis fit sets off-centre features aside
body:
Lathe axis fit sets off-centre features aside (issue #71).

**What changed**
- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_robust.rs` (trimmed least squares / RANSAC consensus refit, Pottmann & Randrup): after the plain fit, keep the facets whose normal lines pass within the fit's tolerance (`REL_TOL·rho`, 3% of the mean radius) of the candidate axis (and facets along the axis), refit the line and the #62 refinement on them, up to 4 rounds until the kept set settles. Each refit must still pass the existing full judgement (90% concurrency share, coarseness) - it can only move an axis the part already earns. A plain revolve returns the plain fit bit for bit. Guard: kept < 50% of area or < 8 facets -> plain fit, untrusted.
- `axis::fit` unchanged in signature; new `axis::fit_report` returns robust and plain axes, set-aside share, trust flag.
- `spindle_law.rs`: a trusted reading keeps the misplaced-part message with "(read on the revolved surface; X% of the part's surface - keyways, flats, holes - set aside)"; an untrusted one says off-centre features bias the fit and moving the work offset cannot fix it.

**Measured** (72-segment D20 shaft, keyway Z0..Z10, floor x = 8): 5.18 mm keyway 0.153 -> 0.000 mm off, 0.9% set aside; 10 mm keyway 0.058 -> 0.000 mm, 0.35%.

**Pinned by** `lathe_spindle_keyed::{a_keyed_shaft_on_g54_passes_the_spindle_law_and_generates, a_keyed_shaft_off_g54_is_refused_as_misplaced_naming_the_set_aside_share}` (both failed on main) + `axis_robust` unit tests (plain revolve bit for bit; keyway no longer drags the axis, direction kept).

**Gates**: quick gate green; app lathe/turning/rotary suites, golden_cl, motion lib + rotary/multiaxis/turning suites green; clippy clean; no golden changed.

**Limit**: a large keyway (> ~10% of the surface) is still refused as not revolved before the robust pass runs - #110.

Changelog: fix(motion,app): the lathe axis fit sets keyways, flats and cross holes aside, so a correctly placed keyed shaft passes the spindle law; the refusal names the set-aside share and gives move-the-offset advice only for a misplaced part

Fixes #71

body:
P0 (#96): verify's rapid law skipped every vertical rapid as "a retract through the tool's own kerf" - including rapids going DOWN into uncut stock - so any op's vertical rapid into declared stock posted silently.

**What changed**
- `crates/sim/src/verify/rapids.rs`: a downward vertical rapid that ends below the stock surface left by earlier cuts, inside the stock, is `RapidInStock`; peck re-entries down their own earlier plunge and retracts up stay clean.
- `crates/app/src/operation/turning_rapids.rs` (one call in `generate.rs`): drops `RapidInStock` only for turning ops' rapids along the spindle axis (no XY travel) - on a lathe world Z is the spindle, and a column reading cannot see what the part or earlier passes removed beside the bar (false conviction). Those rapids were never checked before this PR either; checking them properly in the meridian plane is #103. Every non-turning op, and turning sideways rapids, keep every conviction.

**Triage of every newly failing test** (all 193 debug binaries of app/ui/motion/sim run)

| Test(s) | Op | Rapid | Stock top | Verdict | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| posting: 6 on `contour_and_drill` | Contour, top 5, clearance 10, retract 8 | move 1, Z10 -> Z7 beside the 5 mm box | 10 | real collision | stock 10 -> 5 mm (and the Deep1 shank fixture) |
| control_comp: 3 | same contour | move 1 | 10 | real collision | stock 10 -> 5 mm |
| operations: `the_shell_switch_sends_the_pocket_to_the_offset_engine` | Pocket3D, top 5 | move 1 | 20 | real collision | stock 20 -> 5 mm |
| motion pocket3d_hsm: 2 | Pocket3D, top -5 | move 1 | 0 (test's verify setup) | real by the fixture | verify stock top 0 -> -5 |
| turning_bore: 3 | Boring | move 0, along the axis | 110 mm box | false conviction | `turning_rapids` |
| turning_contour: 5 | Taper / Chamfer / Multi-pass | move 0, along the axis | box over the bar | false conviction | `turning_rapids` |
| lathe_post: `profile_rough_and_finish_post_to_the_lathe_golden` | Profile rough+finish | move 0 | 40 mm box | false conviction | `turning_rapids` |

Goldens unchanged (`contour_control_comp.nc`, `fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` byte for byte).

**Pinned by** `vertical_rapids` (sim, 4) and `vertical_rapid_stock` (app, 2: a contour under a 10 mm block is named at generation and refused at the post; posts clean over stock to its top).

Not re-run on the final build: lathe_field_sim, center_cut_multiaxis (slow lane), motion and sim binaries (green earlier with the same law; the app change only removes turning warnings).

title: fix(app): drilling refuses holes beyond the flute's reach and proves the holder clear (P0)
body:
P0 (#84): no drilling op checked the tool's reach - with a short flute the shank or holder fed into uncut stock unflagged; #77's raw-stock mouths made it far more likely (~16 mm deep vs ~6 mm).

**What changed** (new `crates/app/src/operation/drill_reach.rs`; one call each in `cross_spindle.rs` and `generate.rs`)
- **Reach**: every drilling cycle (axial and cross) refuses by name a hole deeper from the stock surface than the tool's `flute_len` - e.g. "cross hole 0 at (10.000, 0.000, 0.000) is 16.000 mm deep from the stock surface; tool DR-0400's flute reaches 12.000 mm ...". Cross holes: depth from the raw-surface mouths (#77) plus the through-hole exit allowance (spot cycles: the dimple depth). Axial holes: from the highest material over the drill's (or a wider shank's) footprint - the part, plus the setup stock capped at the R plane - down to the cycle bottom, read from the kernel's own cycle records. No exception for necked tools.
- **Holder** (`holder_d` x `holder_len`, `flute_len + shank_len` behind the tip; none when `holder_d`/`holder_len` is 0): on axial holes its face must stay above the material over its footprint; on the cross drill, on every rapid and feed, its lower edge rides above the stock's Z top or its swept footprint stays outside the stock radius. The opposite-station end-face swing is refused, not raised (raising Clearance drills it).

**Fixtures that now refuse - all real reach collisions**: `cross_support` (a 31 mm through hole, 47 mm from the raw box, on a 12 mm flute -> 50 mm flute), `drilling_cross_stock` (16-24 mm from the raw bar -> 30 mm flute), `blind_floor` / `solid_law` drill gouge tests (14-15 mm -> 30 mm), `operations::moving_the_part_marks_the_drill_op_stale_until_regen` (13 mm -> 20 mm). `operations::a_hole_deeper_than_the_drill_reaches_warns_and_still_generates` pinned the old design (generate + warn + post blocks) and is now `..._is_refused_by_name`; `posting::a_warned_path_blocks_even_though_it_generated` now uses a contour whose shank rubs the wall. The verifier's own reach warning stays as a backstop.

**Pinned by** `drill_reach::{a_short_flute_cross_drill_on_raw_stock_wider_than_the_part_is_refused_by_name, a_holder_that_would_sweep_the_end_face_on_the_swing_is_refused_by_name, an_axial_hole_deeper_than_the_flute_from_the_stock_top_is_refused_by_name, the_same_cross_hole_drills_with_a_flute_long_enough}` (first three failed on main) + 2 unit tests.

**Gates**: quick gate green (app 437 s, ui 42 s); the agent ran 20+ app binaries one by one, the app lib tests and 3 UI drilling tests; goldens unchanged; clippy -D warnings clean.

**Known cost**: with stock declared, a hole on a pocket floor may be falsely refused (drilling doesn't know what earlier ops removed) - fails safe; #89.
