title: docs(agents): retarget a stacked PR to main before merging its parent
body:
The Issue Law's stacking rule said the parent merges first, then the child is retargeted. title: fix(app): cross drill stands off the raw stock, not just the part (P0)
body:
Replaces #82 (closed automatically when its stacked base, #78, merged and the base branch was deleted). Same branch and commits; #78 is on main.

P0 (#77): on a mill-turn the cross drill posted silently with its rapids 5 mm inside uncut raw stock.

**Before** (r10 bar in r20 cylinder stock, holes at +X, +Y, -X): standoff measured from the part only - start and approach at r15, station-change rapid `G00 X21.213 Y0 Z10 -> G00 X0 Y21.213 Z0` passing r15 from the spindle. Mill-turn: the verification gate returned no warnings (the rapid-in-stock check is off for radial drilling - filed as #79) and the post went through. Lathe: blocked only by an unrelated false refusal (#80).

**What changed**
- New `crates/app/src/operation/cross_stock.rs`: measures the part and the setup's stock about the same spindle line `cross_spindle.rs` uses and stands off the larger (box stock at its circumscribed radius, cylinder at its radius). Hole mouths move out along their axis to the raw surface, bottoms unchanged (the drill feeds through the skin; Auto switches to full-retract pecking at r20). The stock's Z top sets the over-the-end-face route between opposite stations.
- Every rapid is proved against stock radius + drill half-width (or above the stock top) and the job is refused by name if one fails; retracts back up a just-drilled hole are allowed.
- Stock == part or no stock: falls back to the part, bit-identical output.
- A cross drill's stamp includes the setup stock: resizing the stock after generating stales the op (before, the old hops would post).
- `drilling_cross_spindle.rs` fixture now takes its stock from the bar (it tests the spindle frame alone; a world-centred box read as raw stock broke the #67 comparison).

**After**: start, approach and station-change rapids all at r25 (stock r20 + 5 mm); the mill-turn program posts clear.

**Pinned by** `drilling_cross_stock::{a_cross_drill_on_raw_stock_wider_than_the_part_hops_outside_the_stock, a_cross_drill_with_the_stock_equal_to_the_part_drills_the_part_only_chain, a_station_change_whose_chord_would_clip_the_bar_is_refused_by_name, re_sizing_the_raw_stock_stales_the_cross_drill_and_the_post_refuses_it}`.

**Gates**: quick gate green vs the #67 branch (app 335 s, ui 333 s); the agent ran drilling_cross 9, drilling_cross_spindle 3, drilling_cross_stock 4, drilling_axial 7, lathe_spindle_law 8, lathe_post 5, lathe_post_refusals 5, posting 17, conformance 5, golden_cl 23, verify 21, operations 117, clippy -D warnings - green; drilling_cross and goldens not edited.

**Follow-ups**: #79 (post-gate rapid check blind for radial programs), #80 (lathe cross drills falsely refused by the axial check), #81 (quarter-turn hop assumes on-centre holes).

title: fix(sim): the post gate checks radial (cross-drill) rapids against the raw stock
body:
The post gate's rapid-in-stock law now judges radial (cross-drill) programs (#79, found by #77).

**Why it was off**: M5.2 F2 switched the check off for `Mode::Radial` - the mill check reads stock as columns from above, so a retract sliding out of its own sideways hole looked like a rapid through solid stock; the gate then trusted the cross-drill planner's own promise and was blind (a station-change rapid 5 mm inside uncut stock posted with no warning).

**What changed**
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/rapids_radial.rs` (188 lines); `rapids.rs` routes `Mode::Radial` there instead of skipping it.
- The tool is the drill's cutting length as discs of radius `r - gouge_tol` square to the tool, at the tip and every 1 mm back along the flutes, sampled at most 0.5 mm apart along each rapid with the controller's interpolated orientation (`midpose::intervals`).
- Stock = the stock outline (or the region) under the stock top, unbounded below - the mill check's stock.
- Rapids may pass through material earlier cuts removed (a tool-radius cylinder around each earlier cut, extended along the tool by the cutting length for straight plunges): retracts up a just-drilled hole and peck chip-breaks are clean; a rapid down a hole not yet drilled, or through uncut stock, blocks as `RapidInStock { at }`.

**A real collision caught at once**: `drilling_cross`'s 44 mm box-stock fixture - the approach (move 0) stops inside the box, the slide between holes (move 6) passes through it. That is the #77 bug (PR #82). `a_cross_drill_op_runs_clean_in_the_document` moved onto a bar-sized `bar_stock_world` so it still tests what it was written for; new `a_rapid_inside_the_raw_box_stock_never_posts_silently` asserts every rapid its own geometry finds inside the box is named and blocks the post (vacuous once #82 lands - it won't break then).

**Pinned by** `radial_rapids::{a_station_change_hopped_outside_the_stock_is_clean, a_station_change_chord_through_the_stock_blocks_by_name, the_column_reading_still_stands_for_a_mill_mode_twin, an_approach_that_stops_inside_the_stock_blocks, a_rapid_down_a_hole_not_yet_drilled_blocks, peck_chip_breaks_and_the_full_retract_ride_the_kerf, a_lateral_slide_out_of_the_hole_blocks, the_over_the_end_face_detour_is_clean_and_a_low_one_blocks}` + `drilling_cross::a_rapid_inside_the_raw_box_stock_never_posts_silently`.

**Gates**: quick gate green; the agent ran camcraft-sim, verify 21, drilling_cross 10, drilling_axial 7, posting 17, rotary_verify 9, rotary_fixtures 4, turning 5, lathe_post 5, conformance 5, clippy -D warnings - green.

**Not covered** (as in the mill check): shank/holder vs stock along a rapid; the stock is unbounded below.

Changelog: fix(sim): the post gate's rapid-in-stock law now judges radial (cross-drill) programs against the raw stock - a rapid through uncut stock is named RapidInStock and blocks the post; retracts up a drilled hole stay clean

Fixes #79

title: fix(app): lathe cross-drill measures about the work offset's spindle
body:
Lathe cross-drill measures about the work offset's spindle (#67).

**What was wrong**: cross_drill measured every standoff about world Z through world (0,0) - bar radius, station side, hop and clearance radii, the inter-station clearance rule - while the post programs about world Z through the work-offset origin. On an r10 bar at (10,4) under a moved G54 (radii read from G54):

| Rapid point | Before | After (= bar on the origin) |
|---|---|---|
| Start | 15.770 | 15.000 |
| Hop between stations | 26.444 / 32.444 / 46.444 | 21.213 |
| Final clearance | 35.770 | 15.000 |

Also: on a mill-turn the #62 spindle law didn't cover cross drilling (a bar 10.770 mm off an unmoved G54 drilled silently); on a plain lathe a part the axis fit can't read as turned drilled anyway.

**What changed**
- New `crates/app/src/operation/cross_spindle.rs`: shifts holes into the spindle frame by the `wcs_context` origin, measures `stock_r` about that line, runs the drilling kernel unchanged, shifts back; on-origin parts skip the shift (bit-identical). `lathe_reads` refuses by name a part the fit can't read as turned on a plain lathe.
- `job.rs`: the work-offset origin is read once in `collect_job` (`GenJob::wcs_origin`); the spindle law checks against the same origin.
- `spindle_law::turns` also covers a mill-turn Drill with cross holes - refused by name at generation and posting; moving G54 stales the op.
- A mill-turn still drills square/hex bars (normal cross-drill stock), clearance now about the posted spindle (RECOMMENDED.md #67).

**Pinned by** `drilling_cross_spindle::{a_cross_drill_off_the_world_origin_under_a_moved_g54_drills_the_on_origin_chain, a_cross_drill_on_a_bar_off_an_unmoved_work_offset_is_refused_by_name, a_lathe_cross_drill_on_a_part_that_reads_as_no_revolve_is_refused_by_name}` (all fail on main). Goldens unchanged.

**Gates**: quick gate green (app 334 s, ui 337 s); the agent ran drilling_axial, drilling_cross, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_spindle_fit, lathe_post(_refusals), lathe_field_sim, posting, conformance, golden_cl, all turning suites, clippy -D warnings - green.

**Follow-up**: #77 (standoff from the finished part, not the raw stock).

Changelog: fix(app): cross drill measures its clearance and standoffs about the work offset's spindle, refuses a mill-turn bar off its work offset, and refuses on a lathe a part that can't be read as turned

Fixes #67

title: fix(ui): GPU startup tries adapters one by one and logs slow frames by phase
body:
GPU adapter selection on hybrid laptops, and a frame-stall log (#74, user-reported: Intel UHD + Quadro P3200 never renders / lags 1-2 s on an empty orbit).

**What changed** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/`)
- `gpu_init.rs` (new, out of `shell.rs`): within each backend group of the existing chain, enumerate every adapter and log one `gpu: seen ...` line each (name, vendor, device id, type, backend, surface-compatible). Try adapters one by one: device, surface config, configure - checked for errors, not assumed. A failure logs `gpu: "<name>" via <backend> failed: <reason> - trying the next adapter`; failed adapters aren't retried. If none works, the refusal lists every adapter tried and why, on stderr and in a native error dialog.
- `gpu_select.rs` (+ tests, new): ordering and surface config as pure functions. Order: `--gpu <name>` / `CAMCRAFT_GPU` -> the HighPerformance pick -> every other surface-compatible adapter, discrete > integrated > virtual > other > software; ties to the native API (DX12 on Windows, Metal on macOS, Vulkan elsewhere); incompatible adapters skipped by name.
- Surface config from the surface's reported capabilities (preferred format, Fifo unless missing, Opaque alpha if offered) instead of `get_default_config` + hard-coded AutoVsync.
- `--gpu <part of name>` (beats `CAMCRAFT_GPU`), following `--gpu-backend`; no preferences page yet (no per-machine settings store) - recorded in RECOMMENDED.md.
- `frame_watch.rs` (new): a frame over 100 ms logs one line with time per phase (commands+scene, ui, acquire, encode, submit+present), at most one line per 5 s.

**Stall**: not reproduced headlessly - nothing on the idle frame path blocks (GPU readbacks are tests/diagnostics only). Leading suspect: Vulkan cross-adapter copy on Optimus; DX12-first should avoid it. Issue stays open for the reporter's log.

**Tests**: `gpu_select::tests` (9: discrete_before_integrated_before_cpu, user_choice_wins_case_insensitively, unmatched_choice_is_said_and_auto_order_stands, high_performance_pick_leads_on_its_best_backend, unpresentable_adapters_are_skipped_by_name, nothing_to_order_is_empty_not_a_panic, log_line_names_every_field, config_comes_from_reported_capabilities, incompatible_surface_refuses_by_name), `frame_watch::tests` (3), `gpu::tests::adapter_choice_flag_then_env`. camcraft-ui lib 230 passed; gpu_render 9; shell 19; clippy -D warnings clean; quick gate green.

Changelog: fix(ui): GPU startup tries adapters one by one (named choice, high-performance, discrete before integrated, native backend first), configures the surface from its reported capabilities, adds --gpu/CAMCRAFT_GPU, refuses by name listing every adapter tried, and logs frames over 100 ms by phase

Refs #74

title: fix(ui): prevent GPU render test suite crash
body:
## Bug

The `camcraft-ui` GPU integration test process exited with SIGSEGV after several tests passed. Each test creates and drops its own fallback wgpu device, and Rust runs the tests concurrently. Overlapping device lifecycles appear to trigger a software Vulkan driver crash.

## Fix

Serialize device creation, rendering, readback, and teardown within `gpu_render.rs` using a test-only mutex. Other test binaries and application rendering are unchanged.

## Verification

- Before the fix: `cargo test --locked -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui` reached `gpu_render.rs`, then exited with SIGSEGV after five GPU tests passed.
- After the fix: all nine `gpu_render` tests passed, followed by the full `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui` test run on Fedora 44.

Changelog: Prevent concurrent GPU test devices from crashing the render test suite.

title: fix(app,post): refuse a turning op whose fitted axis is not the lathe spindle
body:
P0: the lathe post accepted a turning op whose fitted spindle leans in Y and cut a taper error (#62).

**What changed**
- New `crates/app/src/operation/spindle_law.rs`, called from `collect_job` (validate early): every turning op, and Drill on a plain lathe, is refused by name when its fitted axis is not world Z through the work-offset origin. The origin comes from `posting::wcs_context`, the same function that gives the post its origin, so generation and post read one spindle.
- Tolerance: the axis may stand at most 0.0005 mm (radius) from the work-offset Z line at both the part's lowest and highest Z - half the posted diameter's last digit, so a passing part posts the same digits as a perfectly placed one. (An angle limit of 0.01 deg was dropped: over 100 mm it allows ~17 um of radius drift.)
- The message names the lean in degrees, the offset in mm at mid-height and the work-offset slot, and says to align the part's axis with world Z and move the work offset onto it.
- Parts the fit cannot read as revolved, or whose axis lies within 1 deg of the table, pass to the turning code's existing refusals unchanged.
- No post-side check: the post only sees points, and a part leaning in Y looks like a plumb one move by move; catching it there would need a new parameter in every lathe stream (every golden changes). The post's existing both-X-and-Y refusal stays.
- Valid programs post byte-identically; lathe goldens unchanged.

**Pinned by** `lathe_spindle_law::{a_bar_leaning_in_y_on_the_origin_is_refused_by_name_at_generation (written first - it posted a taper: X-1.708 diameters with drifting Z), a_plumb_bar_off_the_work_origin_is_refused_by_name_at_generation, an_axial_drill_on_a_bar_off_the_work_origin_is_refused_by_name, a_plumb_bar_on_the_origin_or_under_a_moved_work_offset_posts_the_same_program}`.

**Gates**: quick gate green against origin/main (app + ui suites, 11.7 min); camcraft-ui lib 198 passed; the agent ran 19 app binaries one by one (turning*, lathe_post*, posting, conformance, drilling_axial, ...) and clippy -D warnings - all green.

PR #60 (#19, lathe field sim) depends on this guarantee: it revolves about the fitted axis, which this makes the machine spindle. Merge this first.

Changelog: fix(app): turning ops (and the lathe axial drill) whose fitted axis is not world Z through the work offset within 0.0005 mm are refused by name at generation instead of posting a taper or eccentric

Fixes #62

body:

title: docs(agents): branch per issue, PR to finish, cut by PR review -> merge -> tag
body:
Procedure rework requested by the user: issues start from the latest main on their own branch, finish as a pushed branch with a PR (not a merge to main), and a release cut goes PR review -> merge to main -> tag.

- AGENTS.md Issue Law: start/branch, done = push + PR, `in-review` label, changelog rows at the cut.
- AGENTS.md Commits and Releases: the four-step cut (review + merge issue PRs, release branch + gate, release PR, tag main).
- scripts/release.ps1: `-NoTag` (parse-checked).
- RECOMMENDED.md: the seven decisions taken filling in the mechanics.

Changelog: none (docs/process only)
